The coat didn't get worse. You just aren't that size anymore.

items.sourceNote: Original take on 'every heartbreak cracks open a doorway to new beginnings' theme from 2026 breakup healing collections; rewritten with a 房間騰空 / empty-room metaphor

zh-tw.content:
他走了之後，心裡那塊地方是空的。
但空的不是壞事，
那是你終於有位置，放新的東西進來。
以前塞太滿，連自己都擠不進去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個覺得「沒有他，我什麼都不剩」的朋友。空，不是失去，是空間。等你慢慢把自己擺進來，會發現那個位置原本就該是你的。
variations: 他離開騰出來的不是傷口，是一個你可以重新佈置的空間。
心裡空一塊不可怕，可怕的是繼續被不該留的人佔著。

en.content:
After they left, there's an empty spot inside.
But empty isn't bad —
it means you finally have room to put new things in.
Before, it was packed so full even you couldn't fit.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who feels 'without them I have nothing left.' Empty isn't loss — it's space. As you slowly place yourself back in, you'll realize that spot was supposed to be yours all along.
variations: What they left behind isn't a wound. It's a room you get to redecorate.
An empty spot inside isn't scary. What's scary is letting the wrong person keep occupying it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing quietly without explaining' theme from 2026 IG breakup caption collections; rewritten with a 不發限動 / 安靜長大 angle

zh-tw.content:
我沒有發任何限動，沒有貼任何傷感歌詞，
那不是我裝沒事，是我終於懂——
有些痛不用昭告天下，安靜的長大比較快。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛分手卻不想被全 IG 知道的朋友。不發文不代表沒事，是她選擇用自己的方式消化。陪她安靜就好，不用追問。
variations: 成熟的痛不是不喊，是知道喊出來也沒人能替你扛。
最深的療傷都是無聲的，畢竟你的人生不需要直播。

en.content:
I didn't post a story. I didn't drop a sad lyric.
That's not me pretending I'm fine — it's me finally getting it.
Some pain doesn't need an audience. You grow up faster in silence.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just broke up but doesn't want all of IG to know. No posts doesn't mean she's okay — she's processing her way. Just sit with her quietly. Don't probe.
variations: Grown-up pain doesn't scream. It just knows screaming won't make anyone else carry it.
The deepest healing is silent. Your life was never meant to be a livestream.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'glow up after breakup' 2026 caption trend; rewritten with a 通勤照鏡子 / commute-reflection moment Taiwan-friendly angle

zh-tw.content:
今天通勤的時候，我在捷運車窗看到自己。
沒有特別打扮，但眼神不一樣了——
原來那種「我不需要被誰選」的氣場，是分手送我的禮物。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最強的 glow up 不是變漂亮，是眼神變了。傳給那個剛開始覺得「一個人也可以」的朋友，那不是錯覺，那是真的長出來的東西。
variations: 他離開以後，我才知道原來自信是這種長相。
最好看的妝容是「我不缺你」這四個字寫在臉上。

en.content:
On the train this morning, I caught my reflection in the window.
Nothing fancy on, but the look in my eyes was different —
turns out 'I don't need to be picked' is the energy this breakup gave me.
en.editorNote: The strongest post-breakup glow-up isn't looking prettier — it's the change in your eyes. For the friend just starting to feel 'I'm okay alone.' That's not in her head — it's real, and it just grew in.
variations: After they left, I finally saw what confidence looks like on me.
The best makeup is 'I'm not missing you' written across your face.

items.sourceNote: Original take on 'from us to me, this solo chapter looks really good' theme; rewritten with a 雙人床 / 整張都是我的 daily-life Taiwan metaphor

zh-tw.content:
雙人床第一次整張都是我的，
睡哪一邊都可以，棉被也不用分。
原來「孤單」跟「自由」之間的差別，
只差在你怎麼想而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀第一個月最大的轉變：你發現一個人睡其實滿爽的。傳給那個剛把另一個枕頭收起來的朋友——這不是孤單，是空間還給你了。
variations: 棉被不用搶之後，我才知道自己睡眠品質有多好。
一個人的床不是冷，是終於可以攤開來睡。

en.content:
First time the whole bed is mine.
Any side I want, the whole blanket too.
Turns out the difference between 'lonely' and 'free' —
is just how you decide to frame it.
en.editorNote: Biggest shift in the first month post-breakup: you realize sleeping alone is actually kind of great. For the friend who just put the second pillow away — that's not loneliness, that's your space coming back to you.
variations: Once I wasn't fighting for the blanket, I learned how well I actually sleep.
A bed for one isn't cold. It's finally room to stretch out.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'exchanged my better half for a better peace' savage 2026 caption format; rewritten with a 換掉吵架對象 / 內心安靜 angle

zh-tw.content:
我沒有失去另一半，我換到了一份安靜。
以前的我每天在解釋、討好、猜他的臉色，
現在的我只需要決定中午吃什麼——
這筆交易我覺得很划算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把分手當成「升級安靜」就一點都不慘了。傳給那種「分手後反而睡得比較好」的朋友，互相確認這是正常的，不是冷血。
variations: 我交換的不是愛情，是少一個人在我腦袋裡吵架。
他不在以後，我才發現原來腦袋這麼安靜這麼好。

en.content:
I didn't lose a partner. I traded up for peace and quiet.
Old me spent every day explaining, pleasing, reading his mood.
New me only has to decide what to eat for lunch —
honestly, great deal.
en.editorNote: Reframing a breakup as 'upgrading to quiet' takes all the sting out. For the friend sleeping better since the split — let her know that's normal, not cold-hearted.
variations: I didn't trade away love. I traded away someone arguing inside my head.
Once he was gone, I realized how nice it is when my brain is finally quiet.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I turned my heartbreak into a reset button' 2026 glow-up caption trend; rewritten with a 手機重開機 / 卡頓 Taiwan-friendly tech metaphor

zh-tw.content:
心碎不是壞掉，是按到了重開機。
以前卡卡的、跑不動的、一直跳通知的，
重啟之後一次清乾淨——
原來我一直背著別人的後台程式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛分手覺得「我整個人都崩了」的朋友。沒有崩，只是把佔記憶體的東西關掉了。重開之後你會發現自己跑得多順。
variations: 他不是把我弄壞，他只是逼我重灌一次自己。
心碎是 Ctrl+Alt+Delete，不是 Game Over。

en.content:
Heartbreak isn't a malfunction — it's a forced restart.
Everything that was lagging, freezing, pinging you nonstop —
all cleared in one boot.
Turns out you'd been running someone else's background apps the whole time.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just split and feels 'I'm completely broken.' She's not broken — she just closed the apps eating her memory. After the reboot, she'll see how smooth she runs.
variations: He didn't break me. He just forced me to reinstall myself.
Heartbreak is Ctrl+Alt+Delete, not Game Over.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放下不是丟掉，是把曾經好好放在記憶裡' classic let-go quote; rewritten with a 抽屜深處 / 不上鎖 storage metaphor

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把他從記憶裡刪掉，
是把那段關係收進抽屜最深的地方。
沒有上鎖，但也不會再打開——
因為現在的我，已經不住在那個房間了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 成熟的釋懷不是恨，也不是忘記，是「我知道它在那裡，但我不需要再回去」。傳給那個怕「不再想他就是背叛回憶」的朋友。
variations: 我沒有忘記他，我只是不再需要記得他。
釋懷是把回憶搬進儲藏室，房間騰出來給自己住。

en.content:
Letting go isn't deleting them from your memory.
It's tucking that relationship into the deepest drawer.
Not locked — but I won't open it again either,
because the me of today doesn't live in that room anymore.
en.editorNote: Mature closure isn't hate or amnesia — it's 'I know it's there, I just don't need to go back.' For the friend afraid that not thinking of him is somehow a betrayal of the memory.
variations: I didn't forget him. I just don't need to remember him anymore.
Moving on is putting the memories in storage and turning the bedroom over to yourself.

items.sourceNote: Original riff on 'sometimes the love story you deserve is the one you write with yourself' empowerment frame; rewritten with a 早午餐 / 自己約自己 daily Taiwan ritual

zh-tw.content:
我今天約自己吃早午餐。
不是因為沒人約，是因為我終於知道——
那個願意每週五點起床準備我喜歡的味道的人，
本來就只有我自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最浪漫的轉變：你開始用對待戀人的方式對待自己。傳給那個正在「重新學會單身怎麼好玩」的朋友。
variations: 等別人來愛我之前，我先把自己當喜歡的人對待。
一個人吃早午餐不是寂寞，是我終於配得上好好吃一頓。

en.content:
I took myself out to brunch today.
Not because no one else asked — because I finally got it:
the person willing to get up early to make exactly what I like
was always supposed to be me.
en.editorNote: The most romantic post-breakup shift: you start treating yourself the way you'd treat a partner. For the friend relearning how to enjoy being single.
variations: Before waiting for someone to love me, I started treating myself like someone I love.
Brunch alone isn't lonely. It's me finally believing I deserve a good meal.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'plot twist: the breakup was the best part' savage caption format; rewritten with a 訂閱制 / 自動續約 modern Taiwan-friendly metaphor

zh-tw.content:
他以為分手是他甩了我，
其實是我不續約。
免費試用期看完了，內容沒有比較好，
當然不會升級成年費會員。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把感情當訂閱制看，主導權就回到自己手上了。傳給那個被分手後一直自我懷疑「是不是我不夠好」的朋友——是你不續，不是你被退。
variations: 他不是甩了我，他只是被我從自動續約名單裡刪掉。
試用期結束之後，沒有按續訂的人才是清醒的那個。

en.content:
He thinks the breakup means he dumped me.
No — I just didn't renew.
The free trial ran out, the content wasn't worth it,
so obviously I didn't upgrade to the annual plan.
en.editorNote: Reframing love as a subscription puts the power back in your hands. For the friend stuck on 'maybe I wasn't good enough' — you didn't get cancelled, you cancelled.
variations: He didn't dump me. I just took him off auto-renew.
When the trial ends, the one who doesn't click renew is the one thinking clearly.

items.sourceNote: Original riff on the 'I exited the group chat' savage caption frame; rewritten with a 群組 / 退出 / 通知靜音 messaging-app metaphor for Taiwan readers

zh-tw.content:
我不是被分手，我只是默默退出了那個群組。
沒有公告、沒有解釋，就像那些已讀我訊息三天的人一樣。
退出之後才發現——原來那個群，只有我一個人在認真聊天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把分手當成「退出群組」就沒那麼悲情了。傳給那個一直覺得「是不是我太黏」的朋友——不是你太熱情，是對方早就把通知關靜音了。
variations: 我沒有被踢出群，我是自己按退出的，差很多。
終於退出那個只有我在打字的群組，世界安靜得很舒服。

en.content:
I didn't get dumped. I just quietly left the group chat.
No announcement, no explanation — same energy as the people who leave you on read for three days.
After I left, I realized I was the only one actually talking in there anyway.
en.editorNote: Reframing a breakup as 'leaving the group chat' takes the drama out. For the friend who keeps thinking 'was I too clingy?' — you weren't too much, he just had you muted the whole time.
variations: I didn't get removed from the chat. I hit leave myself. Big difference.
Finally left the group where I was the only one typing. The silence is honestly lovely.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放下不是遺忘，是把篇章好好闔上' classic let-go theme; rewritten with a 電影散場 / 留到片尾 cinema metaphor

zh-tw.content:
他先走了，我卻一個人留到片尾燈亮。
後來我懂了——不是每場電影都要等到工作人員名單跑完。
好看的我記得就好，散場了就該起身回家。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給那個分手後還守在原地、捨不得離場的朋友。故事結束了不代表你輸了，只是這場放完了。下一場，記得買自己喜歡的位子。
variations: 燈亮了還不走的人，不是深情，是還沒承認電影已經演完了。
我把這場記在心裡，但我已經走出影廳了。

en.content:
He left early, but I stayed alone until the house lights came up.
Then it hit me — not every movie needs you to sit through the end credits.
I'll remember the good parts. When it's over, you stand up and go home.
en.editorNote: For the friend still sitting in the same spot, refusing to leave after the breakup. The story ending doesn't mean you lost — this screening is just done. Next time, pick a seat you actually like.
variations: Staying after the lights come up isn't devotion. It's just not admitting the movie's over.
I'll keep this one in my memory. But I've already walked out of the theater.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I stopped setting alarms for someone who never woke up for me' empowerment frame; rewritten with a 鬧鐘 / 賴床 morning-routine metaphor

zh-tw.content:
以前我設五個鬧鐘，是怕錯過他的早安。
現在我設一個鬧鐘，是為了去做我自己想做的事。
原來最該被叫醒的人，從來都是我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最安靜的成長，是你發現早上醒來的理由變成自己。傳給那個剛開始為自己起床的朋友——不是為了等誰，是為了你想過的那一天。
variations: 我不再為了等他的訊息醒來，我為了今天的計畫醒來。
鬧鐘響的時候，我第一個想到的是我自己，這就是進步。

en.content:
I used to set five alarms so I wouldn't miss his good morning.
Now I set one — to get up and do the things I actually want.
Turns out the person who most deserved waking up for was always me.
en.editorNote: The quietest growth after a breakup is realizing your reason to wake up is yourself now. For the friend who's just started getting up for her own day — not waiting on anyone, just living the day she wants.
variations: I don't wake up waiting for his text anymore. I wake up for today's plans.
When the alarm goes off, the first person I think of is me. That's progress.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the '對的人會留下，錯的人是過程' Taiwan breakup motif; rewritten with a 草稿夾 / 沒寄出的訊息 unsent-drafts metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我的草稿夾裡還躺著三十七則沒寄出的訊息。
以前我以為那是還沒說完的話，後來才懂——
那不是想對他說的，是想對那個還愛著他的自己說的。
我把草稿全刪了，因為那個我，已經先放下了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個手機裡藏著一堆「沒勇氣傳出去」訊息的朋友。那些話其實不是給對方的，是給過去的自己的。刪掉它們，不是失去，是你終於不需要再說服自己。
variations: 沒寄出的訊息不是遺憾，是我那時還沒準備好放手的證據。
刪掉草稿的那一刻，我才發現我早就把要說的話，活成了答案。

en.content:
There are still thirty-seven unsent messages sitting in my drafts.
I used to think they were things I hadn't finished saying. Then I understood —
they weren't meant for him. They were for the version of me that still loved him.
I deleted them all, because that version of me had already let go.
en.editorNote: For the friend hiding a folder of 'never had the nerve to send' messages on her phone. Those words were never really for the other person — they were for your past self. Deleting them isn't losing anything. It's no longer needing to convince yourself.
variations: The unsent messages weren't regret. They were proof I wasn't ready to let go yet.
The moment I deleted the drafts, I realized I'd already lived out the answer I was trying to write.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'my glow-up is your loss' empowerment frame; rewritten with a 限量款下架 / 缺貨 sold-out retail metaphor

zh-tw.content:
你錯過的不是打折商品，是限量款。
現在我直接下架，缺貨中，不補貨。
你慢慢後悔，我這邊已經換季了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在徹底走出來、開始過好日子時放 IG 限動。重點不是嗆對方，是宣告自己有多搶手。傳給那個剛變美、開始發光的閨蜜最對味。
variations: 我不是被退貨，是被秒殺完直接停產。
你猶豫的時候，我已經是別人搶不到的款了。

en.content:
What you passed up wasn't a clearance item — it was a limited edition.
Now I'm off the shelf, sold out, no restock.
Take your time regretting it. I've already moved on to the next season.
en.editorNote: Perfect for an IG story when you've fully moved on and life is good. The point isn't to roast them — it's to announce how in-demand you are. Best sent to the friend who just glowed up.
variations: I didn't get returned. I sold out and got discontinued.
While you were hesitating, I became the piece nobody else can get.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '謝謝你的離開，讓我學會放下' farewell theme; rewritten with a 退租 / 押金 lease-and-deposit metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我把那段感情當成租來的房子，到期就退租了。
押金沒拿回來沒關係，那叫學費。
下一個地方，我要找的是能住一輩子的，不是月底就想搬的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把失戀當成「換房子」就沒那麼難過。傳給那個還在心疼「投入這麼多卻什麼都沒留下」的朋友——那些不是浪費，是讓你看清下次要找什麼。
variations: 退租不丟臉，硬住在會漏水的地方才委屈了自己。
押金當作學費，至少你學會了下次先看清楚再簽約。

en.content:
I treated that relationship like a rented apartment — when the lease was up, I moved out.
Didn't get the deposit back? Fine, call it tuition.
Next place, I'm looking for somewhere I could live for life, not somewhere I'd want to leave by month's end.
en.editorNote: Treating a breakup like changing apartments takes the sting out. For the friend still aching over 'I put in so much and got nothing back' — it wasn't wasted, it showed you what to look for next time.
variations: There's no shame in moving out. Forcing yourself to stay somewhere that leaks is the real loss.
Count the deposit as tuition. At least you learned to read the lease before signing next time.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'ex means example of what I don't need' wordplay; rewritten with a 錯題本 / 重考 study-mistakes metaphor

zh-tw.content:
前任就是我的錯題本，
標記著「這題下次別再選一樣的答案」。
不是失敗，是訂正——而且這次我終於看懂題目了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把感情失誤當成「訂正錯題」最不傷自尊。傳給那個一直自責「怎麼又選錯人」的朋友——錯題訂正過就不會再錯，重點是你有翻開那本本子。
variations: 他不是我的遺憾，是我的錯題本範例。
同樣的題型再出現，這次我會了。

en.content:
My ex is my mistake notebook,
marked with 'don't pick the same answer here next time.'
It's not a failure — it's a correction. And this time, I finally understood the question.
en.editorNote: Framing a relationship slip-up as 'correcting a wrong answer' keeps your dignity intact. For the friend beating herself up over 'why did I pick wrong again?' — once you correct a mistake, you stop repeating it. The point is you opened the notebook.
variations: He's not my regret. He's the worked example in my mistake notebook.
Same kind of question shows up again? This time I know the answer.

items.sourceNote: Original riff on the 'single and thriving / self-love mode activated' caption trend; rewritten with a 飛航模式 / 重新連線 phone-settings metaphor

zh-tw.content:
分手後我把自己調成飛航模式。
不是要躲，是先斷線，把自己重新連回正確的訊號。
等我再上線的時候，已經不是那個一直等他來電的人了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後給自己一段「不回應任何人」的時間不是逃避，是維修。傳給那個剛分手、需要許可一個人靜一靜的朋友。
variations: 飛航模式不是關機，是讓自己有空連回自己。
斷線一陣子，是為了下次連到對的人。

en.content:
After the breakup, I switched myself to airplane mode.
Not to hide — to disconnect, and reconnect to the right signal.
By the time I came back online, I wasn't the person who kept waiting for his call anymore.
en.editorNote: Giving yourself a stretch of 'not answering to anyone' after a breakup isn't avoidance — it's maintenance. For the friend who just broke up and needs permission to be alone for a while.
variations: Airplane mode isn't powering off. It's making room to reconnect to yourself.
Going offline for a while is how you connect to the right person next time.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '謝謝你來過我的世界，現在換我學會放下' closure theme; rewritten with a 看完一場電影 / 散場 cinema metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我把你想成一場看完的電影。
當下哭得唏哩嘩啦，散場後燈一亮，我還是得走回自己的生活。
謝謝這部片很好看，但片尾跑完了，我不會一直坐在位子上等續集。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把一段感情當成「一部看完的電影」，能哭、能感謝、也能起身離場。傳給那個遲遲不肯離開戲院、還在等對方回來的朋友。
variations: 好看的電影不一定要有續集，散場了就讓它是回憶。
片尾名單跑完還不走的人，最後只會被工作人員請出場。

en.content:
I think of you as a movie I've already watched.
I sobbed through it, but when the lights came up, I still had to walk back to my own life.
Thanks — it was a good film. But the credits have rolled, and I'm not going to sit in my seat waiting for a sequel.
en.editorNote: Treating a relationship like 'a movie you've finished' lets you cry, give thanks, and still stand up to leave. For the friend lingering in the theater, still waiting for them to come back.
variations: A great movie doesn't need a sequel. When it's over, let it be a memory.
Stay in your seat after the credits and eventually the staff will ask you to leave.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'not heartbroken, just free trial expired' caption format; rewritten with 試用期沒過 / 轉正 workplace metaphor for Taiwan audience

zh-tw.content:
我不是被分手，是試用期沒過，沒幫他轉正。
表現不及格還想領年終，門都沒有。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把感情當求職看，分手就變成「人資的理性決定」。適合在分手後第一次跟同事吃飯時自嘲，氣氛瞬間輕鬆。
variations: 他履歷寫得很漂亮，可惜實作能力跟面試時差很多。
感情也有試用期，不適任就不續約，這不是無情，是專業。

en.content:
I didn't get dumped. He just failed his probation, so I declined to make him permanent.
Underperforming and still expecting a year-end bonus? Not a chance.
en.editorNote: Treating love like hiring turns a breakup into 'a rational HR decision.' Great for self-deprecating laughs at your first dinner with coworkers post-split.
variations: His resume looked great. Shame the actual performance didn't match the interview.
Relationships have a probation period too. Not renewing an underperformer isn't cruelty — it's professionalism.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing isn't linear' theme; rewritten with 退潮 / 海岸線 tide metaphor

zh-tw.content:
復原不是一條直線，是潮水。
今天退得乾乾淨淨，明天又漲回來打濕你的腳。
別罵自己退步，海從來就是這樣，最後它還是會退。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀復原最大的挫折是「明明好了，怎麼又難過」。傳給那個責怪自己「怎麼還沒走出來」的朋友——你沒退步，這就是海的樣子。
variations: 好了又痛，痛了又好，這不是原地踏步，是潮汐。
今天哭了不代表前面白走，浪退過的沙灘還是比昨天乾。

en.content:
Healing isn't a straight line. It's the tide.
Today it pulls all the way out, and tomorrow it rushes back to soak your feet.
Don't scold yourself for sliding back — the sea has always worked this way, and it always goes out again.
en.editorNote: The hardest part of recovery is 'I thought I was fine, why does it hurt again?' For the friend blaming herself for 'not being over it yet' — you didn't regress, this is just what the tide does.
variations: Better, then aching, then better again — that's not standing still, that's the tides.
Crying today doesn't erase the progress. The sand the wave pulled back from is still drier than yesterday's.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'trading my old boo for new shoes / upgrade' caption humor; rewritten with 換季 / 衣櫃斷捨離 wardrobe metaphor

zh-tw.content:
把他從生活裡刪掉，就像換季整理衣櫃。
那件你捨不得丟的，其實早就不合身了，留著只是佔位子。
清空之後，衣櫃跟心裡都多了好多空間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後的斷捨離不只是丟東西，是把不適合的人也一起整理掉。適合傳給那個房間還堆滿前任痕跡、遲遲不肯收的朋友。
variations: 捨不得丟的不一定是好的，常常只是習慣。
衣櫃留位子給新的衣服，心也是。

en.content:
Deleting him from my life felt like a seasonal closet clean-out.
That piece you couldn't bear to toss? It stopped fitting ages ago — it was just taking up space.
Once it's gone, both the closet and my chest have so much more room.
en.editorNote: Post-breakup decluttering isn't just tossing objects — it's sorting out the people who no longer fit. For the friend whose room is still full of ex-traces she won't pack away.
variations: What you can't bear to throw out isn't always good. Usually it's just habit.
A closet leaves space for new clothes. So does a heart.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'some people are part of your history, not your destiny' theme; rewritten with 路過的站 / 終點站 transit metaphor

zh-tw.content:
有些人是你人生的某一站，不是終點站。
你以為要在那裡下車，後來才知道，列車本來就會繼續開。
他是風景，不是目的地。
zh-tw.editorNote: 分手後最難接受的是「他不是命中注定」。傳給那個一直覺得「失去他人生就停了」的朋友——車還在開，你只是少了一個同行的人，不是少了路。
variations: 他是經過的站名，不是你車票上的終點。
下錯站不可怕，可怕的是賴在月台上不肯再上車。

en.content:
Some people are a stop on your journey, not the final destination.
You thought you'd get off there — then you realized the train was always going to keep moving.
They were the scenery, not the place you were headed.
en.editorNote: The hardest thing to accept after a breakup is 'they weren't my destiny.' For the friend who feels life stopped when she lost him — the train's still moving. You lost a fellow passenger, not the road.
variations: They were the name of a station you passed, not the destination on your ticket.
Getting off at the wrong stop isn't the problem. Refusing to board the next train is.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I chased peace, money, and my glow-up' empowerment caption; rewritten with 追蹤清單 / 取消追蹤 social-media metaphor

zh-tw.content:
分手後我沒有去追他，我去追別的東西：
好好睡覺、存錢、還有我自己的發光。
他取消追蹤我沒關係，反正我的更新他已經跟不上了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最有力的姿態不是挽回，是把力氣轉回自己身上。傳給那個剛分手、開始認真過生活的朋友，提醒她重點是往前走，不是回頭追。
variations: 我沒有要他回來，我只是把追他的力氣拿去追更好的生活。
他退追蹤是他的損失，我的版本一直在更新。

en.content:
After the breakup I didn't chase him. I chased other things:
real sleep, savings, and my own glow.
He can unfollow me — he stopped being able to keep up with my updates anyway.
en.editorNote: The most powerful post-breakup move isn't winning them back, it's redirecting that energy into yourself. For the friend who just got serious about her own life — remind her the point is moving forward, not chasing back.
variations: I'm not asking him back. I just took the energy I spent chasing him and chased a better life instead.
Him unfollowing is his loss. My version keeps updating.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'plot twist: I'm now the main character, side quests include self-love and ice cream' caption; rewritten with 支線任務 / 主線 RPG game metaphor

zh-tw.content:
劇情更新：我把那段感情設成「已完成的支線任務」。
獎勵：自由、睡飽、還有一桶冰淇淋。
現在回到主線，主角是我自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把一段過去的感情當成「打完的支線」就不會卡在那裡。傳給那個一直覺得分手是「遊戲結束」的朋友——不是結束，是回到主線。
variations: 他是支線 NPC，不是最終魔王，打完就該往前走。
感情卡關不用一直存檔重來，有些任務做完就該封存。

en.content:
Status update: I marked that relationship as a completed side quest.
Rewards: freedom, full nights of sleep, and a tub of ice cream.
Now back to the main story, where I'm the lead.
en.editorNote: Treating a past relationship as a 'finished side quest' keeps you from getting stuck on it. For the friend who feels a breakup is 'game over' — it's not the end, it's just back to the main quest.
variations: He was a side-quest NPC, not the final boss. Clear it and move on.
You don't have to keep reloading a stuck save. Some quests are meant to be archived once done.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '真正的放下並不是丟掉，而是把曾經好好放進記憶裡' theme; rewritten with 相簿封存 / 不再翻 photo-album metaphor

zh-tw.content:
真正的放下，不是把回憶刪掉，
是把它收進相簿最後一頁，標記日期，然後不再每天翻。
它還在，只是你已經不靠它過日子了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 放下不等於遺忘。傳給那個以為「要徹底忘記才算走出來」的朋友——你可以記得，只是不再痛了，那才是真的好了。
variations: 釋懷不是清空，是你終於可以把那段放在角落，不用一直拿出來看。
你不用假裝沒愛過，你只要不再用那段定義現在的自己。

en.content:
Real letting go isn't deleting the memories.
It's filing them on the last page of the album, dating them, and no longer flipping back every day.
They're still there — you just don't live off them anymore.
en.editorNote: Letting go isn't forgetting. For the friend who thinks 'I have to completely forget to move on' — you can remember and still not hurt. That's what healed actually looks like.
variations: Moving on isn't wiping the slate. It's finally being able to leave that chapter in the corner without pulling it out constantly.
You don't have to pretend you never loved them. You just stop letting it define who you are now.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'You were my cup of tea, but I drink champagne now' caption; rewritten with 手搖飲 / 升級 Taiwan-friendly drink metaphor

zh-tw.content:
你曾經是我的微糖少冰，喝起來剛剛好。
後來才發現，我其實值得一杯料多到滿出來的。
謝謝你讓我知道，我可以加價升級。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把前任當成「喝過但不再點的那杯」最不傷人。適合放在 IG 限時，宣告自己換口味、過得更好。
variations: 他不是不好喝，是我長大了，嘴變刁了。
下一杯我要自己選料，不再將就別人幫我點的。

en.content:
You used to be my half-sugar, light-ice — just right at the time.
Then I realized I deserve the cup that's overflowing with toppings.
Thanks for teaching me I'm allowed to upgrade.
en.editorNote: Framing an ex as 'the drink I tried but no longer order' keeps it painless. Great for an IG story announcing you've changed your taste and you're doing better.
variations: He wasn't bad — I just grew up, and my taste got pickier.
Next cup, I'm picking my own toppings. No more settling for what someone else ordered for me.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '有些人來過你的世界，只是為了教會你如何告別' theme; rewritten with 教練 / 結業 fitness-class metaphor

zh-tw.content:
有些人走進你的人生，不是來陪你到老，是來當你的教練。
他教會你怎麼設界線、怎麼說不、怎麼好好告別。
課上完了，他下課了，但你練出來的肌肉是你自己的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把一段傷過你的感情當成「訓練課程」，痛就有了意義。傳給那個一直問「為什麼遇到他」的朋友——不是來折磨你，是來把你練強。
variations: 他是來教你功課的，不是來陪你寫一輩子作業的。
課程很硬，但結業之後的你，已經不是進場時那個人了。

en.content:
Some people walk into your life not to grow old with you, but to be your coach.
They teach you how to set boundaries, how to say no, how to say goodbye well.
The class ends, they clock out — but the muscle you built is yours to keep.
en.editorNote: Treating a relationship that hurt you as a 'training course' gives the pain meaning. For the friend asking 'why did I have to meet him?' — not to torment you, but to make you stronger.
variations: They came to teach you the lesson, not to do the homework with you forever.
The course was brutal, but the you who graduates isn't the same person who walked in.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'Love sucks. Pizza doesn't.' funny caption; rewritten with 滷味 / 從不已讀 Taiwan-friendly food framing

zh-tw.content:
愛情會讓你失望，滷味不會。
你選什麼它就給你什麼，從不挑食，也從不已讀。
這大概就是我目前最穩定的關係。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最不需要講道理的時刻，就配一份宵夜剛剛好。傳給剛分手的朋友，附上滷味照片殺傷力加倍。
variations: 感情會背叛你，但滷味老闆永遠記得你不要香菜。
下一段感情，我希望對方至少有滷味那麼懂我。

en.content:
Love lets you down. Late-night takeout doesn't.
You pick what you want, it never judges, and it never leaves you on read.
Honestly, it's the most stable relationship I've got right now.
en.editorNote: The post-breakup moment that needs zero life advice — just a midnight snack. Send to a freshly single friend with a food photo attached for double impact.
variations: Love might betray you, but the takeout place always remembers your order.
Next relationship, I just want someone who gets me the way my dinner does.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'From us to me, this solo chapter looks really good' caption; rewritten with 單人套餐 / 加大 dining-for-one metaphor

zh-tw.content:
以前點餐都要先問他要吃什麼，
現在我直接點單人套餐，還加大。
原來一個人吃飯不是孤單，是終於可以全部都照自己的意思。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最被低估的自由，是不用再配合別人的口味。傳給那個剛開始一個人生活、慢慢找回自己節奏的朋友。
variations: 從「我們要吃什麼」到「我想吃什麼」，這一步走得很爽。
一個人的餐桌沒有比較冷，是終於沒有人跟我搶最後一塊。

en.content:
I used to ask him what he wanted before ordering.
Now I just get the meal-for-one — and size it up.
Turns out eating alone isn't lonely. It's finally getting everything exactly my way.
en.editorNote: The most underrated post-breakup freedom is never accommodating someone else's taste again. For the friend starting solo life and slowly finding her own rhythm.
variations: Going from 'what should we eat' to 'what do I want' felt amazing.
A table for one isn't colder. There's just nobody fighting me for the last bite.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放下，才是最好的不打擾' theme; rewritten with 不再查勤 / 不再對號入座 daily-behavior framing

zh-tw.content:
我知道我真的放下了，是因為——
他發限時動態的時候，我沒有想對號入座；
他換了大頭貼，我也沒有想知道是誰拍的。
不是不在乎，是終於把注意力收回給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 釋懷不是大聲宣告，是那些小動作默默停了。傳給那個還在每天分析前任貼文的朋友——等你哪天懶得看了，就真的好了。
variations: 放下的證據不是刪好友，是你連點開都覺得沒必要。
真正走出來的那天很安靜，安靜到你自己都差點沒發現。

en.content:
I knew I'd really let go when —
he posted a story and I didn't try to read myself into it;
he changed his profile photo and I didn't wonder who took it.
It's not that I stopped caring. I just finally pulled my attention back to myself.
en.editorNote: Moving on isn't a loud announcement — it's the small habits quietly stopping. For the friend still analyzing her ex's posts daily: the day you can't be bothered to look is the day you're actually fine.
variations: Proof you've let go isn't unfriending them — it's not even feeling the need to click.
The day you truly move on is quiet. So quiet you almost miss it yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by savage 'thanks for the downgrade lesson' caption format; rewritten with 試用期 / 沒過 probation-period workplace metaphor

zh-tw.content:
他沒有甩我，是試用期沒過，被我資遣了。
表現評估：守時零分、溝通零分、情緒穩定度有待加強。
感謝應徵，但這個職缺我決定空著，自己一個人也能營運。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把分手當成「人資決策」最不傷自尊。傳給那個被分手後自我懷疑的朋友——不是你不夠好，是他試用期表現不及格。
variations: 他不是離職，是我考核沒讓他轉正。
這個職缺我寧可開天窗，也不要再找不適任的人。

en.content:
He didn't dump me. He failed probation, so I let him go.
Performance review: punctuality zero, communication zero, emotional stability needs improvement.
Thanks for applying, but I'm leaving this position open — I run just fine solo.
en.editorNote: Framing a breakup as an HR decision keeps your dignity intact. For the friend doubting herself after being dumped — it wasn't that you weren't enough. He just flunked his trial period.
variations: He didn't quit. I declined to make him permanent.
I'd rather leave the role empty than hire someone unqualified again.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '學會放下，擁抱更好的自己' theme; rewritten with 換季 / 收進衣櫃 seasonal-wardrobe metaphor

zh-tw.content:
放下一個人就像換季收衣服。
你不是討厭那件外套，是天氣變了，它不再適合現在的你。
把它好好摺起來收進衣櫃，不用丟掉，也不用每天穿在身上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 放下不必恨，也不必勉強遺忘。傳給那個覺得「不討厭他就代表還沒走出來」的朋友——你可以平靜地收好，那才是真的長大了。
variations: 有些感情像厚外套，陪你過了一個冬天，季節到了就該收起來。
你不用把回憶燒掉，只要不再每天披在身上就好。

en.content:
Letting someone go is like packing away clothes when the season changes.
It's not that you hate the coat — the weather shifted, and it no longer suits who you are now.
Fold it neatly, tuck it in the closet. You don't have to throw it out, and you don't have to wear it every day.
en.editorNote: Letting go doesn't require hatred or forced forgetting. For the friend who thinks 'not hating him means I haven't moved on' — you can pack it away calmly. That's what growing up actually looks like.
variations: Some relationships are like winter coats — they got you through one season, and then it's time to put them away.
You don't have to burn the memories. You just stop wearing them every single day.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'if my ex calls I'll hang up like a horror movie' savage caption; rewritten with 來電顯示 / 詐騙集團 phone-scam localization

zh-tw.content:
他現在打來，我接起來的反應跟接到詐騙電話一樣——
「您好，我這邊沒有您要的服務，請不要再撥打這支號碼。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 把前任歸類成「詐騙來電」最解氣。傳給那個還會手抖接前任電話的朋友，提醒她該封鎖就封鎖。
variations: 他的來電顯示我已經改成「拒接」，比封鎖溫柔一點，但效果一樣。
以前看到他打來會心跳加速，現在只想按擴音放給朋友聽笑話。

en.content:
If he calls now, I answer it exactly like I'd answer a scam call —
"Hello, we don't offer the service you're looking for. Please stop dialing this number."
en.editorNote: Filing your ex under 'spam caller' is the pettiest kind of peace. For the friend whose hands still shake when his name pops up — remind her the block button exists.
variations: I renamed his caller ID to 'Decline.' Gentler than a block, same result.
His call used to make my heart race. Now I just want to put it on speaker so my friends can laugh.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'growth begins where love ends' healing theme; rewritten with 房間重新裝潢 / 騰出空間 home-renovation metaphor

zh-tw.content:
他搬走以後，我把那個房間重新裝潢。
原來不是房子變大了，是我終於把擺給別人的位置，留給了自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後騰出來的空間，不是缺口，是可以重新規劃的自由。傳給那個剛恢復單身、開始重新佈置生活的朋友。
variations: 他留下的不是空位，是讓我終於可以放自己喜歡的東西的地方。
清空一個人之後，我才看見原來這個空間一直都是我的。

en.content:
After he moved out, I redecorated that room.
Turns out the place didn't get bigger — I just finally gave the space I'd been saving for someone else back to myself.
en.editorNote: The space a breakup clears isn't a hole — it's the freedom to redesign. For the friend who just went single and started rearranging her whole life.
variations: What he left behind wasn't an empty seat. It was room to finally put my own things.
After I cleared a person out, I realized the space was always mine to begin with.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing begins within' self-love theme; rewritten with 慢火燉湯 / 不能催 slow-cooking metaphor

zh-tw.content:
復原像燉一鍋湯，急不得。
你越想開大火快點好，越容易燒焦。
慢慢來，時間到了，自然會香。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀復原最忌諱「逼自己趕快好」。傳給那個一直催自己「怎麼還沒走出來」的朋友——你沒有慢，你只是還在燉。
variations: 好起來沒有快轉鍵，火候到了它自己會熟。
別人問你好了沒，你可以說：還在燉，香味快出來了。

en.content:
Healing is like simmering a pot of soup — you can't rush it.
The harder you crank the heat to finish faster, the more likely you are to burn it.
Take your time. When it's ready, the aroma comes on its own.
en.editorNote: The worst thing in breakup recovery is forcing yourself to 'hurry up and be okay.' For the friend nagging herself with 'why am I not over it yet' — you're not slow, you're still simmering.
variations: There's no fast-forward button for healing. When the heat's had enough time, it's done.
When people ask if you're over it, you can say: still simmering, the smell's almost there.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'single and ready to eat a whole pizza' funny caption format; rewritten with Taiwan 一個人火鍋 / 不用分料 localization

zh-tw.content:
單身又自由？
比較像是單身又可以一個人吃整鍋火鍋，
不用把蛋餃分給別人，也沒人偷夾我的肉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後第一個真正的快樂時刻，常常是發現「終於不用配合別人的口味」。傳給剛恢復單身的朋友，附一張一人鍋的照片更好笑。
variations: 分手最大的好處：火鍋料終於全部都是我的。
我不是孤單，我只是終於可以照自己的順序下菜。

en.content:
Single and free?
More like single and finally eating a whole hot pot alone —
no one to split the dumplings with, no one stealing my beef.
en.editorNote: The first real moment of joy after a breakup is often realizing you no longer have to match someone else's taste. Send to a newly single friend with a photo of a hot pot for one.
variations: Best part of the breakup: all the hot pot ingredients are finally mine.
I'm not lonely. I just get to cook everything in my own order now.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'love is blind but my breakup goggles are clear' caption; rewritten with 近視 / 度數對了 eyesight metaphor

zh-tw.content:
他們說愛情讓人盲目，我現在懂了。
分手之後我的視力突然回正常，
才看清楚他根本不是我想像的那個樣子——是我之前度數配錯了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後看清對方真面目，其實是好事。傳給那個總說「他以前不是這樣」的朋友——他一直都是這樣，只是你現在度數對了。
variations: 戀愛的時候我是高度近視，分手以後突然 1.0。
不是他變了，是我終於把濾鏡拿下來看清楚了。

en.content:
They say love is blind. Now I get it.
After the breakup, my eyesight snapped back to normal,
and I finally saw he was never who I imagined — my prescription was just wrong before.
en.editorNote: Seeing your ex clearly after a breakup is actually a good thing. For the friend who keeps saying 'he wasn't like this before' — he always was, your vision just corrected.
variations: In love I had terrible eyesight. Post-breakup, suddenly 20/20.
He didn't change. I just finally took off the filter and looked.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放下，才是最好的不打擾' canonical line; rewritten with 把鑰匙還回去 / 不再守門 letting-go metaphor

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把他從心裡趕出去，
是把那扇你一直幫他留著的門關上，
然後把鑰匙還給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 很多人放不下，是因為一直幫對方留著回來的位置。傳給那個還在「萬一他回來」的朋友——門關上不是恨，是你決定不再當守門的人。
variations: 你不是忘不了他，你只是還沒願意把那扇門上鎖。
釋懷是把等他的那把鑰匙，重新插回自己的門。

en.content:
Letting go isn't kicking them out of your heart.
It's closing the door you kept holding open for them,
and handing the key back to yourself.
en.editorNote: Many people can't let go because they keep a spot saved for the other person to come back to. For the friend still on 'what if they return' — closing the door isn't hatred, it's deciding to stop being the gatekeeper.
variations: You haven't failed to forget them. You just haven't been willing to lock the door yet.
Moving on is taking the key you saved for them and putting it back in your own door.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I lost in love but gained in freedom' empowerment line; rewritten with 對帳單 / 淨賺 accounting metaphor

zh-tw.content:
這段感情結算一下：
失去一個不珍惜我的人，賺回整個週末、所有的睡眠，還有對自己的話語權。
怎麼算都是淨賺。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後做一次「盤點」，常常會發現自己其實賺到了。傳給那個只盯著「失去」的朋友，提醒她另一欄寫滿了「賺回來」。
variations: 分手對帳單：支出一個前任，收入一整個自由。
別只看你失去什麼，看看你拿回了多少時間。

en.content:
Let's settle the accounts on this relationship:
Lost one person who didn't value me. Gained back my whole weekend, all my sleep, and the final say over my own life.
Net profit, any way you run the numbers.
en.editorNote: Doing an 'inventory' after a breakup often reveals you actually came out ahead. For the friend fixated on the 'lost' column — remind her the other column is full of things she got back.
variations: Breakup balance sheet: expense, one ex. Income, a whole lot of freedom.
Don't just count what you lost. Count how much time you got back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'whole snack, don't need anybody stealing my fries' humor caption; rewritten with 整份套餐 / 加價 Taiwan food metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我本人就是一整份套餐，主餐、副餐、飲料都齊。
誰想分一口薯條都得加價，更別說想白吃整份的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最重要的是把自我價值喊回來。傳給那個總覺得「沒人要」的朋友——不是沒人要，是你定價太佛心了。
variations: 我不是缺一塊的拼圖，我本來就是完整的那幅畫。
想吃我這份套餐，請先看清楚菜單價格。

en.content:
I'm a full combo meal — main, sides, and a drink, all included.
Want to steal a fry? That's extra. Want the whole thing for free? Keep dreaming.
en.editorNote: After a breakup, the key move is reclaiming your own worth. For the friend who feels 'nobody wants me' — they do, you were just priced way too generously.
variations: I'm not a puzzle missing a piece. I was always the whole picture.
Want a taste of this combo? Check the price on the menu first.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'exchanged my better half for a better peace' empowerment line; rewritten with 退貨 / 換購 consumer metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我把「另一半」退貨了，換購了一份「全部的自己」。
結果發現——後者本來就不用湊，我一個人就是滿件。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最大的覺醒：你從來不是半個人，不需要誰來把你補滿。傳給那個總說「我需要找到我的另一半」的朋友。
variations: 我不缺另一半，我缺的是早點發現自己是完整的。
退掉一個不合適的，換回一個一直都在的自己。

en.content:
I returned my 'better half' and exchanged it for a whole self.
Turns out — the second one was never on sale. I was always one complete piece.
en.editorNote: The biggest post-breakup awakening: you were never half a person who needed completing. For the friend always saying 'I need to find my other half.'
variations: I don't need a better half. I just needed to notice sooner that I was already whole.
Returned the one that didn't fit, got back the self that was here all along.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'thank goodness for small miracles / never find someone like him' savage caption; rewritten with 限量 / 缺貨 ironic framing

zh-tw.content:
他說我這輩子再也找不到像他這樣的人。
我說對啊，謝天謝地，這款已經停產了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 嗆得漂亮又不失優雅，適合分手後第一篇限時動態。重點是讓人覺得你已經過得很好，而且很慶幸。
variations: 再也找不到像他這樣的人？這正是我換手機號碼的原因。
他是限量款沒錯，限量到我一個就受夠了。

en.content:
He said I'd never find anyone like him again.
I said — thank goodness, that model's been discontinued.
en.editorNote: Savage but still classy, perfect for the first IG story after a breakup. The point is letting everyone see you're doing great and counting your blessings.
variations: Never find anyone like him again? That's exactly why I changed my number.
He's a limited edition, all right — so limited that one was already too many.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放下不是丟掉，是好好放進記憶裡' theme; rewritten with 收進抽屜 / 不上鎖 gentle-closure metaphor

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把你丟掉，是把那段日子好好摺好，收進抽屜。
我沒上鎖，只是再也沒有打開的理由了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 成熟的釋懷不是恨，也不是刪除，是溫柔地收好。傳給那個怕「放下＝背叛回憶」的朋友——你可以好好保留，也可以好好往前。
variations: 我沒有忘記你，我只是不再需要時時想起。
把回憶收起來，不是因為它不重要，是因為我終於有別的事可以做了。

en.content:
Letting go isn't throwing you away. It's folding those days neatly and tucking them in a drawer.
I didn't lock it — I just no longer have a reason to open it.
en.editorNote: Mature closure isn't hatred or deletion — it's gentle storage. For the friend afraid that 'moving on means betraying the memories' — you can keep them carefully and still move forward.
variations: I didn't forget you. I just no longer need to remember you all the time.
I put the memories away not because they don't matter, but because I finally have other things to do.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'breakup completed, self-respect upgraded, standards raised' empowerment caption; rewritten with 版本更新 / 標準提高 framing distinct from existing reboot item

zh-tw.content:
分手完成。自尊心：升級。
標準：永久調高，不再開放下修。
下一個想進來的，請先符合最低門檻。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀不是降級，是把標準調回它本來該有的高度。傳給那個曾經為了留住對方一再讓步的朋友——這次別再打折了。
variations: 這次分手最大的收穫，是我終於知道自己值得什麼。
標準不是難搞，是我終於肯尊重自己。

en.content:
Breakup: complete. Self-respect: upgraded.
Standards: permanently raised, no longer open to negotiation.
Next applicant, please meet the minimum requirements first.
en.editorNote: A breakup isn't a downgrade — it's resetting your standards back to where they should've been. For the friend who kept lowering the bar to hold onto someone. No more discounts this time.
variations: The biggest win from this breakup: I finally know what I deserve.
High standards aren't me being difficult. They're me finally respecting myself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'phoenixing — rising from the ashes renewed' 2026 caption trend; rewritten with 鳳凰 / 燒掉的是雜質 self-renewal angle

zh-tw.content:
分手後我不是被燒成灰，是像鳳凰一樣重新長出來。
燒掉的不是我，是那些不適合我的雜質。
你看到的不是傷口，是我發光的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀復原最美的版本：你不是修復，是重生。傳給那個覺得自己「整個人被燒光」的朋友——燒掉的只是雜質，主體還在，而且更亮了。
variations: 我沒有被毀掉，我只是換了一身新的羽毛。
別人以為那是灰燼，其實那是我重新起飛的跑道。

en.content:
After the breakup I wasn't burned to ash — I rose like a phoenix.
What burned off wasn't me. It was the impurities that never fit.
What you see isn't a wound. It's where I shine now.
en.editorNote: The most beautiful version of recovery: you're not repaired, you're reborn. For the friend who feels 'completely burned down' — only the impurities went up in smoke. The core's still here, and brighter.
variations: I wasn't destroyed. I just grew a brand-new set of feathers.
People think it's ashes. It's actually my runway for taking off again.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'never lend your heart to someone with bad credit' savage breakup humor; rewritten distinct from existing 信用卡停卡 item using 借出去 / 倒帳 lending angle

zh-tw.content:
教訓學到了：不要把心借給一個信用很差的人。
借出去的時候笑著說不用還，收回來的時候才發現連本金都沒了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把真心當借款看，分手就是認賠殺出。傳給那個一直在自責「我付出這麼多」的朋友——你沒有錯，你只是遇到一個不打算還的人。
variations: 下次借心之前，先查一下對方的還款紀錄。
我的真心不是不值錢，是借錯了人。

en.content:
Lesson learned: never lend your heart to someone with bad credit.
You hand it over smiling, saying 'no need to pay me back,' then realize you didn't even get the principal returned.
en.editorNote: Treating sincerity as a loan turns a breakup into cutting your losses. For the friend blaming herself for 'giving so much' — you weren't wrong, you just met someone who never planned to pay it back.
variations: Next time, run a credit check before lending out your heart.
My heart isn't worthless. I just loaned it to the wrong person.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'exchanged my better half for a better peace' empowerment caption; rewritten with 另一半 / 一整片安靜 wordplay localized for zh-tw

zh-tw.content:
我沒有失去「另一半」，我換到了一整片安靜。
以前我是半個人在配合，現在我是一個完整的人在過日子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 「另一半」這個詞本身就在暗示你不完整。失戀後最大的領悟是——你本來就是一整個。傳給那個害怕「一個人不夠完整」的朋友。
variations: 我不是少了一半，我是終於拿回了全部。
別人說我失去了另一半，我覺得我撿回了整個自己。

en.content:
I didn't lose my 'better half' — I traded it for a whole lot of peace.
I used to be half a person adjusting to someone. Now I'm a whole person just living.
en.editorNote: The phrase 'better half' already implies you're incomplete. The biggest post-breakup realization: you were always whole. For the friend scared that 'being alone means being unfinished.'
variations: I'm not missing half. I finally got all of myself back.
They say I lost my other half. I say I picked up my whole self.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '真正的放下是把曾經好好放進記憶裡' theme; rewritten distinct from bq-138 using 季節 / 換季 seasonal-passing metaphor

zh-tw.content:
你不是我犯的錯，你是我經過的一個季節。
冬天再冷，也沒有要我留在那裡的意思。
換季了，我把厚外套收起來，往前走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把一段感情當成「季節」而不是「錯誤」，就不會帶著悔恨。傳給那個一直說「都怪我當初瞎了眼」的朋友——你沒瞎，那只是一個會過去的季節。
variations: 他不是我的污點，是我人生的某一頁天氣。
再難熬的冬天也會過去，我不需要一直記得它有多冷。

en.content:
You weren't a mistake I made. You were a season I passed through.
No matter how cold the winter, it never meant for me to stay.
The season changed. I packed away the heavy coat and walked on.
en.editorNote: Treating a relationship as a 'season' rather than a 'mistake' means moving on without regret. For the friend who keeps saying 'I was such a fool back then' — you weren't blind, it was just a season that was always going to pass.
variations: He's not a stain on my record. He's a page of weather in my life.
Even the hardest winter ends. I don't have to keep remembering how cold it was.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'we ended but my story didn't — this is where my glow up begins' caption; rewritten with 完結 / 番外篇 spin-off framing distinct from existing 編劇/第二集 item

zh-tw.content:
我們的故事完結了，但我的故事還沒。
那段感情只是正篇，接下來是我一個人的番外篇——
而番外篇，常常比正篇還好看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 分手不是大結局，只是其中一條線收尾了。傳給那個覺得「沒有他人生就沒劇情了」的朋友——你的番外篇才正要開始，而且可以自己決定怎麼演。
variations: 他的戲份結束了，我的連載還在更新。
正篇是合寫的，番外篇我自己一個人寫，反而更自由。

en.content:
Our story ended, but mine didn't.
That relationship was just the main arc. What comes next is my solo spin-off —
and the spin-off is often better than the original.
en.editorNote: A breakup isn't the series finale, just one storyline wrapping up. For the friend who feels 'without him there's no plot left' — your spin-off is just beginning, and you get to decide how it goes.
variations: His screen time is over. My series is still updating.
The main arc was co-written. The spin-off is all mine — and that makes it freer.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'thanks for the experience, but I'm upgrading' breakup humor; rewritten with 系統更新 / 不支援舊型號 tech-upgrade framing distinct from existing 重灌系統 item

zh-tw.content:
謝謝你陪我跑完這個舊版本，
但我已經更新到不支援你這個型號了。
不是你不好，是你的系統真的太久沒維護。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把分手講成「升級」最不傷自己。適合在 IG 限動宣告新生活，語氣輕鬆又有點酸，朋友看了會偷笑。
variations: 我不是換掉你，是你停止更新太久了。
感謝舊版本的服務，但新版本不向下相容。

en.content:
Thanks for running through the old version with me,
but I've updated to a build that no longer supports your model.
It's not that you're bad — your system just hasn't been maintained in way too long.
en.editorNote: Framing a breakup as an 'upgrade' keeps your dignity intact. Perfect for an IG story announcing a fresh start — light, a little spicy, friends will smirk.
variations: I didn't replace you. You just stopped updating.
Thanks for the old version's service, but the new one isn't backward compatible.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'letting go doesn't mean you stop caring, it means realizing the only person you control is yourself' theme; rewritten with 鬆手 / 自己的手 grip metaphor

zh-tw.content:
放手不是不在乎了，
是你終於懂——能握住的，從來只有自己的手。
抓著一個轉身的人，最後磨破的是你自己的掌心。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個還死命抓著不放、覺得「再努力一下就好」的朋友。不是要她無情，是提醒她別再傷自己的手。
variations: 你能控制的不是他要不要留，是你要不要繼續抓。
鬆開的那一刻不是輸了，是終於還手給自己。

en.content:
Letting go doesn't mean you stopped caring.
It means you finally get it — the only hand you can hold is your own.
Clutch someone who's already turning away, and the only palm that ends up raw is yours.
en.editorNote: For the friend still gripping with everything she's got, sure 'one more try will fix it.' Not asking her to go cold — just reminding her to stop hurting her own hands.
variations: You can't control whether they stay. You can control whether you keep clutching.
The moment you let go isn't losing. It's finally giving your hand back to yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'respect yourself enough to walk away / you are worthy of healthy love' self-worth theme; rewritten with 標準 / 不降價 self-pricing metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我不是難追，是我的標準不打折。
你嫌貴可以不買，但別叫我自己降價。
會為了留住一個人而貶值的，從來不是好的感情。
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給那個總被嫌「要求太高」而開始懷疑自己的朋友。標準不是傲慢，是你知道自己值多少。
variations: 我不是高攀不起，是我不接受被殺價。
願意為你降低標準的那個人，最後通常會被你看不起。

en.content:
I'm not hard to get. My standards just don't go on sale.
Too pricey? Don't buy — but don't ask me to mark myself down.
Love that needs you to discount yourself to keep someone was never the good kind.
en.editorNote: For the friend told she's 'too demanding' until she starts doubting herself. Standards aren't arrogance — they're knowing your own worth.
variations: I'm not out of your league. I just don't accept lowball offers.
The person who lowers their standards for you usually ends up being the one you can't respect.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'breakup goggles are crystal clear now / love is blind' humor; rewritten with 濾鏡關掉 / 原圖 photo-filter framing distinct from existing 紅旗/聖誕裝飾 item

zh-tw.content:
戀愛的時候我開了十級美顏看他，
分手後濾鏡一關，看到原圖差點嚇到。
原來不是他變了，是我終於把眼睛調回正常模式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最爽的覺醒：看清原本被濾鏡蓋住的真相。適合在閨蜜聚會講，大家會一邊笑一邊點頭。
variations: 愛情是濾鏡，分手是原圖外洩。
以前覺得他發光，後來才發現那是我自己開的補光燈。

en.content:
When we were dating, I looked at him through a max-level beauty filter.
After the breakup I turned it off, saw the original photo, and nearly jumped.
He didn't change — I just finally set my eyes back to normal mode.
en.editorNote: Best post-breakup awakening: seeing the truth the filter was hiding. Drop this over drinks with friends — they'll laugh and nod at the same time.
variations: Love is the filter. The breakup is the original photo leaking.
I thought he was glowing. Turns out I was the one holding the ring light.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'breaking up is like knocking over a Coke machine — rock it back and forth' humor; rewritten with 飲料販賣機卡幣 Taiwan-friendly framing

zh-tw.content:
分手就像投幣後卡住的飲料機，
要前後搖好幾次，東西才會掉下來。
搖的時候很狼狽，但卡住的不放出來，你永遠喝不到下一罐。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀的拖泥帶水其實是正常程序，不是你不夠灑脫。傳給那個覺得「怎麼還沒走出來」而自責的朋友。
variations: 卡住的不是你，是那段早就該掉下來的感情。
搖一搖很丟臉，但總比站在原地等一罐永遠不會掉的飲料好。

en.content:
A breakup is like a vending machine that jams after you've paid.
You have to rock it back and forth a few times before it finally drops.
It looks clumsy — but if you don't shake the stuck one loose, you'll never get to the next can.
en.editorNote: The messy, drawn-out part of a breakup is a normal step, not a sign you're failing at it. For the friend blaming herself for 'still not being over it.'
variations: You're not the one stuck. It's the relationship that should've dropped ages ago.
Shaking it is embarrassing, sure — but beats standing there waiting on a can that's never coming.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'exchanged my better half for a better peace' empowerment line; rewritten with 另一半/完整 wholeness reframe distinct from existing items

zh-tw.content:
我沒有失去「另一半」。
我只是發現自己從來就不是一半，是完整的一個。
他離開帶走的不是我的一部分，是我以為自己缺的那塊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最大的解脫，是不再覺得「沒有人愛就不完整」。傳給那個習慣把自己定義成別人附屬品的朋友。
variations: 你不是少了一半，你是把多出來的那個人還回去了。
原來我不是被拼起來才完整，我本來就是整片。

en.content:
I didn't lose my 'other half.'
I just realized I was never half of anything — I was always a whole one.
What he took when he left wasn't a piece of me. It was the piece I only imagined was missing.
en.editorNote: The biggest relief after a breakup is no longer feeling 'incomplete without someone.' For the friend used to defining herself as someone's accessory.
variations: You're not missing half. You just handed back the extra person.
Turns out I was never a puzzle waiting to be completed. I was the whole picture.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by savage 'you were a lesson, not a loss' framing; rewritten with 學費 / 退費 tuition metaphor distinct from existing 信用卡/訂閱 items

zh-tw.content:
他不是我的損失，是我繳的學費。
貴是貴了點，但這堂「怎麼看人」的課，我一次就修過。
不退費，但保證以後不重修。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把失戀換算成學費，自責就會少很多。傳給那個一直心疼「浪費了那麼多時間」的朋友——學費不退，但你拿到證書了。
variations: 他不是渣，他是教材，而且是反面教材。
這筆學費我認了，因為我真的學會了。

en.content:
He wasn't my loss. He was tuition.
Pricey, sure — but I passed the 'how to read people' course in one take.
No refunds, but I'm guaranteed never to retake it.
en.editorNote: Converting a breakup into tuition cuts the self-blame way down. For the friend mourning 'all that wasted time' — the tuition's nonrefundable, but you walked away with the certificate.
variations: He wasn't trash. He was course material — the cautionary kind.
I'll eat the tuition, because I genuinely learned the lesson.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放下才是最好的不打擾' classic theme; rewritten with 設成靜音/封鎖 distinction and 自由 angle

zh-tw.content:
我沒有封鎖你，因為封鎖代表我還在意你會不會找我。
我只是把你設成靜音——
你還在，只是再也吵不到我的生活了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 真正的放下不是激烈的斷絕，是溫和的不在乎。傳給那個還在糾結「要不要封鎖前任」的朋友。
variations: 封鎖是還有情緒，靜音才是真的沒事了。
我不恨你，我只是把音量轉到零。

en.content:
I didn't block you — blocking would mean I still care whether you'd reach out.
I just muted you.
You're still there. You just can't make noise in my life anymore.
en.editorNote: Real letting go isn't a dramatic cutoff — it's a gentle indifference. For the friend agonizing over whether to block their ex.
variations: Blocking means there's still emotion. Muting means I'm actually fine.
I don't hate you. I just turned your volume down to zero.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '先讓自己好好難過一回' / permission-to-grieve theme; rewritten with 退潮 / 漲潮 tide metaphor

zh-tw.content:
難過的時候不用急著叫自己堅強。
眼淚像退潮，會把你以為帶不走的東西，慢慢沖回大海。
等它退完，你才看得到底下原本就有的沙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀初期最需要的不是道理，是被允許難過。傳給那個一直逼自己「要趕快好起來」的朋友。
variations: 哭不是軟弱，是身體幫你把那個人慢慢倒出來。
潮水退了會再漲，但下次漲上來的，是新的你。

en.content:
When it hurts, don't rush to order yourself to be strong.
Tears are like an outgoing tide — they slowly carry back to the sea the things you thought you couldn't release.
Only once it's pulled all the way out do you see the sand that was always underneath.
en.editorNote: Early on, you don't need wisdom — you need permission to grieve. For the friend forcing herself to 'hurry up and heal.'
variations: Crying isn't weakness. It's your body slowly pouring that person out.
The tide goes out, then comes back in — but next time, what rises is a new you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'single and ready to get nervous around anyone attractive' savage caption; rewritten with 自我吐槽 social-anxiety angle for Taiwan audience

zh-tw.content:
正式宣布恢復單身：可以重新開始對任何長得好看的人緊張到不會講話。
戀愛技能歸零，社交災難重新上線。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把恢復單身講成「重灌社交障礙」最好笑。傳給剛分手、開始重新面對曖昧的朋友，一起笑自己生疏。
variations: 單身的意思是：又可以為了一句早安緊張一整天了。
重回戀愛市場第一天，發現我的撩人技能還停留在出廠設定。

en.content:
Officially single again: free to get so nervous around attractive people that I forget how to form sentences.
Dating skills reset to zero. Social disaster mode rebooting.
en.editorNote: Reframing 'back to single' as 'reinstalling my social anxiety' lands the laugh. For the freshly single friend facing the talking stage again — laugh at being rusty together.
variations: Single means I get to panic over a good morning text all over again.
Day one back on the market and my flirting skills are still on factory settings.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'love is grand but have you tried not sharing your fries' humor; rewritten with 鹹酥雞獨享 Taiwan localization

zh-tw.content:
戀愛很偉大，但你有試過一整份鹹酥雞不用分人嗎？
我現在連那塊最大的雞排都是我的，這才叫真正的自由。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀的隱藏福利：再也不用把好料讓給別人。傳給剛單身、第一次點宵夜不用問對方要不要的朋友。
variations: 單身最爽的不是沒人管，是那塊最大的不用讓了。
以前點兩份怕他餓，現在點一份全是我的——升級了。

en.content:
Love is grand, but have you ever tried eating a whole basket of fries without sharing?
That biggest piece is mine now. This is what real freedom tastes like.
en.editorNote: The hidden perk of a breakup: you never have to give away the good bits again. For the friend ordering late-night food solo for the first time, no one to ask.
variations: The best part of being single isn't no one nagging — it's not having to hand over the biggest piece.
I used to order extra so he wouldn't go hungry. Now I order one and it's all mine. Upgrade.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'exchanged my better half for a better peace' empowerment line; rewritten with 對帳 / 損益 accounting metaphor

zh-tw.content:
我沒有失去「另一半」，我只是把虧損的部位停損了。
換來的不是空缺，是一整片屬於自己的安靜。
這筆帳，怎麼算我都是賺的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把感情當投資對帳，分手就從虧損變成停損出場。傳給那個還在算「在一起這麼久不甘心」的朋友——別凹單了，止損也是一種賺。
variations: 失去他不是減項，是把一直在賠錢的部位清掉。
我換掉的不是一個人，是換回一整片自己的安靜。

en.content:
I didn't lose my 'better half.' I cut my losses on a position that kept bleeding.
What I got back wasn't an empty space — it was a whole stretch of quiet that's mine.
Do the books any way you like: I came out ahead.
en.editorNote: Treating love like reconciling a portfolio turns a breakup from a loss into a stop-loss exit. For the friend stuck on 'we were together so long, I can't accept it' — stop averaging down. Cutting losses is its own kind of win.
variations: Losing him isn't a deduction. It's clearing out a position that kept losing money.
I didn't trade away a person. I traded back a whole stretch of my own quiet.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'letting go was about finding myself again' healing frame; rewritten with 整理衣櫃 / 留白 decluttering metaphor

zh-tw.content:
分手就像整理衣櫃，把那件再也穿不下的關係折好收走。
空出來的位置我沒有急著塞新的，
我想先看看，原來我的衣櫃這麼大。
zh-tw.editorNote: 放下不是為了趕快找下一個填補，是先把空間留給自己。傳給那個剛分手就被催「快去認識新對象」的朋友——空著也很好。
variations: 清掉一段感情不是為了騰位置給別人，是為了看清自己有多少空間。
衣櫃空了不代表要立刻買新的，留白本身就很好看。

en.content:
A breakup is like cleaning out your closet — you fold up the relationship that no longer fits and put it away.
I'm not rushing to stuff the empty space with something new.
I just want to stand here and notice how big my closet actually is.
en.editorNote: Letting go isn't about quickly finding a replacement to fill the gap — it's about leaving the space for yourself first. For the friend being pushed to 'go meet someone new' right after a breakup. Empty is fine too.
variations: Clearing out a relationship isn't to make room for someone else. It's to see how much room I actually have.
An empty closet doesn't mean buy something new. The blank space looks good on its own.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I dodged a bullet' savage breakup caption; rewritten with 安全帽/車禍 Taiwan everyday metaphor

zh-tw.content:
大家都說我躲過一顆子彈，
但說真的，我是連安全帽都沒戴就騎過去，還能全身而退。
這不是運氣，這是命大。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後回頭看才發現自己其實逃過一劫。傳給那個還在惋惜「差一點就結婚了」的朋友——差那一點，正好救了你。
variations: 別人是擦傷，我是整台車翻了還能站起來走，這不叫失戀，叫逃生成功。
回頭看那段感情，我不是失去，是逃出來的。

en.content:
Everyone says I dodged a bullet.
Honestly? I rode straight through without a helmet and walked away without a scratch.
That's not luck. That's a miracle.
en.editorNote: Looking back after a breakup, you realize you escaped a disaster. For the friend still mourning 'we almost got married' — that 'almost' is exactly what saved you.
variations: Others got a scratch. I flipped the whole car and still stood up and walked. That's not heartbreak, that's a successful escape.
Looking back at that relationship, I didn't lose anything. I got out.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'Love sucks, pizza doesn't' caption; rewritten with 珍奶/不會已讀 Taiwan localization

zh-tw.content:
戀愛很爛，但珍奶不會。
它從不忽冷忽熱，你要全糖它就全糖，你要去冰它真的去冰。
光是這份誠實，就贏過我前任整整一年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀第一週靠美食撐過去最實際。傳給剛分手的閨蜜，附一杯珍奶外送單，比講一百句道理有用。
variations: 前任會變心，但珍奶永遠記得你要半糖少冰。
下一段感情，我只要求對方有珍奶店員一半的記性。

en.content:
Love sucks. Bubble tea doesn't.
It never runs hot and cold — you say full sugar, it's full sugar; you say no ice, it's actually no ice.
That honesty alone beats my ex's entire year.
en.editorNote: Surviving the first week post-breakup on snacks is the most practical plan. Send a friend a bubble tea delivery order — works better than a hundred pep talks.
variations: An ex changes their mind. Bubble tea always remembers your order.
Next relationship, I just want someone with half the memory of the boba clerk.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'You are not half of anything, you are whole' self-love theme; rewritten with 缺角/拼圖 puzzle metaphor

zh-tw.content:
你不是一塊等著被拼上的缺角。
你本來就是完整的一幅畫，
他離開，只是把擋在你前面的人移開了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀最常見的誤會是覺得「少了他我就不完整」。其實你從來都是完整的。傳給那個總說「我們是彼此的另一半」現在卻很迷惘的朋友。
variations: 你不需要另一半才完整，你需要的是別人別再說你不夠。
拼圖少一塊才需要別人，你又不是拼圖，你是整幅畫。

en.content:
You're not a missing piece waiting to be slotted in.
You were always the whole picture.
Them leaving just moved someone out of your way.
en.editorNote: The most common breakup lie is 'I'm incomplete without them.' You were always whole. For the friend who used to say 'we're each other's other half' and now feels lost.
variations: You don't need another half to be complete. You need people to stop telling you that you're not enough.
A puzzle needs missing pieces. You're not a puzzle — you're the whole painting.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'don't let a breakup break you, let it build you' empowerment frame; rewritten with 健身/重量 gym metaphor

zh-tw.content:
別讓一段感情把你壓垮。
那些痛就像健身房的重量——
當下覺得快撐不住，撐過去之後，你會變得比以前更有力。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀的痛不是白受的，是在長肌肉。傳給那個正在最低潮、覺得自己再也站不起來的朋友——你不是被壓垮，你是在練更強的自己。
variations: 心碎不會殺死你，它只會讓你下次更難被擊倒。
現在很重，是因為你正在變強的路上。

en.content:
Don't let a relationship break you.
That pain is like weights at the gym —
it feels unbearable in the moment, but once you push through, you come out stronger than before.
en.editorNote: The pain of a breakup isn't wasted — you're building muscle. For the friend at her lowest, convinced she'll never get up again — you're not being crushed, you're training a tougher version of yourself.
variations: Heartbreak won't kill you. It just makes you harder to knock down next time.
It feels heavy now because you're on your way to getting stronger.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'deleting your number was therapeutic' moving-on caption; rewritten with 封鎖/捷運末班車 Taiwan localization

zh-tw.content:
按下封鎖鍵的那一刻，比我想像中還療癒。
就像趕上捷運末班車——門關上的瞬間有點不捨，
但下一秒就慶幸，還好我上車了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 封鎖前任不是賭氣，是為自己關上一扇會漏風的門。傳給那個一直在猶豫「要不要封鎖」的朋友——關上的同時，你也終於可以往前走了。
variations: 刪掉他的號碼那天，我的世界沒有崩塌，反而安靜得很舒服。
封鎖不是恨，是給自己一個不會再回頭的理由。

en.content:
The moment I hit block was more therapeutic than I expected.
It's like catching the last train — there's a flicker of regret as the doors close,
then, a second later, relief that I made it on.
en.editorNote: Blocking an ex isn't spite — it's closing a door that kept letting the cold in. For the friend stuck on 'should I block them?' — the moment it closes, you finally get to move forward.
variations: The day I deleted his number, my world didn't collapse. It just got quiet — a comfortable kind of quiet.
Blocking isn't hate. It's giving yourself a reason not to look back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'you are not half of anything, you are whole' self-worth angle; rewritten to reframe being single as being complete rather than missing a piece

zh-tw.content:
你不是某個人的另一半，
你本來就是完整的一個人。
他離開帶走的不是你的一塊，是他自己而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個分手後覺得「自己空了一塊」的朋友。提醒她：缺的不是你，走的是他。
variations: 你從來就不缺一半，你只是暫時忘了自己一個人也很完整。
別把他的離開算成你的損失，有時候那是清空，不是缺口。

en.content:
You were never someone's other half.
You were always a whole person.
What they took when they left wasn't a piece of you — it was just themselves.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels like a chunk of her went missing after the split. Remind her: you're not the missing piece — he is the thing that left.
variations: You were never half of anything. You just forgot, for a while, that you're complete on your own.
Don't file their leaving under 'my loss.' Sometimes it's space clearing out, not a hole opening up.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'when you know your worth, you don't lose people, people lose you'; rewritten with a more grounded, conversational Taiwanese tone

zh-tw.content:
當你開始懂自己的好，
就不會覺得是你失去了誰，
而是有人，沒福氣留住你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後正在重新喜歡自己的階段。把焦點從「我被丟下」轉成「他沒留住我」。
variations: 不是你不夠好他才走，是他不夠好，才看不出你的好。
等你真的看得起自己，就會發現走掉的那個，才是真的虧到。

en.content:
The day you start seeing your own worth,
it stops feeling like you lost someone —
and starts feeling like someone wasn't lucky enough to keep you.
en.editorNote: For the stage right after a breakup when you're learning to like yourself again. Shifts the frame from 'I got left' to 'they failed to keep me.'
variations: He didn't leave because you weren't enough. He left because he wasn't enough to see it.
Once you actually value yourself, you realize the one who walked is the one who lost out.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'accept what is, let go of what was, have faith in what will be'; rewritten into a tighter three-beat line

zh-tw.content:
接受現在這樣，
放過已經那樣，
然後相信，總會變成另一種樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合卡在「為什麼會變成這樣」的情緒裡走不出來的時候。三段式節奏，唸起來像給自己的呼吸。
variations: 別跟過去吵架了，它不會改，但你會。
現在的難不是結局，只是還沒翻到下一頁而已。

en.editorNote: For when you're stuck looping on 'how did it end up like this.' The three beats read like a breathing exercise you give yourself.
variations: Stop arguing with the past — it won't change, but you will.
The hard part you're in right now isn't the ending. You just haven't turned the page yet.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'choose yourself every day, you deserve love that stays'; rewritten to contrast staying love with love you have to chase

zh-tw.content:
你值得的，不是要你拼命留住的愛，
是那種會自己留下來的愛。
所以先學會，每天都選自己一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給總是在感情裡用力過頭、怕被丟下的朋友。重點是：好的愛不用你追，而你可以先成為自己的那一票。
variations: 需要你苦苦挽留的，從來都不是愛，是你的不甘心。
與其追著一個會走的人，不如每天都先把自己選回來。

en.content:
What you deserve isn't love you have to fight to keep.
It's love that stays on its own.
So start small — choose yourself, once, every single day.
en.editorNote: For the friend who always over-gives in relationships out of fear of being left. The point: real love doesn't make you chase — and you can be the first vote for yourself.
variations: Anything you have to beg to keep was never love — it was your own refusal to let go.
Instead of chasing someone who's halfway out the door, pick yourself back up first, every day.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'some people enter your world only to teach you how to say goodbye' idea; rewritten to land on gratitude rather than loss

zh-tw.content:
有些人出現在你生命裡，
不是要陪你走到最後，
是來教你怎麼好好說再見。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手一陣子、情緒沒那麼痛、開始能回頭看的時候。把一段關係的意義從「失去」翻成「學會」。
variations: 謝謝他的離開，讓我練習了一次，怎麼放手而不恨。
不是每個人都要留下，有些人本來就只是一堂課。

en.content:
Some people show up in your life
not to walk with you to the end,
but to teach you how to say a good goodbye.
en.editorNote: For a while after the breakup, when it hurts less and you can finally look back. Reframes the relationship's meaning from 'what I lost' to 'what I learned.'
variations: Thank you for leaving — you gave me one good rehearsal at letting go without the hate.
Not everyone is meant to stay. Some people were only ever a lesson.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'your worth isn't negotiable' self-respect theme; rewritten into a concrete refusal-to-discount image

zh-tw.content:
你的價值不是他願不願意看見決定的。
他看不到，是他眼睛的問題，不是你打折的理由。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個分手後一直檢討「是不是我不夠好」的朋友。把問題從「我不夠好」翻回「他剛好不識貨」。
variations: 他不要，不代表你不值得，只代表你們不適合。
別因為一個人沒看懂你，就把自己標成過季商品。

en.content:
Your worth isn't decided by whether they bothered to see it.
Them missing it is their eyesight problem, not your discount.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck on 'maybe I wasn't good enough' after a breakup. Flips the blame from 'I'm lacking' back to 'they just couldn't read the price tag.'
variations: Them not wanting you doesn't mean you're not worth it — it means you didn't fit.
Don't mark yourself down to clearance just because one person couldn't read the tag.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'let go to make space for something better'; rewritten into a packing/moving metaphor to keep it concrete and non-preachy

zh-tw.content:
放手不是認輸，是把佔位子的東西清掉。
空出來的地方，本來就不是要留給回憶的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合卡在「捨不得」階段的朋友。重點不是逼自己丟，是提醒他：空間留著是要給以後的人和事，不是給舊的。
variations: 清掉不是因為討厭，是因為新的東西需要地方放。
你不是把他丟了，你只是把位子還給自己。

en.content:
Letting go isn't admitting defeat — it's clearing out what's hogging the space.
The room you free up was never meant to be a storage unit for memories.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck in the 'I can't bear to' stage. The point isn't forcing yourself to throw things out — it's a reminder that the space is for what's coming, not what's gone.
variations: You're not clearing it out because you hate it. You're clearing it out because the new stuff needs somewhere to go.
You didn't throw them away. You just gave the space back to yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the comeback is stronger than the setback'; rewritten into a Taiwan-flavored everyday comeback image, avoiding the sports cliché

zh-tw.content:
現在很慘沒關係，慘的版本不是最終版。
等你過一陣子回來看，會發現這只是更新前的那個你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛分手、整個人很低落的朋友。不催他振作，只是先給他一個「這不是結局」的安全感。
variations: 你現在不是壞掉，你只是在重開機。
最慘的這幾天，以後會變成你拿來笑的故事。

en.content:
It's okay to be a mess right now — the mess isn't the final version.
Come back to this in a while and you'll see it was just the you before the update.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just broke up and is completely flattened. Doesn't push them to bounce back — just hands them the safety of 'this isn't the ending.'
variations: You're not broken right now. You're just rebooting.
These worst days will turn into the story you laugh about later.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you are not half of anything, you are whole'; rewritten to land on a self-contained, non-needy completeness

zh-tw.content:
你不是誰的另一半，你本來就是一個完整的人。
少了他，你沒有變成半個，只是少了一個習慣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後覺得「身邊空一塊」的朋友。把「失去另一半」翻成「拿回整個自己」，不悲情但有撐住的力量。
variations: 你不是被剩下，你是被釋放。
一個人不是不完整，是終於不用配合別人的版本。

en.content:
You're not anyone's other half — you were always a whole person.
Without them you didn't become half of yourself. You just lost a habit.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels a blank spot beside them after a breakup. Reframes 'losing your other half' into 'getting your whole self back' — steady, not sad.
variations: You weren't left behind. You were let loose.
Being on your own isn't being incomplete. It's finally not having to run someone else's version of you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '分手只是換一個劇場，人生繼續精彩' theatre metaphor; rewritten around an audience-leaving image rather than switching theatres

zh-tw.content:
他離場的時候別追，那只是中場休息，不是散場。
你的人生還很長，後面的劇情精彩到他會後悔提早走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後覺得「故事結束了」的朋友。把離開講成中場，而不是結局，留下繼續往下走的力氣。
variations: 他先走了沒關係，又不是只有他買得起這場票。
退場的人看不到後面的劇情，那是他的損失。

en.content:
When he walks out, don't chase him — it's intermission, not the end of the show.
Your story runs long, and the next act gets good enough that he'll regret leaving early.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels like 'the story is over' after a breakup. Reframes the exit as an intermission, not the finale, so there's reason to keep going.
variations: Him leaving first is fine — he's not the only one who could afford a ticket.
The one who walks out never sees how it ends. That's his loss.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the cure for a broken heart is self-love'; rewritten into a concrete daily-habit framing instead of a slogan

zh-tw.content:
治心碎的藥不是時間，是你終於開始好好對自己。
他沒有的溫柔，你可以自己給。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合催朋友「好好吃飯、好好睡覺」的時候用。把抽象的自我療癒，落到每天怎麼對自己這件小事上。
variations: 與其等他回來疼你，不如先學會自己疼自己。
你不是在等誰來救，你是自己慢慢把自己撿回來。

en.content:
The cure for heartbreak isn't time — it's finally starting to treat yourself well.
The tenderness he never gave you, you can give yourself.
en.editorNote: Use this when you're nudging a friend to eat properly and sleep. Brings abstract 'self-love' down to the small daily act of how you treat yourself.
variations: Instead of waiting for him to come back and love you, learn to love yourself first.
You're not waiting to be rescued — you're slowly picking yourself back up.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'sometimes walking away is the strongest thing you can do'; rewritten to flip the cultural read of leaving as weakness

zh-tw.content:
願意先走的那個人，不是比較不愛，是比較勇敢。
留下來忍，從來不是堅強，放手才是。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那個一直自責「是不是我先放棄」的朋友。把離開重新定義成勇敢，而不是背叛或軟弱。
variations: 先轉身的人，常常是先看清楚的人。
你不是逃，你是終於不想再委屈自己。

en.content:
The one willing to leave first isn't the one who loved less — they're the one who was braver.
Staying to endure was never strength. Letting go is.
en.editorNote: For the friend blaming themselves for 'giving up first.' Redefines walking away as courage, not betrayal or weakness.
variations: The one who turns away first is often the one who saw clearly first.
You didn't run away — you just stopped being willing to shrink yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '真正的放下並不是丟掉，而是把曾經好好放在記憶裡'; rewritten to reframe letting go as filing memories away rather than deleting them

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把那段回憶刪掉，
是終於可以把它好好收進抽屜，不再每天拿出來摸。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給那個一直覺得「忘不掉就是還沒走出來」的朋友。重點不是清空，是不再被回憶綁架。
variations: 不是要你忘記，是要你不再每天回去重看一遍。
曾經很好，現在收好，這樣就夠了。

en.content:
Letting go isn't deleting the memory.
It's finally being able to put it in a drawer and stop taking it out every single day.
en.editorNote: For the friend who thinks 'if I can't forget, I haven't moved on.' The point isn't erasing it — it's no longer being held hostage by it.
variations: Nobody's asking you to forget. Just to stop rereading it every night.
It was good once. Now put it away. That's enough.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you can't start the next chapter if you keep re-reading the last one'; rewritten with a self-aware, slightly wry tone

zh-tw.content:
你翻來覆去看的那一頁，已經寫完了。
下一章不會自己開始，除非你願意翻過去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給卡在原地一直反芻同一段感情的人。語氣帶點推一把的鼓勵，不說教。
variations: 故事沒爛尾，只是那章該結束了。
你一直停在最後一頁，後面那麼多空白頁都在等你。

en.content:
That page you keep rereading? It's already finished.
The next chapter won't start itself until you're willing to turn it.
en.editorNote: For someone stuck replaying the same relationship on loop. A gentle nudge forward — encouraging, not preachy.
variations: The story didn't end badly. That chapter was just supposed to end.
You're frozen on the last page while a whole book of blank ones waits.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you are not broken; you are healing, and that's the bravest thing you can be'; rewritten to push back on the self-talk of being 'damaged'

zh-tw.content:
你不是壞掉了，你是在復原。
會痛代表傷口還活著，活著才好得了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給那種覺得「我是不是再也愛不了了」的朋友。把脆弱重新講成正在癒合的證據。
variations: 結痂之前一定會癢會痛，這不是退步，是在長新的皮。
你沒有比較差，你只是還在好起來的路上。

en.content:
You're not broken. You're healing.
The fact that it still hurts means the wound is alive — and alive things heal.
en.editorNote: For the friend who fears 'maybe I can't love anymore.' Reframes feeling fragile as proof of healing, not damage.
variations: It itches and stings before it scars. That's not a setback — that's new skin.
You're not worse off. You're just still on the way back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '真正的放下並不是丟掉，而是把曾經好好放進記憶'; rewritten to reframe letting go as keeping the memory gently rather than erasing it

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把那段感情丟掉，
是終於可以把它放進記憶裡，不再拿出來割自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給那種覺得「忘不掉就是還沒走出來」的朋友。重點不是刪掉回憶，是讓回憶不再傷人。
variations: 你不用假裝沒愛過，只要學會把它放在不會再痛的地方。
真正的好起來，是想起來會笑一下，而不是再哭一場。

en.content:
Letting go isn't throwing the relationship away.
It's finally being able to set it down in your memory without cutting yourself on it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who thinks 'if I can't forget, I haven't moved on.' The goal isn't deleting the memory — it's making the memory stop hurting.
variations: You don't have to pretend you never loved them. Just learn to keep it somewhere that doesn't sting.
Real healing is remembering and smiling a little, instead of crying all over again.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the best part about a breakup is realizing you're whole even without them'; rewritten to stress completeness predating the relationship

zh-tw.content:
他離開以後你才發現，原來你一直都是完整的。
他不是你缺的那一塊，他只是借住過一陣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給那種覺得「沒有他我就不完整」的朋友。提醒對方：你不是被拿走一塊，你只是收回了借出去的房間。
variations: 你不是因為他才完整，你是完整地遇見了他，又完整地走了。
他帶走的是他自己，不是你的一部分。

en.content:
After they left, you realized you were whole the whole time.
They were never the missing piece — they were just a guest who stayed a while.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels 'I'm incomplete without them.' Reminds them: nothing was taken — you just took back a room you'd lent out.
variations: You weren't completed by them. You met them whole, and you left whole.
What they took with them was themselves — not a piece of you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'accept what is, let go of what was, have faith in what will be'; rewritten into a plainer, more conversational three-beat reframe

zh-tw.content:
接受現在這樣，放過已經那樣，
然後相信，還沒發生的那些會更好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給卡在「為什麼會這樣」的朋友。三句話分別對應現在、過去、未來，幫對方把目光從回頭看慢慢轉向往前走。
variations: 現在很爛沒關係，過去很痛也沒關係，只要你還願意往前看。
你不用馬上好起來，先答應自己不回頭就好。

en.content:
Accept how things are, forgive how things were,
and trust that what hasn't happened yet will be kinder.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck on 'why did this happen?' Three lines for present, past, and future — gently turning their gaze from looking back to moving forward.
variations: It's okay that now is rough and the past still aches — as long as you're still willing to look ahead.
You don't have to be okay right away. Just promise yourself you won't turn back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'don't let a breakup break you; let it build you'; rewritten with a construction metaphor and Taiwan-casual tone

zh-tw.content:
別讓一段分手把你拆掉，
讓它把你重蓋成你早就想成為的那個人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給正在低潮、覺得「我整個人都垮了」的朋友。把崩潰重新講成打掉重練的工程，而不是毀滅。
variations: 拆掉的不是你，是那個一直在配合別人的版本。
這次不是你壞了，是你終於有機會照自己的樣子重蓋一次。

en.content:
Don't let a breakup tear you down —
let it rebuild you into the person you were always meant to be.
en.editorNote: For the friend in a low spot who feels 'I'm completely wrecked.' Reframes the collapse as a demolition-and-rebuild, not a ruin.
variations: What got torn down wasn't you — it was the version that kept bending to fit someone else.
You're not broken this time. You finally get to rebuild on your own blueprint.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'sometimes the most important person to fall in love with is yourself'; rewritten as a redirect of the energy once spent on an ex

zh-tw.content:
你那些拿來愛他、等他、猜他的力氣，
現在全部還給你了，記得花在自己身上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給剛分手、突然不知道把心思放哪的朋友。提醒對方：那份心力沒有消失，只是換你當收件人。
variations: 以前你把最好的都給他，這次換你給自己一次。
省下來的那些等待和遷就，足夠把自己重新養好。

en.content:
All that energy you spent loving them, waiting on them, second-guessing them —
it's yours again now. Spend it on yourself.
en.editorNote: For the freshly single friend who suddenly doesn't know where to put all that attention. Reminds them: the energy didn't vanish — you're just the recipient now.
variations: You used to give them your best. This time, give it to yourself.
All the waiting and compromising you just got back is more than enough to rebuild you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'respect yourself enough to walk away'; rewritten to frame walking away as choosing yourself rather than losing them

zh-tw.content:
走開不是因為不夠愛，
是因為終於夠愛自己了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給那個一直在問「我是不是太狠心」的朋友。提醒他離開不是冷血，是自我尊重的表現。
variations: 離開一個不珍惜你的人，不叫放棄，叫清醒。
你不是輸了這段感情，是贏回了自己。

en.content:
I didn't walk away because I loved you too little.
I walked away because I finally loved myself enough.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps asking 'was I too harsh?' Reminds them that leaving isn't cold — it's self-respect.
variations: Leaving someone who doesn't value you isn't giving up. It's waking up.
You didn't lose the relationship. You won yourself back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'letting go creates space for better'; rewritten as making room rather than emptiness

zh-tw.content:
放手後空出來的那塊位置，
不是用來想念的，是留給更好的東西進來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給剛分手、覺得生活突然空了一塊的朋友。把空缺從失去重新講成空間。
variations: 心裡騰出來的空位，不是傷口，是還沒被填滿的可能。
離開不是把你掏空，是幫你清出位子。

en.content:
The space left when you let go
isn't there for missing them — it's there to let something better in.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels life suddenly has a hole in it. Reframes the gap from a loss into an opening.
variations: The empty space inside isn't a wound. It's room that hasn't been filled yet.
Them leaving didn't hollow you out. It cleared you a space.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I loved you deeply, but I love myself more'; rewritten to land the contrast more plainly and warmly

zh-tw.content:
我是真的很愛你，
但我發現，我更不想弄丟我自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合給卡在「明明還愛著，為什麼要分」的朋友。承認感情是真的，但把自己放回第一順位。
variations: 我沒有不愛你，我只是更不捨得繼續委屈自己。
愛你是真的，但留下來的代價是我，這筆帳我付不起。

en.content:
I really did love you.
I just realized I wasn't willing to lose myself to keep you.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck on 'but I still love them, why leave?' Validates that the love was real while putting themselves back first.
variations: It's not that I stopped loving you. I just couldn't keep shrinking myself to stay.
Loving you was real. But the price of staying was me, and I couldn't afford it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'stop begging for love, start believing you deserve it' self-worth theme; reframed as a quiet realization rather than a slogan

zh-tw.content:
有一天你會突然發現，
你不是不夠好，你只是把好都給了不值得的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個一直在檢討自己「是不是我哪裡做錯」的朋友。把問題從「我不夠好」轉回「對象選錯了」。
variations: 你不缺愛人的能力，你只是曾經把它交給了不會珍惜的人。
缺的從來不是你，是那個看不見你有多好的人。

en.content:
One day it just hits you:
you weren't lacking anything — you just gave your best to someone who didn't deserve it.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck replaying 'what did I do wrong?' Moves the blame off their worth and onto a bad choice of person.
variations: You never ran out of love to give. You just handed it to someone who wouldn't hold it.
