The problem was never you. It was them, not seeing what they had.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'allow yourself to grieve, then keep moving' healing theme; rewritten to permit the sadness instead of rushing past it

zh-tw.content:
你不用急著好起來。
難過也是愛過的證明，慢慢來，沒有人在計時。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個逼自己「趕快振作」卻更累的朋友。給對方悲傷的許可，而不是催促。
variations: 想哭就哭，這不是退步，是你在好好跟過去道別。
復原沒有進度條，你想哭多久，就哭多久。

en.content:
You don't have to be okay on a schedule.
The sadness is proof you loved. Take your time — nobody's holding a stopwatch.
en.editorNote: For the friend exhausting themselves trying to 'just get over it.' Gives permission to grieve instead of pushing them to hurry.
variations: Cry if you need to. It's not a setback — it's you saying a proper goodbye.
Healing has no progress bar. Take exactly as long as you need.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'breakup is the only road to finding your soulmate' theme; reframed the ending as a redirection, not a loss

zh-tw.content:
他離開，不是把你的幸福帶走了，
是把不屬於你的那條路，還給了你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個覺得「以後不會再遇到更好的了」的朋友。把分手講成方向被修正，而不是幸福被剝奪。
variations: 有些人的離開，是在幫你把位子空出來給對的人。
這不是你失去了誰，是你終於走回自己該走的路。

en.content:
When they left, they didn't take your happiness with them.
They handed back the road that was never yours to begin with.
en.editorNote: For the friend convinced they'll 'never find anyone better.' Frames the breakup as a course correction, not a theft of happiness.
variations: Some people leave so the right one finally has a place to stand.
You didn't lose someone. You got your own path back.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'let go and embrace a better self' quotes; rewritten around the moment of noticing you no longer miss them

zh-tw.content:
你知道自己好了，
不是因為不痛了，是有一天想起他，卻忘了要難過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個問「我到底什麼時候才會走出來」的朋友。描寫釋懷不是用力忘記，而是自然而然地不再放在心上。
variations: 釋懷不是驚天動地的，是某個平常的下午，你發現自己已經不在意了。
痊癒的樣子很安靜：想起他，然後繼續過你的日子。

en.content:
You'll know you're healed —
not when it stops hurting, but the day you think of them and forget to feel sad.
en.editorNote: For the friend asking 'when will I finally be over this?' Describes moving on as something quiet that arrives on its own, not a battle you win.
variations: Getting over someone isn't dramatic. It's an ordinary afternoon when you realize you no longer care.
Healing looks quiet: you think of them, and just keep living your day.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'he left, but your worth stayed' self-worth captions; rewritten to separate a person's departure from your value

zh-tw.content:
他走了，帶走的是他自己，
不是你的價值。你還是那個完整的你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個分手後開始懷疑「是不是我不夠好」的朋友。提醒對方：離開的是人，不是你的份量。
variations: 他刪掉的是你的聯絡方式，不是你這個人的好。
會走的是他，會留下來的，是那個一直都很棒的你。

en.content:
He left, but he only took himself with him —
not your worth. You're still every bit as whole.
en.editorNote: For the friend who starts doubting 'maybe I just wasn't good enough' after a breakup. Reminds them a person walked out — not their value.
variations: He deleted your number, not the good in you.
The one who leaves is him. The one who stays is the you who was always enough.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '允許自己悲傷，然後帶著情緒繼續前進' theme; rewritten to give permission to grieve without rushing to heal

zh-tw.content:
你不用急著堅強，
難過就難過吧，眼淚流完，路還是會在那裡等你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個一直逼自己「要趕快好起來」的朋友。允許他慢慢來，不用假裝沒事。
variations: 沒有人規定失戀要幾天內振作，你可以慢慢來。
先讓自己好好哭一場，堅強這件事，明天再說。

en.content:
You don't have to rush to be strong.
Go ahead and fall apart — when the tears run out, the road will still be there waiting.
en.editorNote: For the friend forcing themselves to 'get better fast.' Gives them permission to take it slow and stop pretending they're fine.
variations: Nobody set a deadline for getting over a breakup. Take your time.
Let yourself cry it out first. Being strong can wait until tomorrow.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by empowering 'focus on what's next, not what went wrong' quotes; rewritten around stopping the replay of what went wrong

zh-tw.content:
不要再一直回放哪裡出錯了，
那場電影已經散場，你該走出戲院了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個每晚都在腦內重播分手過程、檢討「當初如果」的朋友。提醒對方：電影演完了，該起身離場。
variations: 一直倒帶只會卡住，把片子關掉，換你當自己的主角。
分手不是要你找出兇手，是要你走出那間放映廳。

en.content:
Stop replaying where it all went wrong.
The movie's over — it's time to walk out of the theater.
en.editorNote: For the friend who reruns the breakup every night, endlessly auditing the 'what ifs.' Reminds them the film has ended and it's time to leave their seat.
variations: Rewinding just keeps you stuck. Turn it off and be the lead in your own story.
A breakup isn't a case to solve. It's a room to walk out of.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'learning to love yourself again' post-breakup themes; rewritten around rediscovering the person you dropped while loving someone else

zh-tw.content:
分手之後最好的事，
是你終於有空，把那個為愛弄丟的自己撿回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個在感情裡把自己活成配角的朋友。分手不只是失去，也是重新找回自己的機會。
variations: 你不是被分手，是被還回了自由。
以前的時間都給了他，現在，該全部拿回來給自己。

en.content:
The best thing about a breakup:
you finally have time to pick back up the you that you dropped for love.
en.editorNote: For the friend who turned themselves into a supporting character in the relationship. A breakup isn't only a loss — it's a chance to find yourself again.
variations: You didn't get dumped. You got handed back your freedom.
You gave all your hours to them. Now take every one of them back for yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'this isn't serving me, walk away in peace' empowerment theme; rewritten around the quiet, undramatic version of walking away

zh-tw.content:
離開一段不再滋養你的關係，
不需要一場大吵，只需要一句「這樣的我，不快樂了」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個總覺得「一定要撕破臉才能走」的朋友。提醒對方：轉身可以很安靜，不欠誰一場戲。
variations: 有些告別不用大聲，你只是輕輕地，把自己帶走。
不是每段結束都要有兇手，有時候只是你終於捨得對自己好。

en.content:
Leaving something that no longer feeds you
doesn't need a big fight — just a quiet 'this version of me isn't happy anymore.'
en.editorNote: For the friend who thinks they need to burn it all down to be allowed to leave. Walking away can be quiet — you don't owe anyone a scene.
variations: Some goodbyes aren't loud. You just gently carry yourself out.
Not every ending needs a villain. Sometimes you just finally chose to be kind to yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'moving on, one step at a time' daily-motivation framing; rewritten around permission to heal slowly rather than on schedule

zh-tw.content:
沒有人規定失戀要幾天才能好，
你可以慢慢走，只要方向是往前的就好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個急著問「我怎麼還沒走出來」的朋友。療傷不是比賽，慢一點不代表輸。
variations: 有些人三天就笑了，有些人三個月才敢哭，兩種都算勇敢。
進度條卡住不是壞掉，只是你這次選擇認真地痛一次。

en.content:
Nobody set a deadline for getting over someone.
You're allowed to go slow — as long as you're still facing forward.
en.editorNote: For the friend anxiously asking 'why am I not over it yet?' Healing isn't a race, and going slow doesn't mean losing.
variations: Some laugh in three days, some don't dare cry for three months. Both count as brave.
A stuck progress bar isn't broken. You just chose to feel this one all the way through.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 「有些人來過你的世界，只是為了教會你如何告別」theme; rewritten to reframe the ex as a lesson rather than a loss

zh-tw.content:
有些人不是來陪你走一輩子的，
是來教你，原來你一個人也能把日子過好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個把整段感情都當成浪費的朋友。就算結束了，那段路也讓你長出了現在的自己。
variations: 他不是你的遺憾，是你這一課的老師，下課了而已。
謝謝那個離開的人，讓你發現你不需要靠誰才完整。

en.content:
Some people aren't here to stay for life.
They're here to teach you that you can build a good life on your own.
en.editorNote: For the friend who writes off the whole relationship as wasted time. Even ended, that road grew the person you are now.
variations: They're not your regret. They're the teacher for this lesson — and class is just over.
Thank the one who left. They showed you that you were never incomplete without them.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from the common 'healing is not linear' theme; rewritten to give permission for setbacks rather than restate the cliché

zh-tw.content:
療傷不是一條直線，
今天想他不代表你退步了，只代表你曾經很認真地愛過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個因為又哭了一場、覺得自己好不起來而自責的人。給他一個可以慢慢來的空間。
variations: 允許自己偶爾倒退幾步，那不是失敗，是傷口在提醒你它還在。
好起來沒有時間表，你不用趕在誰面前假裝已經沒事了。

en.content:
Healing isn't a straight line.
Missing them today doesn't mean you've backslid — it means you loved for real.
en.editorNote: For the friend beating themselves up for crying again and feeling like they'll never get over it. Give them room to take it slow.
variations: Let yourself have the bad days. That's not failure — it's the wound reminding you it's still there.
There's no deadline on getting better. You don't owe anyone a performance of being fine.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'you don't need an apology to begin healing' theme; rewritten to focus on reclaiming closure for yourself

zh-tw.content:
你不用等他的一句對不起，才准自己開始好起來。
那個句號，你自己畫就可以了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個一直在等對方道歉、卡在原地走不出來的人。把主導權拿回自己手上。
variations: 有些道歉一輩子等不到，但你的日子不能一直卡在等待鍵上。
他欠你的那句話，就當作壞帳吧，別再拿你的人生去追討。

en.content:
You don't need their apology to start healing.
That period at the end of the sentence — you're allowed to write it yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck waiting on an apology that keeps them frozen in place. Hand them back the pen.
variations: Some apologies never come. Your life can't stay parked on the waiting screen.
Write off the words they owe you as a bad debt. Stop spending your future trying to collect.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from 'let go of the life you planned' theme; rewritten toward curiosity about the unplanned future

zh-tw.content:
你以為失去的是計畫好的未來，
其實你只是空出了位置，給那個還沒登場的人生。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個把兩人的規劃都想像好、卻突然要全部歸零的人。空下來，才有得填。
variations: 原本以為的終點被劃掉了，但那只是換一條你還沒走過的路。
不是計畫泡湯了，是命運在幫你騰出手，接下來要發生的事。

en.content:
You think you lost the future you'd planned.
Really, you just cleared a seat for the life that hasn't shown up yet.
en.editorNote: For the friend who'd mapped out the whole two-person future and now has to zero it all out. Empty space is where new things get to land.
variations: The ending you'd penciled in got crossed out — but that just swapped you onto a road you've never walked.
The plan didn't fall through. Fate freed up your hands for whatever's coming next.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'never run back to what broke you' theme; reframed as a promise to yourself rather than a warning

zh-tw.content:
會讓你受傷的地方，不叫家。
就算再想念，也不要拿自己去換一個回不去的溫暖。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個深夜又想傳訊息給前任、快要走回頭路的朋友。想念是真的，但值不值得也是真的。
variations: 回頭沒有比較不痛，只是把同一種痛再重新收一次。
你已經爬出來了，別為了一點餘溫又跳回那口井裡。

en.content:
A place that hurts you doesn't get to be called home.
No matter how much you miss it, don't trade yourself for warmth you can't go back to.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's up at 2am about to text the ex and walk back into it. The missing is real — so is whether it's worth it.
variations: Going back doesn't hurt less. It just makes you feel the same pain a second time.
You already climbed out. Don't dive back down the well for a little leftover heat.

items.sourceNote: Reworked from 'you never realize how strong you are until being strong is your only option'; softened toward self-recognition

zh-tw.content:
你不是突然變堅強的，
只是終於發現，原來一個人也撐得住整片天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個以為離開對方就活不下去、結果默默把日子過起來的朋友。堅強一直都在，只是現在你看見了。
variations: 你以為的極限，其實只是還沒被逼到的起點。
撐過來的人不是不痛，是痛著也把自己接住了。

en.content:
You didn't suddenly get strong.
You just finally noticed you could hold up the whole sky on your own.
en.editorNote: For the friend who thought they couldn't survive the leaving, then quietly built a life anyway. The strength was always there — now you can see it.
variations: What you called your limit was just a starting line you hadn't been pushed to yet.
The ones who make it through aren't pain-free. They just caught themselves while it hurt.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '51 percent happy, molecule by molecule' idea; rewritten around gradual, unnoticed recovery

zh-tw.content:
好起來不會有一個明確的那天，
只是某個早上你醒來，發現自己已經很久沒想到他了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個急著想「趕快好」、覺得自己怎麼還沒放下的朋友。療傷沒有截止日，它是悄悄發生的。
variations: 你不會聽到痊癒的那一聲，它是趁你沒注意的時候慢慢長回來的。
別逼自己今天就沒事，你只要比昨天多好一點點就夠了。

en.content:
Getting better won't come with a clear date.
One morning you'll just wake up and realize you haven't thought about them in a while.
en.editorNote: For the friend rushing to 'be over it' and beating themselves up for not being there yet. Healing has no deadline — it happens quietly.
variations: You won't hear the moment you heal. It grows back while you're not looking.
Don't force yourself okay by today. A little better than yesterday is already enough.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from 'your worth isn't defined by someone else's inability to see it'; sharpened into a plain-spoken reminder

zh-tw.content:
他看不見你的好，不代表你沒有那個好。
是他的眼睛壞了，不是你的價值掉了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個被分手後開始懷疑自己是不是不夠好的朋友。不被珍惜，跟不值得被珍惜，是兩件事。
variations: 不是你不夠好，是你放錯了會欣賞你的人面前。
一個人不懂你的價值，頂多證明他不是收藏家，不是你不是寶。

en.content:
Them not seeing your worth doesn't mean the worth isn't there.
Their eyes broke — your value didn't drop.
en.editorNote: For the friend who started doubting they were 'good enough' after the split. Not being cherished and not being worth cherishing are two completely different things.
variations: You weren't not enough. You were just standing in front of the wrong person to notice.
One person missing your value only proves they're no collector — not that you're not the treasure.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from 'a doorway cracks open to new beginnings'; rewritten around the relief of getting your own life back

zh-tw.content:
分手那天你以為關上的是一扇門，
後來才知道，那是你把整間房子還給了自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個一開始只覺得失去、還沒發現自己其實變自由的朋友。空出來的不只是位置，是整個生活。
variations: 你以為丟掉了一段感情，其實是撿回了一整個自己。
門關上的聲音很大，但你之後有多安靜、多自在，只有你自己知道。

en.content:
The day you broke up, you thought a door had closed.
Later you realized — you'd just handed the whole house back to yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend still stuck on the loss, who hasn't noticed how free they've quietly become. What opened up wasn't just a spot — it was a whole life.
variations: You thought you lost a relationship. You actually got a whole self back.
The door slammed loud. But how quiet and easy it got afterward — only you know that.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from 'closure is not a conversation, it's a decision you make within yourself'; rewritten to stop the reader from waiting on the ex for permission to heal

zh-tw.content:
你一直在等的那個「交代」，不會有人給你。
真正的句點，是你自己蹲下來，親手畫上去的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個還在等前任一句「對不起」或「其實我也很痛苦」的朋友。等別人給你結局，只會讓你卡在原地更久。
variations: 沒有誰欠你一個解釋，能結束這一切的，從頭到尾只有你。
與其等他開口說清楚，不如自己決定：這件事，到今天為止。

en.content:
That closure you keep waiting for — no one is going to hand it to you.
The real period at the end is one you crouch down and draw yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend still waiting on their ex for a 'sorry' or an 'honestly, I was hurting too.' Waiting on someone else to end it just keeps you stuck longer.
variations: Nobody owes you an explanation. The only one who can close this is you.
Instead of waiting for them to spell it out, just decide: this ends today.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the no-contact rule; recast as the reader buying back their own mental quiet rather than punishing the ex

zh-tw.content:
不聯絡他，不是為了讓他難受，
是為了讓你的腦子，終於有一天不用一睜眼就想到他。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個把「已讀不回」當成報復手段的朋友。斷聯的重點從來不是他，是你把自己的心思拿回來。
variations: 封鎖不是狠，是你太累了，累到只想安靜地好起來。
不聯絡的那段日子最難，但那也是你唯一開始想別的事情的日子。

en.content:
Going no-contact isn't about making them suffer.
It's about your brain finally getting a morning where they aren't the first thought.
en.editorNote: For the friend treating 'leaving them on read' as revenge. No-contact was never about them — it's about taking your own headspace back.
variations: Blocking them isn't cruelty. You're just tired — tired enough to only want to heal in peace.
The no-contact stretch is the hardest. It's also the only stretch where you finally start thinking about something else.

items.sourceNote: Reworked from 'forgiveness is something we do for ourselves to move on'; sharpened so forgiveness reads as self-release, not absolving the ex

zh-tw.content:
原諒他，不是說他做的都對，
是你不想再把那份怨，繼續背在自己肩上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個嘴上說放下、心裡卻還在生氣的朋友。原諒是放過自己，不是替對方脫罪。
variations: 放下恨意不是原諒他，是你懶得再讓他佔用你的情緒。
你可以永遠不再喜歡他，但沒必要一直帶著那口氣過日子。

en.content:
Forgiving them doesn't mean what they did was okay.
It means you're done carrying the resentment on your own back.
en.editorNote: For the friend who says they've moved on but is still quietly furious. Forgiveness is letting yourself off the hook, not letting them off it.
variations: Dropping the grudge isn't for them. You're just tired of them renting space in your head.
You can dislike them forever. You don't have to live with clenched teeth forever.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from 'you teach people how to treat you by deciding what you will and won't accept'; recast as a post-breakup boundary lesson

zh-tw.content:
這段感情最貴的一課：
你怎麼容忍別人對你，別人就會怎麼繼續對你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個反覆原諒、結果一再被辜負的朋友。分手最實用的收穫，是學會下次哪些事一次都不能接受。
variations: 你願意退到哪，對方就會踩到哪。這次痛過，下次記得別再退。
不是他變本加厲，是你每次都說「算了」，等於告訴他可以。

en.content:
The most expensive lesson from this relationship:
however much you tolerate is exactly how much they'll keep doing.
en.editorNote: For the friend who kept forgiving and kept getting let down. The most useful thing a breakup leaves you is a clear list of what you won't accept even once next time.
variations: However far you're willing to back up is exactly how far they'll push. This time it hurt — next time, don't back up.
They didn't get worse. Every time you said 'never mind,' you told them it was fine.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'you are whole, not half' self-worth theme; rewritten with an original 半個人/一整個人 framing

zh-tw.content:
他離開的時候，你以為自己少了一半。
其實你從來都是一整個人，只是借了他一雙眼睛，才看不見。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個覺得「沒有他我就不完整」的朋友。分手拿走的是一個人，不是你的一半。
variations: 你不是他的另一半，你是你自己的一整個。
感情裡最傷的錯覺，是把「兩個人」算成「半個加半個」。

en.content:
When they left, you thought you'd lost half of yourself.
You were always whole — you'd just borrowed their eyes and forgot how to see it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels 'incomplete without them.' A breakup takes a person away — not half of you.
variations: You were never their other half. You're your own whole.
The cruelest illusion in love is doing the math as 'half plus half' instead of 'two whole people.'

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'moving on is remembering without feeling awful'; reworded with an original 不痛/沒表情 contrast

zh-tw.content:
走出來不是有一天你忘了他，
是有一天你想起他，臉上沒有表情，心裡也沒有起伏。
zh-tw.editorNote: 很多人以為釋懷是忘記，其實是「想起時無感」。傳給還在等自己忘記的朋友——你不用忘，只要不痛就好。
variations: 痊癒的標準不是不再想起，是想起的時候，連嘆氣都省了。
你不會忘記他，你只會有一天，發現這件事一點都不重要了。

en.content:
Moving on isn't the day you forget them.
It's the day you remember them and your face does nothing, and your chest stays still.
en.editorNote: People think healing means forgetting — really it's 'remembering without a flinch.' For the friend still waiting to forget: you don't have to forget, just stop hurting.
variations: You'll know you're healed not when you stop remembering, but when remembering doesn't even cost you a sigh.
You won't forget them. You'll just wake up one day and realize it doesn't matter anymore.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '妳成全的是後來更好的自己'; rewritten to reframe 成全 as an investment in the future self

zh-tw.content:
你以為你在成全他，
其實你成全的，是三個月後那個睡得著、笑得出來的自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 分手當下總覺得是為對方犧牲，回頭看才知道，你真正救的是未來的自己。適合傳給剛做完那個艱難決定的朋友。
variations: 你放的不是手，是一個更值得的未來的門票。
當下像是輸了，其實你只是提早幫未來的自己止血。

en.content:
You thought you were letting them win.
Really, you were setting free the version of you who — three months from now — sleeps through the night and laughs out loud.
en.editorNote: In the moment a breakup feels like a sacrifice for them. Looking back, you saved your future self. For the friend who just made the hard call.
variations: You didn't let go of a person. You let go of the thing standing between you and a better future.
It felt like losing. You were just stopping the bleeding early for future-you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'a doorway cracks open to new beginnings'; original 一扇門關上/沒開燈 metaphor added

zh-tw.content:
一扇門關上的時候，別急著在門口哭。
哭到天亮你會發現，屋子裡其實還有好幾扇你從沒開過燈的門。
zh-tw.editorNote: 剛分手時眼裡只有那扇關上的門。提醒朋友：你的人生從來不是只有一個出口。
variations: 他把門關上，不是要把你關起來，是逼你去找另一扇。
同一扇門守太久，會忘記整棟房子都是你的。

en.content:
When a door closes, don't sit crying in the doorway.
Cry till morning and you'll notice — the house is full of doors you never even turned the lights on for.
en.editorNote: Right after a breakup you only see the door that shut. Remind your friend: your life was never a single exit.
variations: They didn't close the door to trap you. They closed it so you'd go find another.
Guard one door too long and you forget the whole house is yours.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the comeback is stronger than the setback'; reworded with a self-deprecating Taiwanese 谷底/彈起來 tone

zh-tw.content:
現在跌到谷底也好，
至少接下來每一步，都是往上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 帶一點黑色幽默的自我打氣。適合傳給覺得自己「已經爛到不能再爛」的朋友——這其實是好消息。
variations: 谷底最大的好處，就是它沒有樓下了。
現在的你是最低點，恭喜，接下來的版本都是升級。

en.content:
Hitting rock bottom isn't the worst news.
It just means every step from here is up.
en.editorNote: Self-pep-talk with a dash of dark humor. For the friend convinced they've 'hit the lowest possible low' — that's actually good news.
variations: The best thing about rock bottom: there's no floor below it.
This is your lowest version. Congrats — everything that ships from here is an upgrade.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I didn't lose — I outgrew'; reframed to soften the boast into a gentler self-observation

zh-tw.content:
這段感情不是我輸了，
是我長大了，而他還停在原地。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給覺得「分手就是自己失敗」的朋友。把「失去」翻成「長大」，同一件事，心情差很多。
variations: 不是他不要我，是我已經不需要那個版本的自己了。
你沒有失去他，你只是走得比他遠了一點。

en.content:
I didn't lose this one.
I grew — and they stayed exactly where I left them.
en.editorNote: For the friend who reads a breakup as personal failure. Swap 'lost' for 'outgrew' — same event, completely different mood.
variations: They didn't stop wanting me. I stopped needing that version of myself.
You didn't lose them. You just walked a little further than they could.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the modern 追蹤/limited-story ritual of post-breakup social media; common theme across 2026 moving-on listicles

zh-tw.content:
我沒有封鎖他，
只是把他從限動名單裡刪掉，順便把自己救回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 數位時代的放下，是從整理追蹤名單開始。傳給那個每天偷看前任限動、看完又難過的朋友。
variations: 真正的放下，是連他發了新動態你都懶得點進去。
不用大張旗鼓封鎖，靜靜取消追蹤，比較有大人的樣子。

en.content:
I didn't block them.
I just took them off my close-friends list and quietly took myself back.
en.editorNote: Digital-age closure starts with cleaning up who you follow. Send this to the friend who checks their ex's stories daily and feels worse every time.
variations: You've really moved on when they post something new and you can't be bothered to tap in.
No dramatic block needed. A quiet unfollow just looks more grown-up.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'choose yourself every day' / 'I loved you, then I let you go, now I love me'; rewritten into a daily-habit framing

zh-tw.content:
以前每天想的是他今天有沒有想我，
現在每天想的是我今天有沒有對自己好一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把注意力從「他」搬回「自己」的具體練習。適合當作每天早上給自己的一句提醒。
variations: 從今天開始，把留給他的那份在意，分一點給自己。
曾經把最好的都給了他，現在輪到自己排隊了。

en.content:
I used to spend my days wondering if they were thinking of me.
Now I spend them checking whether I've been kind to myself.
en.editorNote: A concrete exercise in moving your attention off 'them' and back onto you. Works as a morning reminder to yourself.
variations: Starting today, take the energy you saved for them and hand a little to yourself.
You gave them your best for years. It's finally your turn in line.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'This isn't serving me, and I walk away in peace'; reworded into plain Taiwanese self-talk without the wellness jargon

zh-tw.content:
「這段關係讓我變得不像我自己。」
說得出這句話，就已經走了一大半。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給還在猶豫該不該離開的朋友。能承認關係不對勁，是放下的第一步，不用等到完全不痛。
variations: 不是他做錯了什麼，是這段關係已經不適合現在的我。
願意轉身，不代表不愛過，只是更愛現在的自己。

en.content:
"This relationship was turning me into someone I don't recognize."
Once you can say that out loud, you're already halfway out.
en.editorNote: For the friend still deciding whether to leave. Admitting the relationship isn't right is the first step — you don't have to wait until it stops hurting.
variations: It's not that they did something wrong. It's that this no longer fits who I am now.
Turning to leave doesn't erase the love. It just means you love who you're becoming more.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I lost you, but I found my worth'; expanded into a before/after contrast with a warmer landing

zh-tw.content:
我是弄丟了他沒錯，
可是在找他的路上，我把很久以前弄丟的自己撿回來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把失戀寫成一場「找回自己」的過程。適合已經走到後期、開始能笑著回頭看的朋友。
variations: 失去一個人，換回一整個自己，這筆帳其實不虧。
他離開之後空出來的位子，剛好夠我把自己放回去。

en.content:
Yeah, I lost them.
But somewhere on the way to looking for them, I found the me I'd misplaced years ago.
en.editorNote: Reframes a breakup as a 'finding yourself' journey. Best for the friend who's far enough along to look back and smile.
variations: Lost one person, got a whole self back. Honestly, not a bad trade.
The space they left behind was just big enough to fit myself back into.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'healing isn't linear' theme; rewritten to normalize relapse days instead of demanding steady progress

zh-tw.content:
復原不是一直往前走的直線。
有天你以為好了，隔天又哭到不行，這都算數，你沒有退步。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「明明上禮拜還好好的，今天又崩潰」而自責的朋友。療癒本來就會反覆，不是進度倒退。
variations: 好起來不是關燈那一下，是燈忽明忽暗，但總體越來越亮。
今天又想他了也沒關係，難過不是打回原形，是你還在認真復原的證據。

en.content:
Healing isn't a straight line forward.
Some days you think you're fine, the next you're crying again — that still counts. You didn't relapse.
en.editorNote: For the friend beating themselves up because they were 'fine last week' and fell apart today. Healing loops back on itself. That's not going backwards.
variations: Getting better isn't a light switch. It's a bulb that flickers, but overall gets brighter.
Missing them again today is okay. A bad day isn't a reset — it's proof you're still doing the work.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you don't need closure to move forward'; reframed so closure is something you give yourself rather than wait to receive

zh-tw.content:
你一直在等他給你一個交代，
但其實那個句點，從頭到尾都握在你自己手上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合還在等前任「解釋清楚」才肯放手的朋友。有些人不會回來把話說完，句點得自己蓋下去。
variations: 不是每段感情都有結局的說明書，有時候結束就是結束。
別再等他親口說再見了，那句再見，你早就可以替自己說。

en.content:
You keep waiting for them to give you an explanation.
But that final period? It's been in your own hand the whole time.
en.editorNote: For the friend who won't let go until the ex 'explains everything.' Some people never come back to finish the sentence — you have to put the period down yourself.
variations: Not every relationship comes with an instruction manual for the ending. Sometimes over is just over.
Stop waiting for them to say goodbye out loud. You've been able to say it for yourself this whole time.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'some people come into your world just to teach you how to say goodbye'; rewritten with a gentler, less bitter landing

zh-tw.content:
有些人走進你的生命，不是為了陪你到最後，
是為了教會你，原來你一個人也走得下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把前任重新定位成「路過的老師」而不是「失去的歸宿」。適合已經開始能平靜回看那段關係的朋友。
variations: 他不是你的終點，只是提醒你路還很長的一個路標。
謝謝那個沒留下來的人，是他讓我發現，我沒有他也活得好好的。

en.content:
Some people walk into your life not to stay till the end,
but to teach you that you can keep walking on your own.
en.editorNote: Recasts the ex as a passing teacher instead of a lost home. Best for the friend who's calm enough now to look back without flinching.
variations: They weren't your destination. Just a sign reminding you the road keeps going.
Thank you to the one who didn't stay — you're the reason I found out I'm fine without you.

items.sourceNote: Original black-humor writing on the post-breakup 'deleting photos' ritual, common across Taiwan breakup listicles

zh-tw.content:
刪照片刪到一半，發現裡面我笑得比他好看。
所以我留下了照片，刪掉了他。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後整理相簿的自嘲時刻。用黑色幽默把「捨不得刪」翻轉成「其實不虧的是我」，適合已經笑得出來的階段。
variations: 本來要把合照全刪的，後來想想，好看的是我，該滾的是他。
刪了聯絡方式、刪了限動、刪了他，唯獨捨不得刪那張我瘦了五公斤的合照。

en.content:
Halfway through deleting our photos, I noticed I look better than they do in every single one.
So I kept the photos and deleted them.
en.editorNote: That self-deprecating moment of cleaning out your camera roll post-breakup. Flips 'I can't bring myself to delete these' into 'honestly, I'm the one who came out ahead.' Best once you can laugh again.
variations: Was gonna delete all the couple pics, then realized the good-looking one is me and the one who should go is them.
Deleted their number, their stories, their whole existence — except that one photo where I looked five pounds lighter.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'your worth is not negotiable'; expanded into a concrete reminder that being left doesn't lower your value

zh-tw.content:
他不要你，不代表你不值得被要，
就像有人不喜歡海，海還是海，它從來不需要靠誰喜歡才存在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把「被分手」和「自我價值」切開來。適合正在懷疑「是不是我不夠好」的朋友，提醒他：被拒絕不等於被貶值。
variations: 有人退貨不是因為東西壞了，是他根本不會用。
你的價值不是投票投出來的，少一個人喜歡，你也沒有變得比較少。

en.content:
Them not wanting you doesn't mean you're not worth wanting.
Some people don't like the ocean — the ocean stays the ocean. It never needed their approval to exist.
en.editorNote: Separates 'getting dumped' from 'your worth.' For the friend spiraling on 'maybe I just wasn't good enough.' Being turned down isn't being marked down.
variations: Someone returning the item doesn't mean it's broken. Sometimes they just never learned how to use it.
Your worth isn't decided by a vote. One less person liking you doesn't make you any less.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'your chapter ended but my story continues'; reframed around one specific person being one page, not the whole book

zh-tw.content:
他只是你故事裡的一章，不是整本書。
那章寫完了，翻頁的手還是你自己的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給覺得「人生就這樣了」的朋友。提醒他分手是結束一段，不是結束整個人生，後面還很長。
variations: 他是其中一頁，不是封底。故事還沒到最後一行。
一個人退場不代表劇終，只是換一幕。

en.content:
They were one chapter in your story, not the whole book.
That chapter's done — and the hand turning the page is still yours.
en.editorNote: For the friend convinced 'this is it, my life is over.' A breakup ends a chapter, not the book. There's a lot of pages left.
variations: They're one page, not the back cover. The story isn't on its last line.
Someone exiting isn't the finale. It's just a scene change.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you're whole even without them'; rewritten to reject the 'other half' framing directly

zh-tw.content:
你不是失去了「另一半」，
你本來就是完整的一整個，只是曾經借了一個位子給他坐。
zh-tw.editorNote: 打破「另一半」的說法。適合正在覺得自己「缺了一塊」的朋友，提醒他：你從頭到尾都是完整的。
variations: 你不是半個人在找另一半，你是一整個人，只是暫時多了個空位。
座位空了不代表你破了個洞，那本來就是你的位子。

en.content:
You didn't lose your 'other half.'
You were always whole — you just lent someone a seat for a while.
en.editorNote: Kills the 'other half' myth. For the friend who feels like a piece of them is missing. You were complete the entire time.
variations: You're not half a person hunting for the other half. You're a whole one with an open seat again.
An empty chair doesn't mean there's a hole in you. That was always your chair.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '想起你時甜甜地就好'; rewritten toward the calm-not-numb version of moving on

zh-tw.content:
有一天你會發現，想起他的時候心裡是平的，
不是恨，也不是還愛，就只是「喔，那個人啊」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 描述釋懷真正的樣子：不是討厭也不是想念，是無感。傳給以為「還會痛」才代表在乎的朋友，讓他知道平靜也是一種痊癒。
variations: 真正好了，不是想起他會笑，是想起他沒什麼感覺。
釋懷的那天沒有煙火，只有一句淡淡的：喔，是他啊。

en.content:
One day you'll think of them and feel nothing sharp —
not hate, not still-loving, just a flat little 'oh, that person.'
en.editorNote: This is what healed actually looks like: not disgust, not longing, just neutral. For the friend who thinks it only counts as caring if it still hurts. Calm is a kind of recovery too.
variations: Truly over them isn't smiling when you remember. It's remembering and feeling basically nothing.
The day you move on has no fireworks. Just a quiet 'oh, right, them.'

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you are not losing, you are freeing yourself'; rewritten around the relief that shows up after the grief

zh-tw.content:
分手不是你輸了，是你終於不用再假裝了。
難過會過去，等它過去，你會先感覺到的其實是「鬆了一口氣」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把分手從「失敗」重新定義成「解脫」。適合在硬撐一段快沒力的關係、剛結束時滿是罪惡感的朋友。
variations: 不是你不夠努力，是你終於不用再一個人努力了。
有些關係結束的第一個感覺不是心碎，是可以好好呼吸了。

en.content:
A breakup isn't you losing. It's you finally not having to pretend anymore.
The sadness passes — and once it does, the first thing you feel is relief.
en.editorNote: Reframes a breakup from 'failure' to 'release.' For the friend who white-knuckled a dying relationship and now feels guilty for feeling okay.
variations: It's not that you didn't try hard enough. It's that you finally don't have to try alone.
Some relationships end and the first feeling isn't heartbreak — it's being able to breathe.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '放下不是丟掉，是把曾經好好收進記憶裡' idea; rewritten to contrast throwing away vs. archiving the memory

zh-tw.content:
放下不是把他從記憶裡刪掉，
是把那段「曾經」好好收進抽屜，關上，然後去過今天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那個以為「忘不掉就是還沒放下」而自責的朋友。放下從來不是失憶，是不再天天打開那個抽屜。
variations: 你不用假裝沒愛過，只要願意把它收好，繼續往前走就好。
回憶可以留著，但別讓它每天都要你回去住一遍。

en.content:
Letting go isn't deleting them from your memory.
It's tucking the whole 'us' into a drawer, closing it, and going to live today.
en.editorNote: For the friend who beats themselves up thinking 'if I can't forget, I haven't moved on.' Moving on was never amnesia — it's just no longer opening that drawer every day.
variations: You don't have to pretend it never happened. You just have to put it away and keep walking.
You get to keep the memories. You just don't have to move back into them every day.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'thank you for showing me what I don't want / expensive but educational lesson' joke; rewritten with a tuition-fee framing

zh-tw.content:
謝謝你讓我知道什麼樣的人不能要，
這堂課學費有點貴，但至少我沒被當。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把爛感情重新定義成一門「昂貴的必修課」。適合已經走出來、可以拿前任開玩笑的朋友，笑著結案。
variations: 這段感情沒有白費，它教會我下次要看清楚再刷卡。
分手費雖然貴，但比起繼續在一起，這筆算便宜的。

en.content:
Thanks for teaching me exactly what I don't want in a person.
The tuition was steep, but hey — at least I passed the class.
en.editorNote: Reframes a bad relationship as an expensive required course. For the friend who's far enough out to joke about their ex and close the case with a laugh.
variations: That relationship wasn't wasted. It taught me to read the fine print before signing next time.
The breakup was pricey, sure. Still cheaper than staying.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I loved you, then I let you go, now I love me' progression; rewritten as a three-stage arc ending on self-love

zh-tw.content:
以前我把全部的愛都給了你，
後來我學會放手，現在，我終於留一份給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 三段式的心境轉變：從全給對方，到放手，到愛自己。適合分手一陣子、開始把重心拉回自己身上的朋友。
variations: 那些沒被珍惜的溫柔，我先收回來，好好對自己一次。
曾經最愛的是你，現在最需要被愛的，是我自己。

en.content:
I used to pour all my love into you.
Then I learned to let go — and now, I finally keep some for me.
en.editorNote: A three-stage shift: all-in on them, then release, then self-love. For the friend who's been broken up a while and is starting to point the care back at themselves.
variations: All that tenderness that went unappreciated? I'm taking it back and spending it on me.
You used to be the one I loved most. Now the one who needs it most is me.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '一個人只要不再想要，就什麼都可以放下'; rewritten around the moment wanting quietly stops

zh-tw.content:
放下這件事很奇怪，它不會敲鑼打鼓通知你。
有一天你只是突然發現，你已經很久沒有想他了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 釋懷往往不是某個決定，而是某天回頭才發現的事。給那個焦急問「我到底什麼時候才會好」的朋友，答案是：不知不覺。
variations: 你不會知道是哪一天放下的，你只會知道，現在的你已經放下了。
痊癒沒有儀式，它總是趁你不注意的時候悄悄完成。

en.content:
Moving on is strange — it never announces itself with a fanfare.
One day you just notice you haven't thought about them in a while.
en.editorNote: Healing is rarely a decision; it's something you catch in hindsight. For the friend anxiously asking 'when will I finally be okay?' The answer is: without even noticing.
variations: You'll never know which day you let go. You'll only know that, by now, you have.
Healing skips the ceremony. It always finishes quietly, while you weren't looking.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the savage 'I'm not single, I'm in a long-term relationship with freedom' line; rewritten with a self-partnership framing

zh-tw.content:
我不是單身，我只是跟自由穩定交往中。
而且這任對象，從來不會已讀不回。
zh-tw.editorNote: 把「單身」重新包裝成一段超穩定的關係。適合剛脫離爛感情、想用幽默對外宣告「我過得很好」的朋友。
variations: 現在跟我交往的是自己，福利很好，還不用配合誰的行程。
感情狀態：跟自由熱戀中，暫不接受面試。

en.content:
I'm not single — I'm in a very committed relationship with my freedom.
And this partner? Never leaves me on read.
en.editorNote: Repackages 'single' as an extremely stable relationship. For the friend fresh out of a bad one who wants to announce 'I'm doing great' with a wink.
variations: I'm dating myself now. Great perks, and I never have to work around anyone's schedule.
Relationship status: madly in love with my freedom, not currently accepting applications.

items.sourceNote: Reframes the common 'you were too much' put-down into a self-worth line; original phrasing built around weight/capacity metaphor

zh-tw.content:
你不是太黏、也不是要求太多，
是他扛不動你這種重量的認真。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個一直檢討自己「是不是我太麻煩」的朋友。問題從來不是你太多，是他接不住。
variations: 你不是難相處，是他還沒長到能接住你的高度。
把你嫌成負擔的人，只是證明他撐不起你的份量。

en.content:
You weren't too clingy, and you didn't ask for too much.
He just couldn't carry someone who loved that seriously.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck asking 'was I too much trouble?' You were never too much — he just couldn't hold you.
variations: You're not hard to love. He just hadn't grown tall enough to reach you.
Anyone who calls you a burden is only admitting they couldn't lift you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the Marilyn Monroe 'good things fall apart so better things can fall together' idea; rewritten with a card-shuffling metaphor

zh-tw.content:
有些關係散掉，不是你輸了，
是命運趁機幫你重新洗牌。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合安慰覺得「我努力那麼久竟然是白費」的朋友。牌散了才有機會重發，你手上的下一手還沒亮。
variations: 這局收掉，不代表你不會贏，只是換一副新牌重來。
散場不是結局，是命運把爛牌收走，準備發新的給你。

en.content:
Some things falling apart isn't you losing —
it's fate quietly reshuffling the deck for you.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels all that effort was wasted. The hand had to be cleared before a better one could be dealt.
variations: Folding this round doesn't mean you can't win — it just means a fresh deck is coming.
The end isn't a loss. It's fate sweeping away the bad cards to deal you new ones.

items.sourceNote: Reframes 'single is not a punishment' into an earned-break framing; original wording

zh-tw.content:
單身不是懲罰，是你辛苦太久，
終於放自己一個不用配合任何人的長假。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給覺得「一個人好像很失敗」的朋友。把單身重新定義成休假，不是被罰站。
variations: 現在的空窗不叫寂寞，叫終於沒人跟我搶行程。
單身是我給自己的補休，還是不扣薪的那種。

en.content:
Being single isn't a punishment.
It's the long vacation you earned after working way too hard to make it work.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels being alone equals failing. Single isn't a time-out in the corner — it's paid leave.
variations: This isn't a lonely gap. It's finally nobody fighting me over the schedule.
Single is the comp time I owed myself — the fully-paid kind.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the petty 'since we broke up my trash took itself out' humor genre; rewritten around reclaiming the bed and remote

zh-tw.content:
分手最大的好處：整張床都是我的，
遙控器也不用讓，冷氣想開幾度就幾度。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合失戀後想笑著往前走的朋友。先從搶回床的對角線和遙控器開始，療傷可以很具體。
variations: 他走了以後，我睡覺終於能大字型攤開，棉被也不會半夜被扯走。
現在的主導權：床我全睡、劇我全選、宵夜我全吃，超爽。

en.content:
Best part of the breakup: the whole bed is mine now,
I never hand over the remote, and the AC sits at exactly my temperature.
en.editorNote: For the friend ready to laugh their way forward. Healing can be very literal — start by reclaiming the diagonal of the bed and the remote.
variations: Since he left, I finally sleep sprawled like a starfish, and nobody yanks the blanket at 3am.
New rules: whole bed is mine, I pick every show, and the late-night snacks are all mine too.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the 'you miss the imagined future, not the actual person' insight common in breakup-recovery content

zh-tw.content:
你想念的其實不是他，
是那個你以為會一直在的未來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜特別想念的朋友。搞清楚自己在想念什麼，往往就沒那麼想聯絡了——你捨不得的是計畫，不是那個人。
variations: 讓你難過的不是失去他，是失去那個有他的明天。
你放不下的是那張還沒實現的藍圖，不是畫藍圖的那個人。

en.content:
What you miss isn't really him —
it's the future you were so sure would always be there.
en.editorNote: For the friend who aches most at midnight. Once you name what you're actually missing, the urge to text fades — you miss the plan, not the person.
variations: It's not losing him that hurts. It's losing the tomorrow that had him in it.
You're not holding onto the person — you're holding onto a blueprint that never got built.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'your worth is not negotiable / rejection isn't a verdict' self-worth theme; rewritten around 'he didn't have the eyes to see it'

zh-tw.content:
他不選你，不代表你不夠好，
只代表他沒那個眼光配你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被分手後開始懷疑自己的朋友。被拒絕不等於被否定——是他不懂欣賞，不是你不值得。
variations: 你的價值不用等誰蓋章認證，他看不見是他的損失。
不是你不夠好，是你太好，好到他接不住。

en.content:
Him not choosing you doesn't mean you're not enough.
It just means he didn't have the eyes to see it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who started doubting themselves after being dumped. Rejection isn't a verdict on your worth — he just couldn't appreciate it.
variations: Your worth doesn't need anyone's stamp of approval. If he couldn't see it, that's his loss.
It's not that you weren't enough. You were so much he couldn't hold it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing is slowly falling back in love with yourself' recovery theme; rewritten to contrast with deleting the memory

zh-tw.content:
療傷不是把他從記憶裡刪掉，
是慢慢地，重新喜歡上那個一個人的自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得「我永遠好不起來」的朋友。復原不是遺忘，是把重心一點一點搬回自己身上。
variations: 好起來不是有一天突然不痛了，是你開始把時間花在自己身上。
真正的復原，是某天你發現：沒有他，日子也過得挺好。

en.content:
Healing isn't deleting him from your memory.
It's slowly, gently falling back in love with the you that's on your own.
en.editorNote: For the friend convinced they'll never be okay. Recovery isn't forgetting — it's moving the center of gravity back to yourself, one day at a time.
variations: Getting better isn't waking up one day pain-free. It's starting to spend your time on you.
Real recovery is the day you notice: life's actually pretty good without him.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by '放不下的其實是曾經的自己' theme; rewritten to frame it as missing the version of you that dared to love hard

zh-tw.content:
你放不下的其實不是他，
是那個曾經很敢愛的自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後覺得「再也不會這樣愛人了」的朋友。你懷念的是還會全心投入的自己，那份能力沒有消失，只是暫時收起來了。
variations: 讓你捨不得的，是那段時光裡毫無保留的你。
你想念的不是那個人，是遇見他之前那個完整的自己。

en.content:
What you can't let go of isn't him —
it's the version of you that once dared to love that hard.
en.editorNote: For the friend who swears they'll never love like that again. You miss the you who gave everything — that ability didn't vanish, it's just packed away for now.
variations: What you're grieving is the wholehearted you from back then.
You don't miss the person. You miss the whole self you were before you met him.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'holding on is believing there's a past, letting go is knowing there's a future'; rewritten and expanded with the open-hands image

zh-tw.content:
抓著不放，是相信一切都停在過去；
願意放手，是知道前面還有明天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合卡在「捨不得又回不去」的朋友。放手不是認輸，是把手空出來，接住還沒發生的好事。
variations: 緊握代表你以為只剩回憶，鬆手代表你相信還有未來。
放下不是失去，是騰出位子給更適合的人生。

en.content:
Holding on means believing everything stopped in the past.
Letting go means knowing there's still a tomorrow.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck between 'can't let go' and 'can't go back.' Letting go isn't surrender — it's freeing your hands to catch the good that hasn't happened yet.
variations: A tight grip says all you have is memories. An open hand says the future's still coming.
Letting go isn't losing. It's clearing space for a life that fits better.

items.sourceNote: Original petty-humor writing on 'reclaiming the beauty/energy you wasted on him' post-breakup glow-up genre

zh-tw.content:
分手後我沒有變憔悴，
我只是把之前浪費在他身上的美貌，收回來自己用。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合想笑著翻篇的朋友。療傷可以很膚淺也很療癒——把注意力和保養品，通通還給自己。
variations: 以前照鏡子想的是他喜不喜歡，現在只想著我喜不喜歡，超省心。
他走了以後我氣色更好，看來我一直過敏的不是花粉，是他。

en.content:
I didn't fall apart after the breakup.
I just took back all the good looks I'd been wasting on him.
en.editorNote: For the friend ready to laugh and move on. Healing can be shallow and effective — redirect your attention (and your skincare) back to yourself.
variations: I used to check the mirror wondering if he'd like it. Now I only ask if I do. So much easier.
My skin cleared up right after he left. Turns out I wasn't allergic to pollen — I was allergic to him.

items.sourceNote: Original rewrite of the 'you said I'd never find anyone better — plot twist, I found myself' empowerment genre

zh-tw.content:
你說我再也找不到比你更好的人。
結果我找到了，那個人是我自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛被「你會後悔」情緒勒索的朋友。分手最好的反擊不是找下一個，是先把自己找回來。
variations: 他離開的時候帶走了很多東西，唯獨忘了帶走我對自己的信心。
我沒有降級去愛別人，我升級成先愛自己。

en.content:
You said I'd never find anyone better than you.
Plot twist: I found someone. It was me.
en.editorNote: For the friend who just got hit with a 'you'll regret this.' The best comeback after a breakup isn't finding the next person — it's finding yourself first.
variations: When he left he took a lot with him. He just forgot to take my faith in myself.
I didn't downgrade to loving someone else. I upgraded to loving me first.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'some endings are protection / release what no longer chooses you'; rewritten with the door metaphor

zh-tw.content:
有些結束不是懲罰，是保護。
那扇關上的門，其實是替你擋掉一段不適合的未來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合還在把分手當成「失敗」的朋友。不是每段感情都要走到最後才算數，及時停損也是一種溫柔。
variations: 他選擇離開的那一刻，也幫你省下了繼續耗下去的好幾年。
關上的門後面不是空的，是還沒輪到你看見的風景。

en.content:
Some endings aren't punishment. They're protection.
That door that closed was blocking a future that didn't fit you.
en.editorNote: For the friend still filing the breakup under 'failure.' Not every relationship has to reach the finish line to have mattered — cutting your losses in time is its own kind of kindness.
variations: The moment he chose to leave, he also saved you years you'd have spent running on empty.
Behind the closed door isn't nothing. It's a view it wasn't your turn to see yet.

items.sourceNote: Original petty-humor rewrite of the 'I replaced you with therapy / therapy is winning' post-breakup upgrade joke

zh-tw.content:
分手後我把你的位子空出來，
給了睡眠、朋友和一台掃地機器人，目前運作良好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合想用幽默翻篇的朋友。把注意力還給那些真正讓生活變好的東西，比挽回一段消耗你的關係實在多了。
variations: 他的位子我沒有再找人補，改放我的手機充電器，至少它每天都在。
以前那個位子放的是他，現在放的是我的好心情，換得超值。

en.content:
After we broke up I cleared out your spot
and gave it to sleep, my friends, and a robot vacuum. Running great so far.
en.editorNote: For the friend who wants to move on with a laugh. Handing your attention back to the things that actually improve your life beats winning back a relationship that drained you.
variations: I didn't fill his spot with someone new. I put my phone charger there. At least it shows up every day.
That spot used to hold him. Now it holds my good mood. Great trade.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you can love and still walk away' theme; rewritten to separate love from staying

zh-tw.content:
你可以還愛著他，同時選擇離開。
愛一個人，從來不代表你必須留下來被消耗。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合卡在「還有感情，是不是就該撐下去」的朋友。愛和留下是兩件事，離開不等於不曾愛過。
variations: 不是不愛了才走，是太愛自己了才走。
有些人你會一直記得，但記得不代表要一直等他。

en.content:
You can still love him and choose to leave.
Loving someone was never a contract to stay and be drained.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck on 'there's still feelings, so shouldn't I tough it out?' Love and staying are two different things — walking away doesn't erase that you loved.
variations: I didn't leave because the love ran out. I left because I finally loved myself too.
Some people you'll always remember. Remembering them doesn't mean waiting for them.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the post-breakup 'don't let it break you, let it build you' growth genre with a rebuilt-house image

zh-tw.content:
這場分手沒有把你打碎，
只是把你拆開，讓你重新蓋一個更堅固、也更像自己的家。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合走到療傷後半段、開始重建的朋友。心碎不是終點，是重新設計人生格局的機會。
variations: 被拆掉的不是你，是那個為了配合他而委屈的自己。
廢墟上長出來的，往往比原本的更耐風雨。

en.content:
This breakup didn't break you.
It just took you apart so you could rebuild something sturdier — and more like yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend in the back half of healing, starting to rebuild. Heartbreak isn't the end — it's a chance to redraw the floor plan of your life.
variations: What got torn down wasn't you. It was the version of you that kept shrinking to fit him.
What grows back on the rubble usually weathers the storms better than the original.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'moving on is remembering without feeling awful' genre; reframed around a scar that stops hurting rather than forgetting

zh-tw.content:
走出來不是把他忘記，
是有一天想起他，就像摸到一道舊疤——知道它在，但已經不痛了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個以為「還沒忘記就是還沒好」的朋友。忘記不是目標，不痛才是。
variations: 你不用逼自己忘記，你只要等到想起的時候，心跳不再亂掉。
傷口結痂不代表沒受過傷，只代表你活下來了。

en.content:
Moving on isn't forgetting them.
It's the day you think of them and it feels like an old scar — you know it's there, but it doesn't hurt anymore.
en.editorNote: For the friend who thinks 'if I still remember, I'm not over it.' Forgetting was never the goal — not hurting is.
variations: You don't have to force yourself to forget. Just wait for the day their name doesn't skip your heartbeat.
A healed wound doesn't mean it never hurt. It means you survived it.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'you are worthy of the love you give others' self-love theme; sharpened into a mirror image

zh-tw.content:
你把整顆心掏給他的那段日子，
記得留一點給那個，一直在旁邊等你回來愛的自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀後最容易忘記的人，其實是自己。適合傳給那個對別人很好、對自己很壞的朋友。
variations: 你值得的，是你曾經給別人的那種愛——只是這次，收件人是你。
先學會愛自己，下一個人才知道，你不是隨便就能將就的。

en.content:
All those days you handed him your whole heart —
remember to save a little for the you who's been waiting on the side for you to love them back.
en.editorNote: After a breakup, the person you forget first is usually yourself. For the friend who's kind to everyone but cruel to themselves.
variations: You deserve the kind of love you gave away — only this time, the recipient is you.
Learn to love yourself first, so the next person knows you were never someone to settle for.

items.sourceNote: Original self-deprecating humor riffing on the 'best revenge is moving on' cliché; flipped into a petty-but-honest joke

zh-tw.content:
他們說最好的報復是過得比他好。
所以我今天多睡了兩小時、吃了三塊雞排——復仇進度超前，謝謝關心。
zh-tw.editorNote: 誰說療傷一定要很勵志。傳給那個嘴上說要振作、身體很誠實地躺平的朋友。
variations: 我的復仇計畫很宏大，第一步：把他的名字從最近聯絡人滑掉。第二步：睡覺。
過得比他好太累了，我決定先過得比昨天的自己好一點就好。

en.content:
They say the best revenge is living better than your ex.
So today I slept two extra hours and ate three fried chickens — revenge is ahead of schedule, thanks for asking.
en.editorNote: Who said healing has to be inspirational. For the friend who swears they're bouncing back while very honestly lying face-down on the couch.
variations: My revenge plan is ambitious. Step one: swipe his name out of recent contacts. Step two: nap.
Living better than him sounds exhausting. I'll settle for living slightly better than yesterday's me.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'let yourself grieve first' theme in Taiwan breakup listicles; added permission-to-feel framing

zh-tw.content:
不用急著堅強，
難過是身體在幫你，把那個人一點一點搬出去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個一直說「我沒事」但眼睛很紅的朋友。允許自己難過，也是療傷的一部分。
variations: 眼淚不是脆弱，是你在清理那個住太久的房客。
你不是還沒好，你只是還在好起來的路上，這很正常。

en.content:
Don't rush to be strong.
The sadness is your body doing the work — carrying that person out of you, one piece at a time.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps saying 'I'm fine' with red eyes. Letting yourself grieve is part of healing, not a detour from it.
variations: Tears aren't weakness. They're you evicting a tenant who overstayed.
You're not un-healed. You're just still on the way there — and that's completely normal.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'every broken heart cracks open a doorway to new beginnings' theme; recast as a door he was blocking

zh-tw.content:
他離開的時候，順手把一扇門帶上了。
過陣子你才發現，那扇門後面，一直擋著另外三扇更漂亮的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合走到療傷後段、開始好奇「接下來呢」的朋友。有時候一段關係結束，只是為了幫你把視野讓出來。
variations: 他關上的那扇門，其實一直卡著你看不到後面的風景。
結束不是損失，是把佔著位置的人，請出你的未來。

en.content:
When he left, he pulled a door shut behind him.
A while later you realized that door had been blocking three prettier ones the whole time.
en.editorNote: For the friend in late-stage healing, starting to wonder 'what's next.' Sometimes a relationship ends just to clear your line of sight.
variations: The door he closed was the one jamming your view of everything behind it.
An ending isn't a loss. It's clearing out someone who was taking up space in your future.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'don't re-read the last chapter' theme; recast as a re-run exam metaphor for the getting-back-together urge

zh-tw.content:
想復合的時候提醒自己：
那不是重考，是同一張考卷、同一個答案、同一個分數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給半夜手指在通訊錄上徘徊的朋友。想念是真的，但結果通常也是真的。
variations: 會想回頭，是因為你記得開頭，不是因為結局變了。
同一條路走第二次，風景不會變，只有你會更累。

en.content:
When you want to get back together, remind yourself:
that's not a retake. Same test, same answers, same score.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose thumb is hovering over that contact at 2 a.m. The missing is real — but so is the ending.
variations: You want to go back because you remember the beginning, not because the ending changed.
Walk the same road twice and the view stays the same. Only you get more tired.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'healing is not linear' theme; recast with a staircase-with-landings image instead of a straight line

zh-tw.content:
好起來不是一條直線，
是一段有轉角的樓梯——你以為在原地繞，其實每一圈都高了一層。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種「我明明上禮拜好多了，今天又想哭」而自責的朋友。倒退不等於失敗。
variations: 今天比較難過，不代表前面那些好日子是假的。
療傷會回頭，但不會回到原點。

en.content:
Healing isn't a straight line.
It's a spiral staircase — you think you're circling the same spot, but every loop puts you a floor higher.
en.editorNote: For the friend beating themselves up because last week was better and today isn't. A step back isn't a failure.
variations: A bad day doesn't cancel out the good ones you already had.
Healing doubles back sometimes. It never takes you all the way to the start.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'you don't need them to be okay' theme; recast with a fridge-leftovers joke for humor variety

zh-tw.content:
分手一個月，冰箱裡他買的醬料還沒過期。
所以你看，你比一瓶醬料還撐得久，這不是很勵志嗎。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給已經笑得出來、但還沒完全好的朋友。用小事把悲傷變荒謬，是最溫柔的止痛藥。
variations: 他留下的東西還沒壞，你已經開始變好了，這局你贏。
醬料會過期，你不會。

en.content:
It's been a month and the sauce he bought still hasn't expired.
So really, you outlasted a condiment. That's growth.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can laugh again but isn't all the way there. Turning grief absurd with small stuff is the gentlest painkiller.
variations: His leftovers haven't gone bad yet and you're already getting better. You win this round.
Sauce expires. You don't.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'letting go is the best form of not-disturbing' theme; recast as savings/interest metaphor about self-worth

zh-tw.content:
他沒看見你的好，不是你不夠好。
是有些人只會看餘額，不懂什麼叫利息。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給開始懷疑「是不是我哪裡不夠好」的朋友。被看不懂，跟沒有價值，是兩件事。
variations: 你不是被淘汰，你只是遇到不會看的評審。
有人只算你現在值多少，忘了你還在增值。

en.content:
He didn't see your worth. That doesn't mean you didn't have any.
Some people only read the balance. They never learned what interest is.
en.editorNote: For the friend spiraling into 'maybe I just wasn't enough.' Being misread and being worthless are two different things.
variations: You weren't rejected. You just got a judge who couldn't read the scoresheet.
Some people price you at today's number and forget you're still appreciating.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'time heals and you stop noticing' theme; recast as the moment you realize you forgot to be sad

zh-tw.content:
你不會有一天突然放下他。
只會有一天，你想起他，然後發現自己忘了要難過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給急著問「我什麼時候才會好」的朋友。釋懷不是宣布的，是某天回頭才發現的。
variations: 放下沒有儀式，只有一個你沒注意到的普通下午。
不是不記得了，是記得的時候，心跳沒有變快。

en.content:
You won't wake up one day suddenly over him.
One day you'll just think of him — and notice you forgot to be sad.
en.editorNote: For the friend asking 'when does this stop hurting.' Moving on isn't announced; you find out about it in hindsight.
variations: There's no ceremony for letting go. Just an ordinary afternoon you didn't notice.
It's not that you forgot him. It's that remembering stopped changing your pulse.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the '還是朋友吧' post-breakup cliché; angle on who really benefits from that offer

zh-tw.content:
「我們還是可以當朋友」這句話，
通常是說給比較捨不得的那個人聽的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 分手後急著提「當朋友」，多半是還放不下的那方，想幫自己留一條隨時能回頭的路。真的走出來的人，不會需要這個頭銜。
variations: 當朋友沒有錯，錯的是你把它當成復合的備胎方案。

en.content:
"We can still be friends" is usually said
for the benefit of whichever one is having a harder time letting go.
en.editorNote: Rushing to 'stay friends' after a breakup usually comes from the person who hasn't let go — they want a door left open. People who've actually moved on don't need the title.
variations: Being friends is fine. Treating it as a backup plan for getting back together isn't.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on the 'reflex to share' habit that outlasts the relationship; distinct from the 3am-text impulse

zh-tw.content:
最難戒的不是他，
是每次發生好笑的事，手還是會先想傳給他的那個習慣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 失戀最磨人的往往不是大哭，是那些「想分享」的瞬間。傳給那個看到迷因就想轉發給前任的朋友，告訴他這很正常，會慢慢變淡。
variations: 你戒的不是一個人，是一個「凡事都先想到他」的反射動作。

en.content:
The hardest habit to quit isn't them.
It's your thumb still reaching to text them every time something funny happens.
en.editorNote: What wears you down after a breakup often isn't the crying — it's the 'I want to share this' reflex. Send this to the friend who still auto-forwards memes to their ex in their head. It fades.
variations: You're not quitting a person. You're quitting the reflex of thinking of them first.

items.sourceNote: Counter to the '放下、原諒' rush; validates the anger stage that most breakup quotes skip

zh-tw.content:
你不用馬上原諒他，
生氣也是療傷的一部分，不代表你不夠成熟。
zh-tw.editorNote: 太多語錄叫人「快點放下、原諒」，可是憤怒也需要空間。允許自己氣一陣子，反而比硬裝大方好得快。
variations: 先氣完，再談原諒。跳過生氣的原諒，只是把情緒埋起來等它發芽。

en.content:
You don't have to forgive them yet.
Being angry is part of healing too — it doesn't make you immature.
en.editorNote: So many quotes rush you to 'let go and forgive,' but anger needs room too. Letting yourself be mad for a while actually heals faster than faking grace.
variations: Be angry first, forgive later. Forgiveness that skips the anger just buries it to sprout again.

items.sourceNote: Modern dark-humor angle on the digital footprint of a breakup (shared playlist/streaming); distinct from physical-object jokes

zh-tw.content:
分手最麻煩的不是搬東西，
是那個共用歌單裡，每一首歌都還記得你們。
zh-tw.editorNote: 黑色幽默款。現代分手多了一項工程——清理數位痕跡。適合傳給正在猶豫要不要退出前任 Netflix 帳號的朋友。
variations: 都分手三個月了，他的 Spotify 還在推薦我們以前一起聽的歌，比他還念舊。

en.content:
The hardest part of a breakup isn't moving your stuff out.
It's that every song on the shared playlist still remembers the two of you.
en.editorNote: Dark-humor pick. Modern breakups come with an extra chore — cleaning up the digital trail. Send to the friend still debating whether to leave their ex's Netflix account.
variations: Broke up three months ago and his Spotify still recommends our old songs. More sentimental than he ever was.

items.sourceNote: Original reframe for the 'seeing your ex with someone new' moment; focus on the unchanged pattern rather than the new partner

zh-tw.content:
看到他身邊換了人，先別急著崩潰。
他只是把同一套劇本，換一個主角重演一次而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 看到前任有新對象是最容易破功的一刻。提醒自己：換的是人，沒換的是他。那套會讓你受傷的模式，下一個人也會遇到。
variations: 他不是找到更好的，只是找到還沒看穿他的。

en.content:
When you see someone new on his arm, don't spiral just yet.
He's only running the same script with a different lead.
en.editorNote: Seeing an ex with someone new is the easiest moment to relapse. Remind yourself: the cast changed, he didn't. The pattern that hurt you will find the next person too.
variations: He didn't find someone better. He found someone who hasn't seen through him yet.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the boomerang-ex who resurfaces once you've moved on; focus on his terrible timing rather than any temptation to go back

zh-tw.content:
他總是在你終於睡得著的那個月，突然傳來一句「最近好嗎」。
不是他想你了，是他發現你不再等他了——
有些人只有在快要失去掌控權的時候，才記得你的存在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛收到前任「在幹嘛」訊息、心又開始亂的朋友。提醒他：對方挑的時間點不是巧合，是你好起來的訊號被對方接收到了。你不用回，你已經贏了。
variations: 他不是想復合，他只是想確認你還在原地——結果發現你已經搬家了。
會在你最好的時候回來的人，通常是來確認自己還有沒有位子，不是來還你當初的委屈。

en.content:
He always resurfaces the month you finally sleep through the night, with a casual 'hey, how've you been?'
It's not that he misses you. He noticed you stopped waiting —
some people only remember you exist the second they feel their grip slipping.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who just got a 'you up?' from their ex and feels the ground tilting again. The timing isn't a coincidence — it's proof your healing showed. You don't owe a reply. You already won.
variations: He doesn't want you back. He wants to check that you're still where he left you — and you've already moved.
The ones who come back when you're thriving aren't returning your pain. They're checking if their seat is still warm.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on the mutual-friends fallout after a breakup; the quiet grief of losing a whole social circle, not just one person

zh-tw.content:
分手最安靜的痛，不是少了他，
是那群本來一起吃飯的朋友，突然變成要選邊站的難題。
有些人會留下，有些人會跟著他走——
留下的，才是本來就屬於你的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個分手後發現「連朋友都一起弄丟了」的人。提醒他：那些因為感情才靠近的關係，散掉是自然的，不是你人緣差。真正的朋友不用你爭取，他們早就選好邊了。
variations: 分手後那群共同朋友的沉默，不是背叛，只是他們也不知道該站哪。留下來的那幾個，記得抱緊。
你不是失去了一群朋友，你只是看清楚了誰本來就是他的、誰一直都是你的。

en.content:
The quietest part of a breakup isn't losing him.
It's watching the whole friend group turn into a seating chart nobody wants to fill in.
Some people stay, some drift off with him —
the ones who stay were always yours to begin with.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who realized they lost a whole circle, not just a partner. The friendships that only existed because of the relationship were always going to fade — that's not a reflection on you. Real friends never made you audition.
variations: The silence from the mutual friends isn't betrayal. They just don't know where to stand either. Hold the few who stayed a little tighter.
You didn't lose a group of friends. You just found out which ones were his all along, and which ones were always yours.

items.sourceNote: Original take on muscle-memory after a breakup; deleting the contact but the body still remembers, with a wry hopeful turn

zh-tw.content:
我把他的號碼刪了，可是手指還是記得那串數字。
原來遺忘一個人，身體永遠比心慢半拍。
沒關係，慢慢來——
哪天你撥錯號碼會笑出來，就代表真的過去了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「明明刪了聯絡人，手卻還會自動打出前任號碼」而覺得自己很失敗的朋友。提醒他：那不是退步，是肌肉記憶，會退的。判斷好了沒的標準，不是想不想得起來，是想起來時還痛不痛。
variations: 刪掉聯絡人只要三秒，讓手指忘記那串號碼要久一點——但它一定會忘。
你不是還放不下，你只是身體的記憶比你勇敢的速度慢了一點而已。

en.content:
I deleted his number, but my thumb still remembers the digits.
Turns out when you're forgetting someone, the body always lags half a beat behind the heart.
It's okay, take your time —
the day you catch yourself misdialing and laugh, that's when it's really over.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who deleted the contact but whose thumb still types the number automatically, and feels like a failure for it. That's not a relapse — it's muscle memory, and it fades. The test isn't whether you remember. It's whether it still hurts when you do.
variations: Deleting the contact takes three seconds. Teaching your thumb to forget the number takes longer — but it will.
You haven't failed to let go. Your body's memory is just running a little behind how brave you've already gotten.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the photo app's 'On This Day / Memories' feature resurfacing couple photos unsolicited; reframed around reclaiming the notification setting

zh-tw.content:
手機今天早上跳出「一年前的這一天」，是我們的合照。
它不知道我們分手了，還很努力地幫我回味。
我按了刪除，但沒有難過——
原來有些回憶，是它比我還放不下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被相簿「回顧」功能突襲、一睜眼就破防的朋友。軟體不懂人心，那不是命運的暗示，只是演算法在做它的工作。想關掉那個通知的權利，一直都在你手上，不用等它自己學會。
variations: 相簿不會通融，它只認日期，不認心情。想關掉回顧提醒的權利，一直都在你手上。
它推播的是一年前的你們，不是現在的你。你已經翻頁了，手機只是還沒更新。

en.content:
This morning my phone popped up 'On This Day, one year ago' — a photo of us.
It doesn't know we broke up. It's still trying so hard to help me reminisce.
I hit delete, but I didn't ache —
turns out some memories were harder for the phone to let go of than for me.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend ambushed by their photo app's 'Memories,' gut-punched before they're even out of bed. Software doesn't read hearts — that's not a sign from the universe, it's an algorithm doing its job. You can switch the notification off; you don't have to wait for it to learn.
variations: The photo app doesn't do exceptions. It only knows the date, not how you feel. The right to turn off Memories was always yours.
It's serving you the two of you from a year ago, not the you of today. You already turned the page — the phone just hasn't synced.

items.sourceNote: Original sensory-memory angle on keeping an ex's unwashed hoodie for the smell; reframes washing it as the concrete act of letting go

zh-tw.content:
他留下的那件連帽外套，我一直沒洗，因為上面還有他的味道。
昨天我終於把它丟進洗衣機，
看著泡泡把那個味道洗掉，我哭了一下，然後鬆了一口氣。
原來放下，有時候只是按下洗衣機的啟動鍵。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「留著前任的衣服捨不得洗，怕洗掉最後的味道」的朋友。那件衣服留著的不是他，是你怕忘記的心情。洗掉味道不是背叛回憶，是允許自己往前。想洗的時候就洗，不用等一個特別的日子。
variations: 你留著的不是那件外套，是怕一洗就真的沒有他了的那種害怕。但衣服洗得掉，你的人生洗不掉。
那個味道總有一天會散，不是因為你不夠愛，是因為你終於準備好了。

en.content:
He left a hoodie, and I hadn't washed it — because it still smelled like him.
Yesterday I finally threw it in the machine.
Watching the suds rinse that smell away, I cried a little, then felt myself exhale.
Turns out letting go, sometimes, is just pressing start on the washer.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend keeping an ex's clothes unwashed, afraid of losing the last trace of their smell. What they're keeping isn't the person — it's the fear of forgetting. Washing it out isn't betraying the memory; it's permission to move forward. Wash it when you're ready — no special day required.
variations: What you're holding onto isn't the hoodie. It's the fear that one wash makes them really gone. But the smell washes out — your life doesn't.
That smell was always going to fade. Not because you loved them less, but because you were finally ready.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on a pre-booked couple's trip after a breakup; going solo reframed as reclaiming something that was always yours

zh-tw.content:
那趟我們一起訂好的旅行，機票飯店都付了，人卻只剩我一個。
本來想退掉認賠，後來我決定自己去。
站在那片本來要一起看的海前面，我發現——
風景一直都在，需要有人陪才看得懂的，從來不是風景。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「分手後不知道要不要去那趟訂好的旅行」而卡住的朋友。那張機票不是他的，是你的。一個人去不是逞強，是把本來屬於你的東西拿回來。重點不是證明給誰看，是那片海你也值得看。
variations: 訂好的旅行不用退，退掉的是那個以為少了他就哪都去不了的自己。
他缺席的位子，你可以留給海風、留給自己，不一定要留給遺憾。

en.content:
The trip we booked together — flights and hotel paid, but only me left to go.
I almost cancelled and ate the loss. Instead, I went alone.
Standing at the sea we were supposed to see together, I realized —
the view was always there. Whatever needed company to make sense was never the view.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend stuck deciding whether to take a trip booked before the breakup. That ticket isn't theirs — it's yours. Going alone isn't toughing it out; it's taking back something that was always yours. The point isn't proving anything to anyone. It's that you deserve to see that ocean too.
variations: You don't have to cancel the trip. What you cancel is the version of you who thought you couldn't go anywhere without them.
The empty seat beside you can go to the sea breeze, or to yourself. It doesn't have to go to regret.

items.sourceNote: Original humor angle on a year-end music recap labeling a 'heartbreak era'; the turn is the playlist slowly getting happier as proof of healing

zh-tw.content:
年度音樂回顧出來了，系統貼心地幫我把六七月標成「心碎時期」。
我最常聽的歌手，是一個專門唱分手的。
謝謝演算法，連App都知道我那陣子過得很慘。
但你看，今年的清單裡，已經開始有幾首歡樂的歌了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被年度音樂回顧「心碎時期」四個字狠狠嘲諷的朋友。連App都看得出來你那段時間在單曲循環哭。但這其實是好消息——資料會說話，你的歌單正在慢慢變回快樂的，那就是復原的證據。
variations: 演算法很誠實，它記得你每一次的單曲循環。但它也會記得，你後來開始聽的那些快歌。
被App診斷出「心碎時期」不丟臉，丟臉的是它還很精準。至少明年的回顧，主題會不一樣。

en.content:
My year-end music recap dropped, and it kindly labeled June and July my 'heartbreak era.'
My most-played artist? Someone who only sings about breakups.
Thanks, algorithm — even the app knows I was going through it.
But look: this year's list is already picking up a few happy songs.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend roasted by their year-end music recap slapping a 'heartbreak era' label on their listening. Even the app could tell they were crying on repeat. But that's good news — the data doesn't lie, and a playlist slowly turning happy again is proof of healing.
variations: The algorithm is honest. It remembers every song you looped. But it'll also remember the upbeat ones you started playing later.
Getting diagnosed with a 'heartbreak era' by an app isn't embarrassing. What's embarrassing is how accurate it was. At least next year's recap gets a new theme.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on turning off live location sharing after a breakup; the vanished dot reframed from loss into freedom to look at your own direction

zh-tw.content:
我們曾經開著即時位置分享，地圖上有兩個小點，一直知道對方在哪。
分手那天我把它關了，地圖上只剩我一個。
剛開始很不習慣，後來我懂了——
我不用再盯著他往哪走，我終於可以只看自己要去哪。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「關掉共享位置後，一直忍不住想看他在哪」的朋友。那個小點消失不是失去，是自由。你花在追蹤別人的注意力，本來就該還給自己的方向。不用再靠地圖確認他還在不在，你的路自己走。
variations: 地圖上少了一個點，不是你的世界變小，是你終於不用再繞著別人的位置轉。
以前你靠那個小點確認他在不在乎，現在你靠自己的腳步，確認你要去哪。

en.content:
We used to share live locations — two little dots on the map, always knowing where the other was.
The day we broke up, I turned it off. Now there's just one dot: me.
It felt strange at first. Then I understood —
I don't have to track where he's going anymore. I finally get to look at where I'm going.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who turned off location sharing but can't stop wanting to check where their ex is. That vanished dot isn't a loss — it's freedom. The attention you spent tracking someone else was always meant to go back to your own direction. You don't need a map to confirm he's still there. Walk your own road.
variations: One fewer dot on the map doesn't mean your world got smaller. It means you finally stopped orbiting someone else's location.
You used to check that dot to confirm he cared. Now you check your own footsteps to confirm where you're headed.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on phone keyboard autocomplete still predicting an ex's name; clearing the learned dictionary reframed as relearning how to write your life

zh-tw.content:
我才打了一個字，輸入法就自動跳出他的名字。
我教過它幾千次，它學得比我認真多了。
昨天我把那個候選字從詞庫裡清掉——
原來連手機都要重新學一次，沒有他的日子要怎麼寫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「打字打到一半被輸入法推薦前任名字」而突然愣住的朋友。那不是命運在暗示什麼，是你自己輸入太多次留下的紀錄而已。清掉它不代表你否認那段日子，只是不想每天打字都被埋伏一次。
variations: 輸入法只是誠實，它記得你打過幾千次他的名字。但你也可以教它新的字。
詞庫可以清空，回憶不用。你刪掉的只是那個每天跳出來嚇你的捷徑。

en.content:
I typed one letter and my keyboard suggested his name.
I taught it that thousands of times — it learned better than I ever did.
Yesterday I deleted the word from my phone's dictionary.
Turns out even a phone has to relearn how to spell a life without him.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who freezes mid-text when autocomplete offers their ex's name. That's not the universe hinting at anything — it's just a log of how many times you typed it. Clearing it doesn't erase what happened. It just means you stop getting ambushed every time you open a keyboard.
variations: Autocomplete is only being honest — it remembers the thousands of times you typed his name. You're allowed to teach it new words.
You can wipe a dictionary without wiping the memory. All you deleted was the shortcut that jumped out at you daily.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on a mutual friend's wedding invitation still addressed to both names; going solo reframed as being able to celebrate others while whole

zh-tw.content:
共同朋友的喜帖寄來了，收件人上面寫著我們兩個的名字。
我沒有生氣，也懶得解釋，只是把出席人數改成一。
那天我一個人去，敬酒、拍照、把整桌菜吃完。
原來一個人也可以好好祝福別人，一點都不會少。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「收到寫著兩個人名字的喜帖」而不知道要不要出席的朋友。印錯的是喜帖，不是你的人生。一個人赴宴不是要證明什麼，是那杯喜酒你本來就有資格喝。
variations: 喜帖上多印的那個名字，是印刷廠的事，不是你的事。
出席人數改成一，不是縮水，是你終於只需要為自己確認一次。

en.content:
A mutual friend's wedding invite came, addressed to both our names.
I didn't get angry, didn't bother explaining. I just changed the headcount to one.
I went alone, raised a glass, took the photos, ate the whole table's worth.
Turns out one person can celebrate someone else completely. Nothing missing.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend holding a wedding invite with two names on it, unsure whether to go. The invite is what's outdated — not their life. Going solo isn't proving a point; that glass of champagne was always theirs to raise.
variations: The extra name on the envelope is the printer's problem, not yours.
Changing the RSVP to one isn't shrinking. It's finally only having to check with yourself.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on a series left half-watched because of a promise to watch it together; finishing it alone as permission to close things yourself

zh-tw.content:
我們一起追的那部劇，停在第七集，因為說好要一起看。
分手三個月，我終於自己按了下一集。
結局其實沒有多好看，但我把它看完了。
有些事不用等誰回來一起做，你自己也有權利把它結束掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「因為當初說好要一起看，所以片單卡在那裡動不了」的朋友。那個約定的另一半已經離席了，你不用替他守到最後一集。看完不是背叛，是把遙控器拿回自己手上。
variations: 那部劇不是在等他，是在等你願意按下一集。
有些約定過期了，你不用一個人守著它到片尾。

en.content:
The show we were watching together stopped at episode seven, because we'd promised to finish it together.
Three months after the breakup, I finally hit next episode alone.
The ending wasn't even that good. But I finished it.
Some things don't need anyone to come back for. You're allowed to end them yourself.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend whose watchlist has been frozen for months because of a promise made with someone who's gone. The other half of that deal already left the room — you don't have to keep the seat warm through the finale. Finishing it isn't betrayal. It's taking the remote back.
variations: The show isn't waiting on him. It's waiting on you to press next.
Some promises expire. You don't have to sit through the credits guarding one alone.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on a co-owned pet going to the ex because the microchip is registered in their name; visitation reframed as love that counts without ownership

zh-tw.content:
我們一起養的貓判給了他，因為晶片登記的是他的名字。
我每個月去看牠一次，牠還是會爬上我的腿踩踩踩。
離開的時候我沒有哭，只是輕輕跟牠說：
有些愛不用擁有也算數，我還是你的人，只是不住在一起了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「分手後寵物歸對方，只能偶爾去探望」的朋友。晶片上寫誰的名字是法律的事，牠記得誰是感情的事，這兩件事從來不衝突。你半夜起來餵過的那些奶、跑過的那些急診，不會因為戶口不在你這裡就不算。
variations: 登記表上沒有你的名字，但牠的記憶裡有。那個誰都改不了。
你失去的是同住的資格，不是被牠認得的資格。

en.content:
The cat we raised together went to him — the microchip was registered in his name.
I visit once a month. She still climbs onto my lap and kneads like nothing ever changed.
I didn't cry on the way out. I just told her quietly:
some love counts without ownership. I'm still yours. We just don't live together anymore.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend whose pet stayed with the ex and who only gets occasional visits. Whose name is on the chip is a legal question; who the animal remembers is an emotional one, and the two were never in conflict. Those 3am feedings and emergency vet runs don't stop counting because the paperwork says otherwise.
variations: Your name isn't on the registration. It's in her memory. Nobody gets to edit that one.
What you lost was the right to live with her, not the right to be recognized by her.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on discovering every password is still the ex's birthday; changing them all reframed as reclaiming something you use a hundred times a day

zh-tw.content:
換手機的時候我才發現，我所有帳號的密碼，都是他的生日。
分手一年了，我每天還在輸入那六個數字，一天一百次。
那個下午我把它們全部改掉，改成我自己的。
花了三個小時，但我拿回了一件我每天都要用到的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「分手很久了，密碼還是前任生日」而覺得有點難堪的朋友。那不代表你還愛他，那只代表你懶得改——但改掉它真的會有感覺。一件每天做一百次的小事，換成你自己的號碼，那是最便宜也最有效的重新開始。
variations: 你不是忘不了他，你只是還沒把那六個數字換成自己的。
改密碼花不了三個小時，花掉的是你終於承認：那組數字不該再由他決定。

en.content:
Setting up a new phone, I realized every password I own is his birthday.
A year after the breakup, I was still typing those six digits a hundred times a day.
That afternoon I changed all of them — to mine.
It took three hours, but I took back something I use every single day.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend quietly embarrassed that their passwords are still an ex's birthday long after the breakup. It doesn't mean they're still in love. It means they never got around to it — but changing them genuinely lands. Swapping a number you enter a hundred times a day is the cheapest, most effective fresh start there is.
variations: You haven't failed to move on. You just haven't swapped those six digits for your own yet.
Changing the password doesn't take three hours. What takes three hours is admitting that number shouldn't be his call anymore.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'single and ready to eat a whole pizza / freedom from bad culinary adventures' caption cluster; rewritten around reclaiming the small daily choices instead of the pizza gag itself

zh-tw.content:
分手最爽的一點：
晚餐終於不用再問「你想吃什麼」，然後聽到「都可以」。
現在我想吃什麼就吃什麼，一個人一鍋也很滿足。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛脫離「什麼都可以」地獄的朋友。失戀的正能量不用很偉大，光是重新拿回點餐的主導權就值得慶祝一下。
variations: 單身最大的福利，是我的餐廳口袋名單再也不用配合另一個人的胃。
他走了以後，我發現原來我一直很討厭那家店，只是以前不敢說。

en.content:
Best part of the breakup:
dinner is no longer 'what do you want to eat' followed by 'I don't mind.'
Now I eat exactly what I want, and a table for one tastes great.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who just escaped the 'I don't mind' dinner loop. Post-breakup wins don't have to be profound — reclaiming who picks the restaurant is worth a small celebration.
variations: The best perk of being single: my restaurant shortlist no longer has to negotiate with someone else's stomach.
After he left I realized I'd always hated that place — I just never felt allowed to say so.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'my love life is like my Wi-Fi, always disconnecting' joke; reworked into a two-bars-of-signal metaphor that lands as self-aware rather than bitter

zh-tw.content:
這段感情從頭到尾只有兩格訊號。
我一直以為是我站錯位置，換個角度再等一下就會通。
後來才懂——是這個房間本來就沒裝網路。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那個一直檢討「是不是我不夠好」的朋友。有些關係不是你的努力有問題，是對方根本沒打算接上線。訊號弱不是你的錯。
variations: 我不是收訊差，是我一直在對一支沒開機的手機傳訊息。
與其一直移動找訊號，不如承認這個地方本來就連不上。

en.content:
That whole relationship ran on two bars of signal.
I kept thinking I was standing in the wrong spot — move a little, wait a little, and it'd connect.
Turns out the room was never wired for internet at all.
en.editorNote: For the friend still auditing 'was I not good enough?' Some relationships don't fail because of your effort — the other person was simply never planning to connect. A weak signal isn't your fault.
variations: My reception wasn't bad. I was just texting a phone that was switched off.
Instead of pacing around hunting for signal, admit it: this place was never going to connect.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'ex texted I miss you, I replied the person youre looking for is no longer available' petty caption; rewritten as a quieter, non-vengeful boundary line

zh-tw.content:
他半年後傳來「我最近常想到你」。
我看了很久，沒有生氣，也沒有心動。
你想找的那個人，還在原地等你的那個版本，
已經搬走了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給收到前任「回頭訊息」而心裡動搖的朋友。你不用回得多狠，光是「那個等你的我已經不在了」就是最溫柔也最徹底的句點。放下不是報復，是升級。
variations: 不是不原諒你，是當年那個會為你熬夜的我，已經不接這支電話了。
你想念的不是我，是那個對你有求必應的自己——可惜他離職了。

en.content:
Six months later he texted, 'I've been thinking about you a lot.'
I stared at it for a while. No anger. No flutter.
The person you're looking for — the version that waited right here for you —
has moved out.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend rattled by an ex's 'coming back' text. You don't need a savage reply. 'The me who waited for you isn't here anymore' is the gentlest and most final period there is. Moving on isn't revenge — it's an upgrade.
variations: It's not that I won't forgive you. The me who used to lose sleep over you just doesn't take this call anymore.
You don't miss me. You miss the version of me who said yes to everything — and he handed in his notice.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '放不下的不是那個人，而是曾經的自己' theme; original angle added — grieving the wasted time rather than the person

zh-tw.content:
你以為你捨不得的是他，
其實你捨不得的是那三年你付出的自己。
人可以說走就走，但你的認真是真的。
別為了討回一個不值得的人，把那份認真也一起否定了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那個覺得「這幾年都白費了」的朋友。你的付出沒有錯，錯的是收下它卻不珍惜的人。認真愛過的能力，會跟著你到下一段——那才是你真正帶走的東西。
variations: 那段時間不是浪費，是你證明了自己有能力全心去愛一個人。
你哀悼的不是他，是那個曾經那麼相信愛的自己——但你可以把她接回來，而不是留在他那裡。

en.content:
You think what you can't let go of is him.
What you can't let go of is the version of you who gave three years everything.
People can walk out overnight — but your sincerity was real.
Don't cancel that sincerity just to win back someone who didn't deserve it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels those years were 'wasted.' Your effort wasn't the mistake — the mistake belonged to the person who took it and didn't treasure it. The ability to love wholeheartedly travels with you into the next chapter. That's what you actually keep.
variations: That stretch of time wasn't wasted. It proved you're capable of loving someone with your whole heart.
You're not grieving him. You're grieving the you who believed so hard in love — and you get to bring her home instead of leaving her with him.
