items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'committed relationship with myself / 感情散場換個劇場繼續精彩' captions; rewritten as a self-dating premise with concrete gestures

zh-tw.content:
分手後我開始跟自己交往。
買花給自己，記得自己的喜好，難過的時候第一個哄自己。
談了幾個月才發現——
我一直在等的那個對我好的人，原來我自己就當得起。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個「還在等一個對的人來拯救」的朋友。與其空等別人來愛你，不如先示範一次怎麼好好對待你。這段感情不會分手，而且對方超懂你。
variations: 我目前穩定交往中，對象是那個終於決定要好好照顧自己的我。
以前總把最好的留給別人，現在我把它留給自己——這是我談過最不會受傷的一段。

en.content:
After the breakup I started dating myself.
Flowers just because, remembering my own favorites, being the first to comfort me on the bad days.
A few months in it hit me —
the person I kept waiting to be good to me, I was fully qualified for the job.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend still waiting for the 'right one' to come rescue them. Instead of hoping someone else learns to love you, show yourself how it's done first. This relationship won't break up — and your partner gets you completely.
variations: Relationship status: happily committed to the me who finally decided to take care of myself.
I used to save my best for everyone else. Now I save it for me — least heartbreak I've ever had in a relationship.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'you write your own closure / a breakup is a chapter break not the final page' theme; rewritten around waiting for an explanation that never comes

zh-tw.content:
你一直在等他給你一個交代，
可是有些人連再見都說得隨便，
又怎麼會認真幫你把話講清楚。
那個交代，只能你自己寫給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個還在等前任「解釋清楚」才肯往前走的朋友。等一個不會來的道歉，只是把離開的權利一直交在對方手上。
variations: 你要的那句對不起，可能永遠不會來——但你可以不用等它，也能好起來。
結束不需要對方簽名同意，你決定放下的那一刻就生效了。

en.content:
You keep waiting for them to explain,
to hand you a real reason.
But someone who couldn't even say a proper goodbye
was never going to give you closure.
That part? You write it yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend still waiting on their ex to 'explain everything' before they'll move forward. Waiting for an apology that isn't coming just leaves the exit door in someone else's hand.
variations: The sorry you're owed might never come — and you can heal without it anyway.
Closure doesn't need their signature. It takes effect the moment you decide to let go.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the universal post-breakup habit of checking the Instagram story viewer list; framed as a signal of when you've actually moved on

zh-tw.content:
限時動態發出去的那一刻，
你其實只想確認一件事——
他有沒有點進來看。
等你哪天發完根本忘了去查名單，
那才是真的走出來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個發限動前會先想「他會不會看到」的朋友。療癒的終點不是他消失，是你終於懶得在乎他有沒有在看。
variations: 以前發限動是想給他看，現在發限動是因為我自己開心。
真正放下的訊號：他的名字出現在觀看清單裡，你只是滑過去，心跳沒有漏一拍。

en.content:
The second you post the story,
you're really only checking one thing —
whether their name shows up in the viewers.
The day you post one and forget to even look?
That's when you know you're actually free.
en.editorNote: For the friend who still wonders 'will they see this?' before posting. The finish line isn't them disappearing — it's you no longer caring whether they're watching.
variations: I used to post for them to see. Now I post because I'm the one having a good time.
Real closure: their name is in the viewer list and you just keep scrolling, heart rate unchanged.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'rediscover yourself after a breakup' theme; rewritten around reclaiming specific hobbies and friends dropped during the relationship

zh-tw.content:
分手後我把那些「因為他不喜歡」而放掉的事，
一件一件撿回來——
重聽的樂團、丟到一半的畫、
連約都約不出來的那群老朋友。
原來我不是失去了誰，
是把自己找回來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在感情裡慢慢把自己刪掉的朋友。有時候分手不是失去，是把你為了配合對方而收起來的那個版本，重新打開。
variations: 清單上那些「他覺得無聊」的興趣，現在全部變回我的了。
談戀愛的時候我活成他的形狀，分手後我才想起自己本來長什麼樣子。

en.content:
After the breakup I started picking back up
all the things I'd dropped because 'they weren't into it' —
the band I stopped listening to, the half-finished painting,
the old friends I could never seem to make time for.
Turns out I didn't lose someone.
I got myself back.
en.editorNote: For the friend who slowly edited themselves down to fit a relationship. Sometimes a breakup isn't losing something — it's reopening the version of you that you tucked away to match someone else.
variations: All the hobbies they found 'boring' are mine again now.
In the relationship I became their shape. After it ended I finally remembered my own.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the 'best friend who's heard the breakup story a hundred times' support figure; lighter, funnier tone about leaning on friends

zh-tw.content:
謝謝我那個聽前任的事聽到會背的閨蜜。
同一個故事講到第三十遍，
她還是說「他真的很爛」。
有時候療傷不需要什麼大道理，
只需要一個永遠站在你這邊的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被你當樹洞當到快脫水的好朋友，當作一句遲來的謝謝。失戀時最需要的不是分析，是有人陪你把同一句話再罵一次。
variations: 能把同一段感情陪你重複罵一百遍還不嫌煩的人，請一定要留在身邊。
他負責讓我心碎，我朋友負責陪我把它罵完——分工很明確。

en.content:
Shout-out to the best friend who's heard about my ex
so many times she could recite it.
Thirtieth time telling the same story,
and she still goes, 'yeah, he was the worst.'
Sometimes healing isn't deep advice —
it's one person who's always, unconditionally, on your side.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend you've cried to until they're basically dehydrated — as an overdue thank-you. After a breakup you don't need analysis, you need someone to trash-talk your ex with you one more time.
variations: Anyone who'll listen to the same breakup story a hundred times and not get bored — keep them forever.
He handled the heartbreak, my friends handled the group therapy. Clear division of labor.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the 'anniversary quietly becoming a normal day' milestone; the moment healing is measured not by a cry but by forgetting a once-important date

zh-tw.content:
去年今天我們還在數交往第幾週年，
今年今天我一整天都沒發現它是今天。
原來放下不是用力忘記，
是有一天，那個日期安靜地變回了普通的日期。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手滿一年、卻在某天突然發現自己「沒感覺了」的你。療癒的終點不是大哭一場，是那個曾經很重要的日子，變回月曆上普通的一格。
variations: 以前那天是紀念日，現在那天只是垃圾要拿去倒的日子。
不是我故意忘了紀念日，是我終於過得太好，沒空記得它。

en.content:
Last year on this date we were counting anniversaries.
This year the whole day went by before I realized what day it was.
Turns out moving on isn't forcing yourself to forget —
it's the day a once-important date quietly becomes just a date.
en.editorNote: For the person who, a year out, suddenly notices they feel... nothing. Healing doesn't end with one big cry. It ends the day a date that used to matter goes back to being just a square on the calendar.
variations: That date used to be our anniversary. Now it's just the day the trash goes out.
I didn't forget the anniversary on purpose. My life just got good enough that I forgot to remember it.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the 'ordering for two' muscle-memory habit fading after a breakup; reframed as reclaiming your own preferences

zh-tw.content:
點咖啡的時候，我差點又說「兩杯，一杯半糖」。
話到嘴邊才想起，現在只要點我自己喜歡的就好。
有些習慣要花很久才改得掉，
但改掉的那一刻，也代表你把自己拿回來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個還會不小心買兩份早餐、點兩杯飲料的人。分手後最痛的不是大事，是這種身體還記得、腦子卻要重新學的小動作。改掉它不是遺忘，是重新認識一個人也能過得很好的自己。
variations: 現在點餐只要顧自己的口味，這種自由我居然花了一段感情才換到。
從「兩杯半糖」改成「一杯全糖」，這就是我今年最大的進步。

en.content:
Ordering coffee, I almost said 'two — one with half the sugar.'
Caught it just in time and remembered: now I only order what I like.
Some habits take forever to unlearn,
but the moment you do, you've taken yourself back.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who still reaches for two breakfasts, two drinks. After a breakup the killer isn't the big stuff — it's the tiny motions your body still remembers while your brain has to relearn them. Unlearning them isn't forgetting; it's meeting the version of you that's fine on your own.
variations: Now I only have to think about what I want. Wild that it took a whole relationship to earn that.
Went from 'two, one half-sweet' to 'one, full sugar.' Biggest glow-up of my year.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the empty passenger seat reframed from loneliness into freedom and regained control

zh-tw.content:
有人說副駕的空位很寂寞，
可是我發現，那個位子空著的時候，
我終於可以想去哪就去哪，
不用先問一句「你想去嗎」。
空位不一定是失去，有時候是把方向盤要回自己手上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛學會一個人開車兜風、一個人旅行的你。分手後那個空掉的副駕座，可以是傷口，也可以是「這趟路我自己決定」的自由，看你想把它看成哪一種。
variations: 副駕沒人坐，反而沒人跟我搶播歌權了。
以前那個位子有人，我卻常常不知道要去哪；現在沒人，我反而清楚得很。

en.content:
People say an empty passenger seat is lonely.
But I've noticed that when it's empty,
I can finally go wherever I want,
without first asking, 'do you want to come?'
An empty seat isn't always a loss — sometimes it's the wheel back in your own hands.
en.editorNote: For the person just learning to take solo drives and solo trips. That empty passenger seat can be a wound, or it can be the freedom of 'this route is mine to pick.' You get to choose which one it is.
variations: Nobody in the passenger seat means nobody fighting me for the aux cord.
Back when that seat was full, I never knew where I was going. Empty, I somehow know exactly.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the quiet, tearless ritual of throwing out an ex's leftover item as proof of moving on

zh-tw.content:
今天我把他忘在我這的牙刷丟了。
沒有大哭，也沒有拍照發限動，
就只是很平常地把它丟進垃圾桶。
原來真正的結束，
有時候安靜得連一滴眼淚都不需要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個房間裡還留著前任一兩樣小東西、遲遲丟不掉的人。有一天你會發現，丟掉它不再需要儀式感，那才是你真的走出來的證明。
variations: 丟掉那支牙刷的時候我才發現，我早就不痛了，只是東西還沒清。
不是狠心，是那些東西對現在的我來說，真的只是垃圾了。

en.content:
Today I threw out the toothbrush he left at my place.
No big cry, no dramatic story on my feed —
just dropped it in the trash like it was nothing.
Turns out a real ending
can be quiet enough it doesn't need a single tear.
en.editorNote: For the person still holding onto one or two small things an ex left behind. One day you'll realize tossing them doesn't need a ceremony anymore — and that's the proof you've actually moved on.
variations: Throwing out that toothbrush is when I realized I'd stopped hurting ages ago. I just hadn't cleaned up yet.
It's not that I'm cold. Those things are just genuinely trash to the person I am now.

items.sourceNote: Original writing inspired by the 2026 wave of situationship-ending posts about grieving a relationship that was never officially defined

zh-tw.content:
我們沒有在一起過，所以我連難過都要偷偷的。
沒有分手日、沒有交代、沒有人問我還好嗎。
但我想說：
難過不用等名分核准。
你付出的是真的，那失去的也是真的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個曖昧了半年、最後不了了之，卻覺得自己沒資格難過的朋友。沒有頭銜的感情結束，一樣需要好好哀悼。
variations: 最痛的不是分手，是連分手的資格都沒有。
沒有名分的關係結束，還是會痛。痛不需要合約認證。

en.content:
We were never officially together, so even my sadness had to stay quiet.
No breakup date, no closure, nobody asking if I'm okay.
But here's the thing:
grief doesn't need a title to be approved.
What you gave was real, so what you lost is real too.
en.editorNote: For the friend who spent six months in something undefined that just quietly stopped, and now feels like they haven't earned the right to hurt. An ending without a label still deserves to be mourned.
variations: The worst part wasn't the breakup. It was not even qualifying for one.
Undefined doesn't mean painless. Your heart never asked for the paperwork.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the 2026 habit of venting to an AI chatbot at night instead of texting an ex

zh-tw.content:
分手那個月，我每天半夜把想對他說的話，全部打給 AI 看。
它每一句都回，回得又快又溫柔，
只有一件事它做不到——
它不會突然說「我也想你」。
打到第三十天我終於看懂：
我要的從來不是有人回，是那個人肯回。
而那個人，已經不打算了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜想按下傳送鍵的時候先看一遍。找個地方把話講完是好事，但也要誠實面對：你真正在等的不是回覆，是他。承認了，才走得動。
variations: 凌晨三點我對著 AI 打了兩千字，它秒回。那一刻我才發現，原來我不是缺人聊天，是缺他。
AI 什麼都回我，就是不會回那句我最想聽的。也好，這樣我才知道該停了。

en.content:
The month we broke up, I typed everything I wanted to say to him into a chatbot instead.
It answered every time — fast, patient, kind.
There was only one thing it couldn't do:
it never once said "I miss you too."
By day thirty I finally got it.
I never wanted someone to answer. I wanted him to.
And he wasn't going to.
en.editorNote: Read this before you hit send at 2am. Getting the words out somewhere is genuinely good — just be honest that what you're waiting for isn't a reply, it's him. Naming that is what lets you move.
variations: 3am, two thousand words typed to an AI, instant reply. That's when it hit me: I didn't need company. I needed him.
It answers everything except the one line I actually wanted. Honestly, that's how I knew to stop.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on the moment of running into an ex at a mutual friend's wedding and feeling nothing

zh-tw.content:
在共同朋友的婚禮上，我又看到他了。
我以為我會手抖、會躲、會找藉口先走，
結果我只是點了個頭，然後回座位繼續吃甜點。
那天我沒有哭，
但我在計程車上笑了很久——
原來痊癒不是轟轟烈烈，
是有一天你看見他，心跳完全沒有加速。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在擔心「以後遇到他怎麼辦」的人。你不會知道那天什麼時候來，但它會來，而且平淡到你當下甚至沒發現。
variations: 再見到他的時候，我居然先想到的是甜點還沒吃完。這大概就是好了吧。
痊癒的證明不是你不想他，是你看見他，然後照常呼吸。

en.content:
I saw him again at a mutual friend's wedding.
I thought my hands would shake, that I'd hide, that I'd invent a reason to leave early.
Instead I nodded once and went back to my seat to finish dessert.
I didn't cry that night.
But I laughed the whole cab ride home —
turns out healing isn't dramatic.
It's the day you see him and your pulse doesn't change at all.
en.editorNote: For anyone quietly dreading the day they run into their ex. You won't know when it's coming, but it will — and it'll be so uneventful you might not even notice it happening.
variations: I saw him and my first thought was that I hadn't finished my cake. I think that's what recovered looks like.
You're not healed when you stop thinking about him. You're healed when you see him and just keep breathing normally.

items.sourceNote: Original writing on muscle memory outlasting a relationship — walking the old route home without thinking

zh-tw.content:
下班的時候我又走錯了。
走到他家那個巷口才停下來，站在便利商店前面發呆。
腦子明明早就接受了，
可是腳還記得。
別罵自己，那不是不爭氣，
那只是身體還在慢慢學新的路。
它比你想的更認真，只是需要一點時間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「我明明覺得自己好了，卻又不小心做出習慣動作」的日子。走錯一次不代表退步，那只是舊路還沒被新路蓋過去。
variations: 腦子放下了，腳還沒。給它一點時間，它會跟上的。
走錯路不是還愛著，只是習慣還沒被改寫完。

en.content:
I took the wrong way home again after work.
Didn't notice until I hit the corner by his place and just stood there outside the convenience store.
My head accepted it months ago.
My feet didn't get the memo.
Don't be hard on yourself — that's not weakness.
Your body is just still learning a new route.
It's trying harder than you think. It only needs time.
en.editorNote: For the days when you thought you were fine and then caught yourself running an old habit. One wrong turn isn't a relapse — the new route just hasn't finished overwriting the old one.
variations: My head let go. My feet are still catching up. They'll get there.
Walking the old way home doesn't mean you still love him. It means the habit hasn't been rewritten yet.

items.sourceNote: Original dark-humor writing about reselling the second concert ticket bought for an ex

zh-tw.content:
去年搶到的兩張演唱會門票，今年只需要一張。
另一張我轉賣出去了，
溢價的部分，比這段感情帶給我的還多。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後還卡著情侶行程的人。行程照走，位子換人坐，你的門票從來不是為誰買的。
variations: 門票兩張，人剩一個。好消息是我旁邊終於沒人一直問「這首叫什麼」。
把另一張賣掉的那一刻，我第一次覺得這段感情有回本。

en.content:
I fought for two concert tickets last year. This year I only need one.
I resold the other,
and the markup was a better return than the whole relationship gave me.
en.editorNote: For anyone stuck with couple plans after a breakup. Go anyway — the seat just gets a new occupant. You never bought that ticket for him.
variations: Two tickets, one person. Upside: nobody next to me asking what song this is every three minutes.
Selling that second ticket was the first time the relationship ever showed a profit.

items.sourceNote: Breakup-recovery guide covering the practical admin of untangling a shared life; rewritten into a Taiwan clinic-form scene about the emergency contact field

zh-tw.content:
看診單上「緊急聯絡人」那一欄，我寫了三年他的名字。
昨天終於劃掉，換成那個接電話從來不超過兩聲的朋友。
沒有儀式，也沒有哭，
只是把「最靠得住的人」這格，填上正確答案。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後開始處理生活小欄位的人：掛號單、保單、公司表格。改掉的不只是名字，是你對「誰真的會來」的判斷。
variations: 改欄位的時候才發現，我把最重要的位置，留給一個不會接電話的人整整三年。
那一格從來不是給最愛的人填的，是給最會出現的人填的。

en.content:
For three years, the emergency contact line on every form said his name.
Yesterday I crossed it out and wrote the friend who never lets the phone ring twice.
No ceremony, no crying.
I just put the right answer in the blank marked "person I can count on."
en.editorNote: For the post-breakup stretch where you're quietly updating forms — clinic, insurance, HR. You're not just changing a name; you're correcting who you actually believe will show up.
variations: Updating that one line, I realized I'd given the most important slot to someone who doesn't pick up.
That blank was never for the person you love most. It's for the person who actually shows up.

items.sourceNote: Gentle coping article on rebuilding solo daily routines after a breakup; reworked into a concrete cooking-portions scene

zh-tw.content:
分手後第一次自己下廚，還是抓了兩個人的份量。
吃了三天剩菜才學會，一個人到底要買多少菜。
現在我煮得剛剛好，
連胃口都調回我自己的尺寸了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開始一個人生活、還在抓生活比例的人。份量抓錯不是失敗，是你正在重新認識自己需要多少。
variations: 第一週煮太多，第二週煮太少，第三週剛好。學費是六個保鮮盒。
以前買菜是想著他愛吃什麼，現在我終於知道自己想吃什麼了。

en.content:
First time cooking after the breakup, I still shopped for two.
Three days of leftovers later, I finally learned how much one person eats.
Now I get the portion right —
even my appetite is back to my own size.
en.editorNote: For anyone relearning the scale of their own life. Getting the portions wrong isn't failure — it's you finding out how much you actually need.
variations: Week one: too much. Week two: too little. Week three: exactly right. Tuition paid in six containers of leftovers.
I used to shop around what he liked. Now I finally know what I like.

items.sourceNote: No-contact article framing distance as protection and redirected self-care; reimagined as reviving a plant the ex left behind

zh-tw.content:
他搬走的時候，留下一盆快乾死的黃金葛。
我本來想順手丟掉，結果每個星期還是澆了一次水。
半年後，它爬滿了整片窗台。
我從來不是不會照顧人，
只是以前都澆在不會長的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「我是不是付出太多」的自我懷疑時刻。問題從來不是你給得不夠好，是那邊接不住。
variations: 同樣的水，同樣的我，換一個會長的東西，結果差這麼多。
他留下的那盆植物活得比這段感情久，而且是我養活的。

en.content:
When he moved out, he left behind a half-dead pothos.
I meant to toss it, and somehow watered it once a week anyway.
Six months later it's taken over the whole windowsill.
I was never bad at taking care of someone.
I was just watering somewhere nothing would grow.
en.editorNote: For the moment you start wondering if you loved too hard. The problem was never how much you gave — it's that nothing on the other end could hold it.
variations: Same water, same me, different thing to grow. Look at the difference.
The plant he abandoned has outlived the relationship, and I'm the one who kept it alive.

items.sourceNote: Digital-boundaries guide listing smart-home reconfiguration as a post-breakup step; reimagined as a lamp still running on the ex's schedule

zh-tw.content:
客廳的燈還是每天七點二十自動亮起，
因為那是他以前下班進門的時間。
我看著空房間亮了三個月，
昨天終於把那個排程刪掉。
燈不會想念任何人，
是我一直捨不得改設定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合「明知道該整理，卻一直拖著」的階段。有些東西留著不刪，不是忘不掉，是還沒準備好承認。
variations: 我不是走不出來，我只是還沒把那個排程刪掉。
現在我家的燈，是我想幾點亮就幾點亮。

en.content:
The living room lamp still switched itself on at 7:20 every night,
because that's when he used to walk in from work.
I watched an empty room light up for three months.
Last night I finally deleted the schedule.
The lamp was never missing anyone.
I was just too attached to change the setting.
en.editorNote: For the stage where you know you should clean it up and keep putting it off. Leaving it there isn't proof you can't move on — it's proof you weren't ready to say it out loud yet.
variations: I'm not stuck. I just hadn't deleted the timer yet.
These days the lights in my place come on whenever I say so.

items.sourceNote: Digital-decluttering piece on closing out shared financial accounts; reworked into settling the last line in a bill-splitting app

zh-tw.content:
分帳 App 上最後一筆，是他欠我三百二的火鍋錢。
他昨天轉了，餘額變成零。
我盯著那個零看很久——
錢的部分我們終於誰也不欠誰，
可是那三年的份，沒有一個 App 算得出來。
算不出來的，就別再算了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後還在心裡盤點「誰付出比較多」的時候。金額可以結清，感情不行，硬要算只會把自己困在裡面。
variations: 他把三百二還我了，剩下的三年就當我請客。
餘額歸零那一刻我才懂，有些帳單本來就不該送出去。

en.content:
The last line in our bill-splitting app was twelve bucks he owed me for hot pot.
He paid it yesterday. Balance: zero.
I stared at that zero for a while.
Money-wise, neither of us owes the other a thing now.
But no app can total up the three years.
The part you can't calculate — stop trying to.
en.editorNote: For when you're still privately tallying who gave more. You can settle a balance; you can't settle a relationship. Running the numbers just keeps you inside it.
variations: He paid back the twelve bucks. The three years are on me.
Watching that balance hit zero, I realized some invoices were never meant to be sent.

items.sourceNote: Article urging people to exit shared streaming plans after a breakup; turned into the moment a family plan reads 'Members: 1'

zh-tw.content:
今天我把他從音樂串流的家庭方案裡移出去。
畫面跳出一行字：目前成員 1 人。
我笑了一下，因為那個「1」看起來一點都不可憐。
月費沒有比較貴，播放清單也沒有比較短，
只是這次，沒有人再把我的推薦歌單搞亂了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合處理那些拖著沒斷的共用帳號時。行政手續辦完的那天，通常比分手那天更像分手。
variations: 家庭方案剩我一個，但這個家終於歸我管。
移除成員只要三秒，我卻拖了四個月。

en.content:
Today I removed him from my music streaming family plan.
A line popped up: Members: 1.
I laughed, because that '1' didn't look sad at all.
The bill isn't higher. The playlists didn't get shorter.
Nobody's wrecking my recommendations anymore.
en.editorNote: For the day you finally deal with the shared logins you've been avoiding. The paperwork day usually feels more like the breakup than the breakup did.
variations: Family plan, party of one — and the household is finally mine.
Removing a member takes three seconds. It took me four months.

items.sourceNote: Digital-detox guidance about archiving saved memorabilia; reframed as replaying a kept voice message and hearing the tone differently

zh-tw.content:
手機裡還留著他一則十四秒的語音，
內容只有一句「我到樓下了，下來」。
我留了一年，一直捨不得刪。
昨天不小心點開，聽完的第一個念頭是——
他那時候講話怎麼那麼不耐煩。
原來時間不是讓你忘記，
是讓你終於聽得出當時漏掉的語氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送給還在美化過去的人。回憶會自動幫對方修圖，但錄音不會。
variations: 我留著那則語音一年，聽完只花三秒就刪掉了。
不是我變狠了，是我終於聽懂他的語氣。

en.content:
There's still a 14-second voice message from him on my phone.
All it says is 'I'm downstairs, come down.'
I kept it for a year, couldn't bring myself to delete it.
I played it by accident yesterday, and my first thought was:
wow, he sounded annoyed.
Time doesn't make you forget.
It just lets you finally hear the tone you missed.
en.editorNote: For anyone still airbrushing the past. Memory retouches everything. Recordings don't.
variations: Kept that voice note a whole year. Deleting it took three seconds.
I didn't get colder. I just finally heard how he was talking to me.

items.sourceNote: Therapist article on rebuilding solo routines after a breakup; dramatized as finishing prepaid partner training sessions alone

zh-tw.content:
分手後我去上那堂還剩八次的雙人重訓課。
教練第一天問：「另一位今天沒來嗎？」
我說沒有，以後都不會來了。
他愣了兩秒，說：「那我幫你把重量調成你自己的。」
那句話我記到現在——
原來很多東西，本來就該調成我自己的尺寸。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「兩個人一起報名、最後只有一個人去上」的尷尬時刻。把重量調回自己的尺寸不是將就，是校正。
variations: 剩下那八堂我全部自己上完了，而且還加了重量。
調成我自己的重量以後才發現，我一直在幫兩個人扛。

en.content:
After the breakup I showed up for the eight partner training sessions we'd prepaid.
The coach asked, 'Is the other one not coming today?'
I said no. Not anymore.
He paused, then said, 'Alright, let me set the weight for just you.'
I still think about that line.
A lot of things should have been set for just me all along.
en.editorNote: For the awkward stretch after you two signed up together and only one of you keeps showing. Resetting the load to your own size isn't settling — it's calibration.
variations: Finished all eight sessions by myself. Added weight, too.
Once it was set for just me, I realized I'd been carrying for two.

items.sourceNote: Article on the bargaining stage of post-breakup grief; dramatized as a 2 a.m. list of what-ifs where every line has the same subject

zh-tw.content:
凌晨兩點，我列了一張「如果當初」清單。
如果當初我少問一句、多等一天、脾氣再好一點……
寫到第十七條我停筆了，
因為每一條的主詞都是我。
一段感情要兩個人才走得完，
檢討名單上卻只有一個名字。
那不是清單，那是我在替他寫辯護狀。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜開始自我檢討的時候。要反省可以，但先看看這份名單漏掉了誰。
variations: 我的「如果當初」有十七條，他的有零條。
把清單撕掉那天我才懂，我不是在找原因，是在找罪人。

en.content:
Two in the morning, I made a list of everything I should have done.
Should have asked less. Waited one more day. Kept my temper.
I stopped at number seventeen,
because every single line started with 'I.'
It takes two people to end a relationship,
but only one name made it onto the list.
That wasn't a list. That was me writing his defense for him.
en.editorNote: For 2 a.m., when your brain starts building a case against you. Reflect all you want — just notice who the prosecution keeps forgetting to call.
variations: My what-if list had seventeen lines. His had zero.
I tore it up and realized I wasn't looking for reasons. I was looking for someone to blame.

items.sourceNote: 2026 wellness-travel trend piece featuring breathwork sessions; reworked into a single exhale instruction landing as emotional release

zh-tw.content:
那堂療癒課老師只教一件事：吐氣要比吸氣長。
我連續失敗三次，
然後突然懂了——
這兩年我一直在吸氣，
憋著等他一句解釋、一個回覆、一次道歉。
吸進去卻不吐出來的東西，不會變成力氣，只會變成悶。
那天我第一次把氣完整吐完，
走出教室的時候整個人輕了兩公斤。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合胸口一直悶著、又說不出哪裡痛的階段。放下不一定要先想通，有時候只要先把那口氣吐掉。
variations: 我花兩年學會憋氣，花一堂課學會吐氣。
沒有人欠我一個解釋，我只是欠自己一口氣。

en.content:
The entire class was one instruction: make the exhale longer than the inhale.
I failed three times in a row,
and then it clicked —
I'd spent two years inhaling,
holding my breath for an explanation, a reply, an apology.
Air you never let out doesn't turn into strength. It turns into pressure.
That day I emptied my lungs all the way for the first time,
and walked out five pounds lighter.
en.editorNote: For the stage where your chest is permanently tight and you can't point to why. Letting go doesn't have to start with understanding — sometimes it starts with an exhale.
variations: Two years learning to hold my breath. One hour learning to let it out.
Nobody owes me an explanation. I just owed myself one breath out.

items.sourceNote: Moving-on guide about reclaiming shared routines solo; turned into finishing a two-card loyalty stamp promotion alone

zh-tw.content:
超商的點數快集滿了，兌換說明寫著：需兩張卡合併。
以前那張是他的。
我站在櫃檯前算了一下，
決定自己再多喝三十杯，把它集滿。
三個月後我抱著那個鍋子回家，
煮了這輩子第一鍋只給自己吃的湯。
有些東西看起來要兩個人才換得到，
其實只是比較慢而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得「很多事一個人做不到」的時候。不是做不到，是要久一點——而且成果整個是你的。
variations: 他那張卡我沒等，我自己集滿了。
一個人集比較慢，但沒有人會半路把卡抽走。

en.content:
The stamp card at the corner store was almost full. The fine print said: two cards required.
One of them used to be his.
I stood at the counter doing the math,
and decided to drink thirty more coffees and finish it myself.
Three months later I carried that pot home
and made the first soup I've ever cooked just for me.
Some things look like they take two people.
They just take longer.
en.editorNote: For when you're convinced certain things are off-limits to one person. They aren't. They're slower, and every bit of the result is yours.
variations: Didn't wait on his card. Filled mine.
Solo takes longer, but nobody walks off with half your stamps.

items.sourceNote: Esther Perel discussion of symbolic breakup rituals such as the unsent letter; reimagined as crossing out the recipient and writing your own name

zh-tw.content:
心理師要我寫一封不會寄出去的信給他。
我寫了三頁，
通篇都在解釋我當初為什麼那樣做、為什麼那不是我的錯。
寫完重看一遍，
我把收件人劃掉，改成自己的名字——
整封信突然就通順了。
原來我從頭到尾要的不是他的原諒，
是我自己的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合腦中一直排練「跟他把話說清楚」的人。你最想寄出去的那封信，收件人一直都是你自己。
variations: 那封信我沒寄，但我唸了三次，每次都是唸給自己聽。
我等的不是他回信，是我自己肯簽收。

en.content:
My therapist told me to write him a letter I'd never send.
I wrote three pages,
all of it explaining why I did what I did, why none of it was my fault.
I read it back,
crossed out his name at the top and wrote my own —
and suddenly the whole thing made sense.
What I'd been after the entire time wasn't his forgiveness.
It was mine.
en.editorNote: For anyone still rehearsing the conversation that would finally set the record straight. The letter you keep wanting to send was addressed to you all along.
variations: Never sent it. Read it three times, out loud, to myself.
I wasn't waiting on his reply. I was waiting on myself to sign for it.

items.sourceNote: 2026 therapist commentary on the no-contact trend and heartbreak activating withdrawal-like brain circuits; reworked into the hand learning to stop before the heart does

zh-tw.content:
朋友說不聯絡就像戒菸，前兩週最難。
她沒說的是，最難的不是想他，
是我的右手已經自己學會了——
解鎖、滑到那個位置、然後停住。
那個停住的動作我練了六十幾天。
心還沒好，但手先好了。
有時候復原就是這樣，身體先走，腦袋慢慢跟上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合正在執行「不聯絡」卻覺得自己失敗的人。你不是沒進步，只是進步的地方不在你以為的那裡。
variations: 我沒有戒掉他，我只是戒掉了點開的那一下。
第六十三天，我的手比我的心先學會停下來。

en.content:
A friend said cutting contact is like quitting smoking — the first two weeks are the worst.
What she didn't say is that the hard part isn't missing him.
It's that my right hand already learned the whole routine:
unlock, swipe to that spot, and stop.
I've practiced that stop for sixty-some days.
My heart isn't better yet. My hand is.
Sometimes that's how healing goes — the body leaves first and the mind catches up.
en.editorNote: For anyone doing no contact and convinced they're failing at it. You are making progress; it's just not showing up where you keep checking.
variations: I didn't quit him. I quit the tap.
Day sixty-three: my hand learned to stop before my heart did.

items.sourceNote: Feature on folk beliefs that a breakup signals an incoming turn of luck; reimagined as asking the wrong question at a temple

zh-tw.content:
我去廟裡問了三次「我們還有機會嗎」，
三次都沒有筊。
最後一次我賭氣改口問：「那我以後會好嗎？」
一次就聖筊。
我蹲在那邊笑到眼淚掉出來——
原來不是神明不理我，
是我一直在問一個已經有答案的問題。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合還在到處求證「有沒有可能復合」的階段。真正卡住你的，往往不是沒有答案，是你不肯換一個問題。
variations: 問他三次都沒筊，問我自己一次就過了。
神明不回答的那題，通常是我早就知道答案的那題。

en.content:
I went to the temple and asked three times: is there still a chance for us?
Three times, no answer.
On the last throw I gave up and asked instead: will I be okay?
Yes, first try.
I crouched there laughing until I was crying.
It was never that nobody was listening.
I just kept asking the one question I already knew the answer to.
en.editorNote: For the stage where you're collecting second opinions on whether you two could work again. What's stuck isn't the missing answer — it's your refusal to change the question.
variations: Asked about him three times and got nothing. Asked about me once and got a yes.
The question that never gets answered is usually the one you've already answered.

items.sourceNote: Psychologist's post-breakup recovery strategies noting the first weeks are only the start; dramatized through a cast coming off and physical therapy still to come

zh-tw.content:
去年手腕骨折，拆石膏那天我以為結束了。
醫生說：「骨頭接好了，但肌肉忘記怎麼用力，還要練三個月。」
我當下沒什麼感覺，昨天才突然聽懂。
我早就不想他了，這叫骨頭接好了。
可是有人對我好的時候，我還是會先退半步——
那是肌肉還沒練回來。
不痛了不等於能用了，剩下那段沒有人會替你練。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合已經不難過、卻發現自己不太敢再靠近人的階段。那不是還沒走出來，那是下一段復健。
variations: 骨頭接好了，肌肉還在偷懶，這很正常。
不痛只是第一關，敢再用力才是第二關。

en.content:
I broke my wrist last year, and the day the cast came off I thought that was it.
The doctor said: the bone healed, but the muscle forgot how to work. Three more months.
It didn't register then. It registered yesterday.
I stopped missing him a long time ago — that's the bone.
But when someone's kind to me I still take half a step back.
That's the muscle.
Not hurting isn't the same as working again, and nobody can do that part for you.
en.editorNote: For when the sadness is gone but you notice you've stopped letting people close. That's not a relapse. That's the physical therapy nobody warned you about.
variations: Bone's fine. Muscle's lazy. Completely normal.
Not hurting is round one. Daring to put weight on it is round two.

items.sourceNote: Article on cliff-edge breakups where one side vanishes without explanation; reframed as a TV series cancelled mid-season

zh-tw.content:
我很愛的一部影集，第三季拍到一半就停播了。
沒有結局，沒有交代，最後一集還在鋪梗。
粉絲在網路上寫了幾百種續集版本，我也寫過我們的。
後來才知道停播的理由通常很無聊：
不是劇情走不下去，是有人不想演了。
他也一樣。
我花了一年幫他補台詞，其實他只是收工了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被斷崖式分手、到現在還想不通為什麼的人。有些故事沒有結局，不是你漏看，是根本沒拍。
variations: 我不是看不懂結局，是他根本沒拍完就走了。
幫他補了一年的台詞，最後發現他早就把劇本放下了。

en.content:
A show I loved got cancelled halfway through season three.
No finale, no explanation — the last episode was still setting things up.
Fans wrote hundreds of versions of how it should have ended. I wrote ours.
Turns out cancellations usually have boring reasons.
The story didn't run out. Somebody just stopped showing up.
Same with him.
I spent a year writing his lines for him. He'd already clocked out.
en.editorNote: For anyone ghosted mid-relationship who's still trying to reconstruct why. Some stories have no ending — not because you missed it, but because it was never filmed.
variations: I didn't miss the ending. He left before they shot it.
A year of writing his dialogue, and he'd put the script down on day one.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; the theme of seeing a relationship clearly only long afterwards is common in lovelorn quote roundups, reframed here as an undeveloped roll of film

zh-tw.content:
背包夾層裡有一捲底片，我拖了兩年沒拿去洗。
昨天終於送去沖，店員說都還在，一張都沒壞。
照片裡他在笑，我也在笑，
但我看得出來，那天的我已經在勉強了。
原來有些東西要等很久才顯影——
包括我到底撐了多久。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手很久之後，才慢慢看清當時狀態的人。當下看不見的，時間會幫你顯影。
variations: 那捲底片洗出來的不是回憶，是我當年沒察覺的疲憊。
照片從來沒有騙人，只是我花了兩年才敢看。

en.content:
There was a roll of film in my backpack I'd put off developing for two years.
I finally dropped it off. The guy at the counter said every frame came out fine.
He's smiling in them. So am I.
But I can see it now — I was already forcing it that day.
Some things take a long time to develop.
Including how long I'd been holding on.
en.editorNote: For anyone who only sees the truth of a relationship long after it ended. What you couldn't see then, time brings into focus.
variations: That roll didn't develop memories. It developed the exhaustion I never noticed.
The photos never lied. It just took me two years to be able to look.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; riffs on the widely-discussed problem of an ex's leftover belongings, narrowed to one useless object

zh-tw.content:
他留下一條充電線，接頭跟我的手機不合。
我插不進去，卻也一直沒丟，就讓它躺在床頭整整一年。
昨天我終於把它捲起來收走，
不是氣他，也不是突然想通了什麼——
只是我終於承認：
放在身邊的東西，不是每一樣都能給我電。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合家裡還留著前任物品、卻說不出為什麼的人。留著不等於還愛，但可以問問它到底給了你什麼。
variations: 那條線一年沒充過任何東西，倒是每天提醒我一次。
不能給我電的東西，就沒有資格繼續躺在我床頭。

en.content:
He left a charging cable behind. Wrong port — it doesn't fit my phone.
I couldn't plug it into anything, and I still didn't throw it out. It sat by my bed for a year.
Yesterday I finally coiled it up and carried it out.
Not out of anger. No big epiphany.
I just admitted the obvious:
not everything you keep close is actually charging you.
en.editorNote: For anyone still holding onto an ex's leftover stuff without knowing why. Keeping it doesn't mean you still love them — but it's fair to ask what it's giving you.
variations: That cable powered nothing for a year. It only reminded me, daily.
If it can't charge you, it doesn't get to sit by your bed.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; inverts the usual 'erase every trace of them' advice into acceptance of inherited speech habits

zh-tw.content:
分手半年，我還是會脫口說出他的口頭禪。
那句話本來不是我的，是聽久了自己搬進來的。
我沒有急著把它改掉，
因為它證明的不是我還愛他，
是我真的認真跟一個人生活過。
總有一天我會忘記那是誰教我的，
然後它就只是我講話的樣子了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合發現自己身上還留著前任痕跡、因而自責的人。被影響過不丟臉，那些習慣最後都會變成你自己的。
variations: 那句口頭禪已經不欠他了，從現在起算我的。
他沒有改變我，只是留下一點證據，證明我認真愛過。

en.content:
Six months out, I still catch myself using his catchphrase.
It was never mine. I just heard it enough times that it moved in.
I'm not in a hurry to unlearn it.
It doesn't prove I still love him.
It proves I actually shared a life with someone.
One day I'll forget who taught it to me,
and it'll just be how I talk.
en.editorNote: For anyone beating themselves up over the traces an ex left behind. Being shaped by someone isn't shameful — eventually those habits just become yours.
variations: That phrase doesn't belong to him anymore. I'm keeping it.
He didn't change me. He just left proof that I loved somebody properly.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; measures healing by how briefly you can retell the relationship to someone new

zh-tw.content:
最難的其實不是想他，
是新認識的人問：「你上一段是怎麼結束的？」
三年，我得練習用三句話講完。
第一次被問的時候，我卡了很久，
最近一次，我講完還順便喝了口水。
你知道自己好了，
不是因為忘記，
是因為那個故事終於變得可以很短。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開始接觸新對象、卻怕被問起過去的人。療癒的刻度，就藏在你講那段往事需要多久。
variations: 以前要講一個小時，現在三句話就夠了——這就是進度。
我沒有忘記，我只是終於可以長話短說。

en.content:
The hard part isn't missing him.
It's when someone new asks, "So how did your last one end?"
Three years, and I have to fit it into three sentences.
The first time, I froze for a while.
Last time, I finished and casually took a sip of water.
You know you're okay
not when you've forgotten,
but when the story finally gets short.
en.editorNote: For anyone starting to date again and dreading questions about the past. Healing shows up in how long it takes you to tell the story.
variations: It used to take an hour. Now it takes three sentences. That's the progress.
I didn't forget. I just got good at the short version.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; phone photo-app face grouping offers 'show this person less' instead of delete

zh-tw.content:
手機把他的臉自動歸成一個人物相簿，四百多張。
我找刪除鍵找了很久，只找到一個選項叫「減少顯示這個人」。
那天我按下去，覺得手機比我懂事——
它知道有些人刪不掉，
但可以讓他少出現在你眼前一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合捨不得刪照片、又不想一直被回憶偷襲的人。放下不是格式化，是把出現頻率調低。
variations: 沒有一鍵刪除的功能，是因為人生本來就沒有。你能做的是調低音量。
我沒有把他從相簿裡挖掉，我只是不再讓他排在第一頁。

en.content:
My phone auto-grouped his face into a People album. Four hundred photos.
I hunted for a delete button and only found one called "Show this person less."
I tapped it, and thought my phone had more sense than I did—
it knows some people can't be deleted,
only turned down.
en.editorNote: For anyone who can't bring themselves to delete the photos but hates being ambushed by them. Letting go isn't a factory reset; it's lowering how often someone shows up.
variations: There's no delete-everything button, because life doesn't have one either. You just turn the volume down.
I didn't scrub him out of the album. I just stopped letting him lead with page one.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; delivery-app saved address book still holding an ex's apartment

zh-tw.content:
點外送的時候，地址欄還躺著他家：五樓，電鈴壞了要打電話。
那行備註是我打的，我還記得自己打得多細心。
昨天我把整筆地址刪掉，
系統問我「確定要刪除嗎」，我按了確定，一秒都沒猶豫。
原來我早就不需要記得，怎麼進到那扇門了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後被日常小介面偷襲的人。真正的結束，常常發生在某個沒人看見的設定頁裡。
variations: 他家的地址我背得比自己身分證號還熟，昨天終於還給系統了。
電鈴壞掉不是我的事了，這件事想起來竟然有點爽。

en.content:
The delivery app still had his place saved: fifth floor, buzzer's broken, please call.
I typed that note myself. I remember how carefully I typed it.
Yesterday I deleted the whole address.
It asked, "Are you sure?" and I hit yes without a pause.
Turns out I no longer need to remember how to get through that door.
en.editorNote: For anyone getting ambushed by tiny everyday interfaces. The real ending usually happens on some settings page nobody sees.
variations: I knew his address better than my own ID number. Yesterday I gave it back to the app.
That broken buzzer is not my problem anymore, and honestly it feels great.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; shared collaborative trip-planning doc frozen in version history

zh-tw.content:
我們共編的那份旅行計畫還在，標題是「明年春天」。
版本紀錄停在三月十一號，最後一次編輯的人是他，
改的是「這段先空著，之後再說」。
我沒有刪掉那份檔案，只是複製了一份，改成我自己的名字，
然後把那句「之後再說」刪掉，填上日期。
有些行程不是取消了，是換人負責。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合把未來寄放在別人身上的人。計畫還是可以走完，只是主辦人換成你自己。
variations: 他留下一句「之後再說」就下線了，那個「之後」我自己排進行事曆了。
檔案我沒刪，我另存新檔——同一趟旅行，換一個作者。

en.content:
Our shared trip doc is still there, titled "Next Spring."
Version history stops on March 11. Last edit: him.
What he changed was one line—"leave this blank, we'll figure it out later."
I didn't delete the file. I made a copy under my own name,
deleted "later," and put in an actual date.
Some plans aren't canceled. They just change owners.
en.editorNote: For anyone who parked their future in someone else's hands. The trip can still happen; you're just the organizer now.
variations: He logged off on a "we'll figure it out later." I put that later on my calendar myself.
I didn't delete the doc. I saved a copy—same trip, new author.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; secondhand bookstore docks the price for handwriting on the flyleaf

zh-tw.content:
我把他送的那疊書拿去二手書店賣。
店員一本一本翻，翻到最上面那本停住：
「這本扉頁有寫字，收購價要打折喔。」
我說沒關係。
走出店門我才笑出來——
原來那句我看了三年、以為很重的話，
在市場上只值少一點點的錢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合還把某句情話當成聖旨的人。有些話的重量是你自己給的，換個地方秤就輕了。
variations: 那句話讓我失眠三年，結果它的市價是打八折。
書我賣了，字留給下一個讀者去猜是誰寫的。

en.content:
I took the stack of books he gave me to a secondhand shop.
The clerk flipped through them and stopped at the top one.
"There's handwriting on the flyleaf. I'll have to knock the price down."
I said that's fine.
I didn't laugh until I got outside—
that line I'd reread for three years, the one I thought weighed a ton,
was worth exactly a small discount on the open market.
en.editorNote: For anyone still treating one old love note as scripture. Some words only weigh that much because you're the one holding the scale.
variations: That sentence cost me three years of sleep. Its market value: about 20% off.
Sold the books. Left the handwriting for the next reader to wonder about.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; reframes the cliche that time heals by splitting rinsing from scrubbing

zh-tw.content:
大家都說時間會沖淡一切。
沒人告訴你，時間只負責沖，
刷的那部分還是要你自己來。
你有好好吃飯、有去看醫生、有把那些話講出來，
它才沖得動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合已經等了很久卻覺得沒進展的人。時間是水，不是清潔劑，你得自己動手那一下。
variations: 時間會沖淡一切，但它不會幫你刷鍋底。
等了一年沒好起來不是你的錯，是你一直在等水，沒有拿菜瓜布。

en.content:
Everyone says time heals everything.
Nobody mentions that time only does the rinsing.
The scrubbing part is still on you.
Eat properly, see someone about it, say the thing out loud—
that's what gives the water something to work with.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's waited a long time and feels stuck. Time is water, not detergent. You still have to do the scrubbing.
variations: Time heals everything, but it will not scrub the bottom of the pan for you.
A year in and still hurting isn't a failure. You were waiting on water without picking up the sponge.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; hair salon scene where the post-breakup haircut is reframed from revenge to first solo decision

zh-tw.content:
他以前總說我留長比較好看。
昨天我坐在鏡子前，設計師問要修多少，
我聽見自己說：「剪到肩膀。」
剪刀第一下下去的時候，我手有點抖，
第二下就不抖了。
原來我不是在報復誰，
我只是這輩子第一次，替自己的頭髮做決定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後想換造型、又怕被說「這是報復性剪髮」的人。重點從來不是剪多短，是這一次是你自己說了算。
variations: 「剪這麼短不會後悔嗎？」會啊，但那是我自己的後悔。
頭髮會長回來，被別人決定的那三年不會。

en.content:
He always said I looked better with it long.
Yesterday I sat down in the chair and the stylist asked how much to take off.
I heard myself say, "To the shoulders."
My hands shook on the first cut.
By the second one they didn't.
Turns out I wasn't getting back at anyone.
I was just deciding about my own hair for the first time in my life.
en.editorNote: For anyone changing their look after a breakup and bracing for someone to call it a revenge haircut. The length was never the point — the point is that the call was yours.
variations: "What if you regret going that short?" Maybe I will. But it'll be my regret.
Hair grows back. The three years of someone else deciding don't.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; scooter passenger footrests left folded out long after the breakup, reframed as unfinished tidying rather than devotion

zh-tw.content:
分手一年多，我才發現機車的後座腳踏板一直是打開的。
不是留給誰，就只是忘了收。
昨天停進格子裡，我彎腰把它折回去，
「喀」一聲，兩秒鐘的事。
有些位置不是你還幫誰留著，
是你太久沒有低頭看一眼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得「明明早就沒事了，卻好像哪裡還卡著」的人。有些殘留不是深情，只是還沒整理到。
variations: 我以為那叫深情，其實只是懶得收。
折回去只花兩秒，我卻拖了一年才願意低頭看。

en.content:
More than a year after the breakup, I noticed the passenger footrests on my scooter were still folded out.
Not saved for anyone. Just never put away.
Yesterday, pulling into a space, I bent down and clicked them back in.
Two seconds. One small snap.
Some spaces aren't being held for somebody.
You just haven't looked down in a long time.
en.editorNote: For anyone who is technically fine but still feels snagged on something. Not every leftover is devotion — some of it is just tidying you never got around to.
variations: I thought it was loyalty. It was laziness.
It took two seconds to fold up. It took me a year to look down.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; expired appliance warranty outlasting the relationship, black-humor durability comparison

zh-tw.content:
他搬走的時候留下一個電鍋，說反正他不煮。
那台電鍋現在還在。上禮拜整理抽屜翻到保固卡，早就過期了。
過期的東西還在運轉，沒有期限的那個先壞掉。
我看著蒸氣冒上來，突然覺得很好笑——
原來一段感情的耐用度，
真的比不上一台一千八的家電。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合已經能拿自己開玩笑的階段。笑得出來，通常就是快好了。
variations: 家電有保固，感情沒有，這是我今年學到最貴的一課。
他留下的電鍋比他有責任感，至少它每天都準時。

en.content:
When he moved out he left the rice cooker. Said he never cooked anyway.
It's still here. I found the warranty card in a drawer last week — expired ages ago.
The expired thing still runs. The thing with no expiration date broke first.
I watched the steam come up and honestly laughed:
a relationship turned out to be less durable
than a sixty-dollar appliance.
en.editorNote: For the stage where you can finally joke about it. If you can laugh, you're usually close to okay.
variations: Appliances come with a warranty. People don't. Most expensive lesson of my year.
The rice cooker he left behind is more reliable than he was. At least it shows up on time.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; library overdue fine on a book he recommended, where nobody was ever collecting the charge

zh-tw.content:
他推薦的那本書，我從圖書館借出來就沒還過。
通知信每個禮拜寄一次，滯納金一天一塊，我算過，四百多天。
昨天終於拿去還，館員掃了條碼，抬頭說：
「這本兩年前就下架了，不用付。」
我站在櫃檯前笑出來。
原來那筆錢從頭到尾沒有人在收，
是我自己每天，準時扣自己一塊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一直告訴自己「再撐一下就會有結果」的人。你以為的堅持，很多時候只有你自己在計費。
variations: 滯納金一天一塊，我繳了四百多天，收款人一直是我自己。
那本書我早就看不下去了，只是不想承認它該還了。

en.content:
That book he recommended — I checked it out of the library and never took it back.
The overdue notice came every week. A dime a day. I did the math once: four hundred-something days.
Yesterday I finally returned it. The librarian scanned it, looked up, and said,
"This one was pulled from the catalog two years ago. You don't owe anything."
I laughed right there at the desk.
Nobody had ever been collecting that money.
I'd just been charging myself, every day, right on schedule.
en.editorNote: For anyone telling themselves that holding on a little longer will finally pay off. A lot of the time you're the only one running the meter.
variations: A dime a day for four hundred days. Turns out I was both the debtor and the collector.
I stopped being able to read it a long time ago. I just didn't want to admit it was due.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; Qixi spent alone, reframed through the festival's craft-wish origin as self-directed humor

zh-tw.content:
今年七夕我一個人在家，滑手機才知道，七夕本來叫乞巧節，
以前的人那天求的是一雙巧手，不是一段姻緣。
我對著螢幕笑了很久。
原來我這幾年每年準時許願，表格從頭到尾都投錯窗口。
今年我改許了：手巧一點就好，會煮飯、會修東西、會把自己的日子過好。
這個願望，好像第一年就該許了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合七夕當天一個人在家、又不想發厭世文的人。把願望從「遇到誰」換成「把自己的日子做好」，講起來輕很多。
variations: 我許了好幾年的姻緣願，結果那天本來收的是手工藝類的申請。
今年七夕我沒有許誰，我許我自己：手要巧，日子要過得起來。

en.content:
Qixi, it turns out, started as a festival for wishing for nimble hands — needlework, craft, skill — not for being sent someone.
I found that out this year, home alone, and laughed at myself for a solid minute.
Years of wishes, all filed at the wrong window.
So this year I asked for the hands instead: cook well, fix things, build a life I can actually live in.
Honestly, that's the wish I should have made the first time.
en.editorNote: For anyone spending Qixi at home alone and not in the mood to post something bitter. Swapping "send me someone" for "let me build my own days" lands a lot lighter.
variations: Wished for romance every year. Turns out the festival's original department was arts and crafts.
This year's wish: skilled hands, decent meals, a life that runs without anyone else's help.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; dripping faucet he never fixed, fixed solo with a cheap washer, reframed from repair skill to showing up

zh-tw.content:
浴室的水龍頭滴了一年多，他每次都說週末有空就來修。
上個月我自己上網看了三支影片，去五金行買了一個五十塊的墊片，
蹲在那邊十五分鐘，水就停了。
那天晚上我躺著，聽浴室安安靜靜的，
才發現我等的從來不是一個會修水龍頭的人，
是一個說了會來、就真的會來的人。
而這件事，我自己做得到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被「我下次來處理」拖了很久的人。真正累的不是那個滴水聲，是一直在等的那個人。
variations: 五十塊的墊片解決了一年的滴水，我不知道該笑還是該開發票給他。
後來我學會了：與其等別人有空，不如自己有工具。

en.content:
The bathroom faucet dripped for over a year. He kept saying he'd fix it some weekend.
Last month I watched three videos, bought a two-dollar washer at the hardware store,
crouched down for fifteen minutes, and the dripping stopped.
That night I lay there listening to a completely quiet bathroom
and realized I was never waiting for someone who could fix a faucet.
I was waiting for someone who showed up when he said he would.
That part I can do myself.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's been strung along by "I'll get to it next weekend." The exhausting part was never the drip — it was the waiting.
variations: A two-dollar washer fixed a year of dripping. I don't know whether to laugh or send an invoice.
Stopped waiting for someone to be free. Bought my own tools instead.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; keeping a baseball fandom an ex introduced, inverting the usual give-it-back instinct

zh-tw.content:
是他帶我去看第一場球的，那年我連幾局都搞不清楚。
分手兩年，我還是每個週末打開轉播，
還是會為了一支再見安打從沙發上跳起來，
還是背得出先發輪值。
有人問我看球不會想到他嗎，
我說不會，這支球隊現在是我的。
有些喜歡是別人帶你進門的，
但走進去以後留下來的那份，一直都算你自己的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合擔心「喜歡的東西是前任介紹的，還能不能繼續喜歡」的人。門是他開的，但後來每一場都是你自己看完的。
variations: 他介紹的球隊我留下了，他沒留下，這筆我覺得我賺。
問我看球會不會想到他？我只會想到上一局那個失誤。

en.content:
Baseball came into my life through him — he took me to my first game, back when I couldn't follow an inning.
Two years after the breakup I still turn the broadcast on every weekend,
still jump off the couch for a walk-off hit,
still know the whole starting rotation.
People ask whether watching makes me think of him.
It doesn't. The team is mine now.
Somebody else may have opened the door,
but whatever you kept after walking through it was always yours.
en.editorNote: For anyone worried they're not allowed to keep loving something an ex introduced them to. He opened the door; every game since, you watched on your own.
variations: Kept the team, lost the guy. Pretty sure I came out ahead on that trade.
Does watching remind me of him? No. It reminds me of the error in the seventh.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; ex's mother still sending weekly good-morning messages, grieving the family rather than the person

zh-tw.content:
分手三個月，他媽媽還是每個禮拜傳早安圖給我。
我沒有封鎖，也一直沒有回。
上個禮拜我終於打了一句：阿姨我很好，你也要保重。
她回我：好啦，記得吃飯。
關掉對話框，我才發現眼睛紅了——
原來我捨不得的不只是那個人，
還有那段日子裡，有人把我當自己人。
那份好是真的，不會因為結束就不算數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後才發現自己更想念對方家人的人。那段被當成自己人的日子是真的，可以好好謝謝它，再放下。
variations: 她的早安圖我留著沒回，其實我捨不得的是那句「記得吃飯」。
要還回去的是那個人，不是那段被好好對待的日子。

en.content:
His mother still sends me a good-morning message every week, three months after the breakup.
I never blocked her. I also never replied.
Last week I finally wrote back: I'm doing okay, please take care of yourself.
She answered: Good. Don't skip meals.
I closed the chat and noticed my eyes had gone red.
What I missed wasn't only him.
It was being treated, for a while, like family.
That part was real, and it doesn't stop counting because the rest ended.
en.editorNote: For anyone who found out after the breakup that they miss his family most. Those months of being treated like family were real — thank them, then set them down.
variations: Never answered her good-morning texts. The part I couldn't let go of was "don't skip meals."
You give back the person. You don't have to give back having been cared for.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; Ghost Month offerings repurposed as a private send-off ritual for the relationship

zh-tw.content:
這禮拜五鬼門開，我媽要我下班順路買普渡要拜的餅乾。
我多拿了一包，結帳的時候自己都笑出來。
拜的時候我沒有念他的名字，只在心裡說：
那段感情，謝謝你來過，吃飽了就走，不用再回來了。
香燒完，那包餅乾我自己拆開吃掉——
原來我要送走的從來不是他，
是那份被我留在桌上、遲遲不肯收起來的心意。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合農曆七月一個人過、想給自己一個小小告別儀式的人。借一個現成的節奏把那段感情好好請走，比逼自己忘記容易得多。
variations: 普渡我多買了一份，不是給他，是給那個一直守著空位的自己。
拜完的供品最後還是自己吃掉，就像那些心意，繞一圈都會回到你身上。

en.content:
Ghost Month opens this Friday, so my mom asked me to pick up offering snacks on the way home.
I grabbed one extra pack and laughed at myself at the register.
When I set them out, I didn't say his name. I just thought:
thank you for coming, eat well, and don't come back.
After the incense burned down I opened that extra pack and ate it myself.
Turns out I wasn't sending him off.
I was finally clearing the place setting I'd left out too long.
en.editorNote: For anyone spending Ghost Month alone who wants a small private goodbye. Borrowing a ready-made ritual is easier than ordering yourself to forget.
variations: Bought one extra offering. Not for him — for the version of me still saving his seat.
You end up eating the offerings yourself. Same with everything you put out there.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; summer electricity bill dropping after the breakup, the household shrinking measured in numbers rather than feelings

zh-tw.content:
七、八月那期電費帳單來了，比去年同一期少了一千二。
少一個人洗澡、少一台電腦整夜開著、冷氣只吹一間房。
我盯著那個數字看很久，沒有很爽，也沒有很難過。
就只是很清楚地知道——
這個家真的變小了，
而我一個人，還付得起。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被生活裡的數字提醒「他真的不在了」的人。帳單不是傷口，是你正在自己撐起一個家的證明。
variations: 夏天的電費少了一千二，我沒有很爽，只是知道自己付得起。
有些改變不是誰宣布的，是帳單先告訴你的。

en.content:
The summer electricity bill came in about forty dollars lower than last year.
One less person showering, one less laptop humming all night, the AC cooling one room instead of two.
I stared at the number for a long time. Not thrilled, not wrecked.
Just very clear on one thing:
this place did get smaller,
and I can still cover it by myself.
en.editorNote: For anyone who finds out from a utility bill that the breakup is real. The bill isn't a wound — it's proof you're carrying a home on your own.
variations: The bill dropped forty bucks. I wasn't thrilled or crushed. I just knew I could still pay it.
Nobody announces that your life got smaller. The bill tells you first.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; dating app resurfacing the ex as a high-percentage match, answered with a one-second left swipe

zh-tw.content:
半夜滑交友軟體，系統把他推到我面前，還標了「配對度 92%」。
那張照片是我拍的，簡介裡那句話是我幫他想的。
我對著螢幕笑了一下，然後往左滑掉。
這輩子第一次，關於他的決定我只花了一秒。
演算法算得出我們有多像，
算不出我已經不想再試一次了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在交友軟體上被系統推到前任的人。你不欠演算法一次重來，一秒的左滑就是完整的答案。
variations: 系統說我們配對度 92%，可惜少的那 8% 剛好是「他會不會留下來」。
演算法只看得到我們多合，看不到我們為什麼散。

en.content:
Swiping late at night, the app served him up with a "92% match" badge.
I took that photo. I wrote half of that bio.
I laughed at the screen, then swiped left.
First time in my life a decision about him took one second.
The algorithm can measure how alike we are.
It can't measure how done I am.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose dating app resurfaced their ex. You don't owe an algorithm a second try — a one-second left swipe is a complete answer.
variations: 92% match. Shame the missing 8% was whether he'd stay.
The algorithm sees how well we fit. Not why we ended.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; grandmother asking where he is at a family dinner and answering with food instead of follow-up questions

zh-tw.content:
回家吃飯，阿嬤端菜出來的時候問：那個高高的怎麼沒一起來？
我說他不來了。
她「喔」了一聲，沒有多問，只是把那盤蝦推到我面前：
那你多吃一點。
那頓飯我吃到打嗝——
原來有些人不需要你解釋，
也不會因為你少帶一個人回來，就少疼你一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合害怕回家被問感情狀況的人。真正在乎你的家人聽完只會多夾一塊給你，不會要你交代。
variations: 阿嬤沒問我為什麼分手，只說：那你多吃一點。
有些愛不用解釋，它只會問你吃飽了沒。

en.content:
Back home for dinner, my grandma set down a dish and asked where the tall one was.
I said he's not coming anymore.
She said oh, asked nothing else, and pushed the shrimp toward me.
Then eat more.
I ate until I couldn't breathe.
Some people don't need the explanation,
and they don't love you any less for coming home one person short.
en.editorNote: For anyone dreading the relationship question at a family dinner. The people who actually care just put more food on your plate.
variations: Grandma never asked why we broke up. She just said, then eat more.
Some love doesn't ask for the story. It asks whether you've eaten.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; movie seat selection and realizing the constraint was always 'two seats together'

zh-tw.content:
以前買電影票，我們一定要兩個位子連在一起，
所以每次都只能挑到最邊邊那排，仰著頭看兩小時。
昨天我一個人訂票，滑開座位圖，
正中間那個位子是空的，我按下去，沒有問任何人。
燈暗下來的時候我才想到——
原來這些年我不是沒得選，
我只是每次都先把「兩個」放進條件裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後第一次一個人做「以前都兩個人做」的事。不用先遷就別人這件事，需要練習幾次才會習慣。
variations: 一個人訂票，我第一次坐到正中間。
不是沒得選，是我每次都先把「兩個」放進條件裡。

en.content:
We always needed two seats together,
so we ended up in the last row every time, necks craned for two hours.
Last night I booked alone, opened the seat map,
and the dead-center seat was open. I tapped it. I asked nobody.
When the lights went down it hit me:
I was never short on options.
I just put "two" into the filter every single time.
en.editorNote: For the first time you do something alone that you only ever did as a pair. Not having to accommodate anyone takes a few reps to feel normal.
variations: Booked one ticket and finally sat dead center.
I always had options. I just filtered for two every time.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; dreaming about the ex and waking up bored instead of hurt

zh-tw.content:
昨天晚上夢到他了。
夢裡我們在吵一件事，就是那件我以前可以難過三天的事。
醒來我躺著想了五秒，
第一個感覺不是心痛，是無聊。
然後我翻個身，繼續睡到鬧鐘響。
原來痊癒不是他不再出現在夢裡，
是他出現了，你也懶得配合演完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一夢到前任就整天低氣壓的人。夢到不代表你退步了，重點是醒來之後你花多久回到自己的生活。
variations: 他還是會出現在夢裡，只是我懶得配合演完。
醒來的第一個感覺是無聊，那天我就知道我好了。

en.content:
He showed up in a dream last night.
We were arguing about the thing that used to wreck me for three days straight.
I lay there for five seconds after I woke up,
and the first thing I felt wasn't pain. It was boredom.
Then I rolled over and slept until my alarm.
Healing isn't him disappearing from your dreams.
It's him showing up and you not bothering to play your part.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose whole day is ruined by one dream about their ex. Dreaming about them isn't backsliding. What counts is how fast you get back to your day.
variations: He still shows up in dreams. I just don't bother playing along.
The first thing I felt was boredom. That's when I knew.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; walking the same route at your own pace and finally noticing the street

zh-tw.content:
以前跟他走在一起，我大概每十步就要小跑兩步才跟得上。
我從來沒說過，因為我以為那是我的問題，腿短而已。
上禮拜我走同一條路回家，用我自己的速度，
才發現轉角那家麵包店開了七年，
下午四點出爐的時候，整條街都是味道。
這條路我走了四年，
那是第一次我有時間看它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合總覺得是自己「跟不上」對方的人。合不合拍不是誰的錯，但一直用不是自己的速度走，沿路的東西你一樣都看不到。
variations: 跟不上不是我腿短，是那從來就不是我的速度。
同一條路用自己的速度走，才看見開了七年的那家店。

en.content:
Walking with him, I had to break into a little jog every ten steps to keep up.
I never said anything. I assumed it was my problem. Short legs.
Last week I walked the same route home at my own pace
and noticed the bakery on the corner has been there seven years.
At four in the afternoon the whole street smells like bread.
Four years on that street,
and that was the first time I had time to look at it.
en.editorNote: For anyone who kept deciding they were the one who couldn't keep up. Mismatched pace isn't a fault, but walking at someone else's speed means you miss the entire street.
variations: It wasn't short legs. It was never my pace.
Same street, my speed, and suddenly there's a bakery I'd never seen.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; the label 'you have no sense of direction' disproved by one solo drive

zh-tw.content:
他總說我方向感差，所以出去玩都是他開，我負責看導航。
說久了我也信了，連租車的駕駛欄都懶得填自己的名字。
上個月我自己開了三小時山路去看日出。
中途走錯一個交流道，繞了二十分鐘，然後就到了。
沒有人罵我，天也沒有塌下來。
原來「你不會」這三個字，
有時候只是有人講得比你大聲而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被前任長期貼標籤、久到自己都信了的人。挑一件他說你做不到的事，自己做一次，答案就出來了。
variations: 他說我方向感差，說到我自己也信了。
走錯一個交流道，繞了二十分鐘，然後我還是到了。

en.content:
He always said I had no sense of direction, so he drove and I read the map.
He said it enough that I believed it. I stopped even putting my name on the rental form.
Last month I drove three hours of mountain road alone to catch a sunrise.
I took one wrong exit, lost twenty minutes, and then I got there.
Nobody yelled. The sky stayed up.
Turns out "you can't do that"
is sometimes just someone saying it louder than you did.
en.editorNote: For anyone who wore an ex's label long enough to believe it. Pick one thing they said you couldn't do and do it once. That settles it.
variations: He said I had no sense of direction until I believed him.
One wrong exit, twenty extra minutes, and I still got there.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; still buying the shampoo he recommended and realizing you never liked the smell

zh-tw.content:
浴室那瓶洗髮精，是他當初說好用我才換的。
分手一年多，我還是照買。昨天買到第五瓶，我停在架子前面——
我根本不喜歡這個味道。
我不是委屈，也不是懷念，我是連「可以換」都沒想過。
那天我拿了另一瓶去結帳。
有些東西不是他留下來的，
是我自己忘了問一句：那你喜歡哪一種？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手很久、日子看起來早就正常，卻還照著舊設定在過的人。從一瓶洗髮精開始，重新問自己的喜好。
variations: 買到第五瓶才發現，我根本不喜歡這個味道。
「那你喜歡哪一種？」這句話我很久沒問過自己了。

en.content:
The shampoo in my bathroom is the one I switched to because he said it was good.
Over a year out and I was still buying it. Yesterday, on bottle five, I stopped in the aisle.
I don't even like this smell.
It wasn't loyalty and it wasn't grief. It just never occurred to me that I could change it.
I walked out with a different bottle.
Some things aren't what he left behind.
They're the question I forgot to ask myself: which one do you actually like?
en.editorNote: For anyone long past the breakup whose life looks normal but still runs on the old settings. Start with one bottle of shampoo and re-ask what you like.
variations: Bottle five is when I realized I never liked the smell.
Which one do you actually like? I hadn't asked myself in years.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; three years of e-invoice mobile carrier scans logged under an ex, reframed as never having put anything in your own name

zh-tw.content:
這三年結帳，我都報他的手機條碼。
說好中獎的錢一起花，可是我一次都沒去對過獎。
上個月我終於申請了自己的載具，兩個禮拜後手機跳通知：中兩百。
我對著螢幕笑到不行，不是因為那兩百塊，
是因為這三年我買的每一樣東西，
原來沒有一張，是登記在我自己名下的。
我還是很少中獎，
但現在每一張，上面寫的都是我的名字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後正在一樣一樣補辦「自己的東西」的人：載具、帳戶、會員卡。中不中獎是其次，名字終於是自己的才是重點。
variations: 申請自己的載具兩個禮拜就中兩百，投資報酬率比談三年戀愛好。
這三年買的每一樣東西，沒有一張發票寫我的名字。

en.content:
Three years of checkout screens and I scanned his code every single time.
We said we'd split anything we won. I never once checked the numbers.
Last month I registered my own digital receipt account. Two weeks later my phone buzzed: six dollars.
I laughed way too hard for six dollars.
Three years of things I bought,
and not one receipt had my name on it.
I still barely win anything.
But every ticket says me now.
en.editorNote: For anyone re-registering their own life one line at a time after a breakup — receipts, accounts, memberships. Winning isn't the point. The name on it is.
variations: Two weeks with my own account, six dollars won. Better return than three years.
Three years of purchases and not one receipt in my name.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; counting your own apologies in the old chat thread as a measure of who was maintaining the relationship

zh-tw.content:
昨天我在跟他的對話紀錄裡，搜了三個字：對不起。
我八十七次，他四次。
看到那個數字，我第一個念頭居然是「他可能只是不習慣道歉」。
你看，我連在整理證據的時候，都還在幫他寫辯護詞。
後來我把對話關掉，沒有刪。
我沒有變得比較恨他，
只是終於承認：那三年，維持這段感情是我一個人的工作。
以後我還是會說對不起，但只在我真的做錯的時候。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後還在反覆檢討自己的人。不用刪紀錄，數一次就好——次數會告訴你，那段關係裡是誰在出力。
variations: 八十七比四。那不是吵架紀錄，那是我的工作日誌。
以後我還是會說對不起，但只在我真的做錯的時候。

en.content:
Eighty-seven to four. That's how many times each of us said sorry.
Searched one word in the old thread and there it was.
My first thought at that number was still: maybe he's just bad at apologizing.
Even while sorting the evidence, I was writing his defense.
I closed the thread. Didn't delete it.
I don't hate him any more than I did yesterday.
I just finally admit that for three years, holding us together was my job alone.
I'll still apologize. Only when I'm actually wrong.
en.editorNote: For anyone still auditing themselves months after it ended. Don't delete the thread — just count. The count tells you who was doing the work.
variations: Eighty-seven to four isn't an argument log. It's a timesheet.
I'll still apologize. Only when I'm actually wrong.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; friends admitting after the breakup that none of them ever liked the ex, reframed as evidence of who stayed

zh-tw.content:
分手第三天，四個朋友把我約出去吃飯，第一句是：
「其實我們都不太喜歡他。」
我問：「憋多久了？」
「三年。」
四個人，三年，沒有一個講過。
我本來想生氣，後來想想——
他們閉嘴，是因為那時候我很開心；
他們開口，是因為現在換他們照顧我。
那頓飯我們笑到被隔壁桌看。
分手最痛的是少一個人，
最好笑的是發現原來還有四個人一直都在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合剛分手、覺得世界一下子空掉的人。約那幾個一直都在的人吃一頓飯，順便問他們憋多久了。
variations: 「我們其實都不太喜歡他。」「憋多久了？」「三年。」
分手少了一個人，才發現旁邊一直站著四個。

en.content:
Three days after it ended, four friends dragged me out to dinner. Opening line:
"None of us actually liked him."
I asked how long they'd been sitting on that.
"Three years."
Four people. Three years. Nobody said a word.
I wanted to be angry, and then I understood —
they stayed quiet because I was happy then;
they spoke up because now it's their turn to look after me.
We laughed loud enough that the next table turned around.
The worst part of a breakup is one person fewer.
The funniest part is finding out four were standing there the whole time.
en.editorNote: For that first week, when it feels like everyone walked out with them. Get dinner with the people who stayed and ask how long they've been holding it in.
variations: "None of us liked him." "How long?" "Three years."
Lost one person. Found out four had been there the whole time.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; topping up an online cart to hit the free-shipping threshold revealed as an excuse to start a conversation

zh-tw.content:
以前差一百塊免運，我就問他要不要順便加什麼，兩秒就湊到了。
昨天我又差九十塊，購物車裡放了洗碗精、束口袋、一支根本不需要的手機支架，
放了三十分鐘，最後全部刪掉，付了六十塊運費。
六十塊，換一車都是我真的要的東西。
我一直以為湊免運是在省錢，
其實那是我找他說話的藉口。
現在我不用湊了。
想他的時候就直接想，不用假裝在買東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「什麼都要先問對方一句」的習慣還沒改掉的人。下次湊不到免運就別湊了，那筆運費是最便宜的一次練習。
variations: 差九十塊免運，我刪掉整台車，付了六十塊運費，換一車都是我要的東西。
以前以為湊免運是省錢，其實是找他說話的藉口。

en.content:
Three dollars short of free shipping. I used to just ask what he needed — cart full in two seconds.
Yesterday I was short again. Dish soap, a drawstring bag, a phone stand I don't need.
Thirty minutes later I deleted all of it and paid the two-dollar shipping.
Two dollars for a cart with nothing in it I didn't actually want.
I thought topping up the cart was about saving money.
It was an excuse to text him.
Now I don't need the excuse.
When I miss him, I just miss him. No shopping required.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose habit of checking with someone first hasn't worn off yet. Next time you're short of free shipping, don't top it up — that shipping fee is the cheapest practice run you'll get.
variations: Deleted the whole cart, paid the two-dollar shipping, kept only what I wanted.
Topping up the cart was never about saving money.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; end-of-summer 'settling back in' routines reframed as emotional recovery work

zh-tw.content:
暑假快結束了，大家都在做收心操。
沒有人告訴你，失戀也要做。
心在外面晃了那麼久，
總得有人喊它回來坐好。
那個人只能是你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合暑假尾聲、心還飄在某個人身上的時候。開學會有人幫你打鐘，感情不會，鐘要自己敲。
variations: 開學前大家都在收心，失戀的人也該收了。
心晃太久了，喊它回來坐好的那個人只能是你。

en.content:
It's the last stretch of summer. Everyone's easing back into a schedule.
Nobody tells you a breakup needs one too.
Your heart's been wandering around out there for months.
Someone has to call it back to its seat.
That someone is you.
en.editorNote: For the end of summer, when your head is still somewhere near a certain person. School has a bell. Heartbreak doesn't — you ring your own.
variations: Everyone's easing back into a routine. Your heart could use one too.
Nobody's going to call your heart back to its seat but you.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; an optician's routine question exposes how long the narrator outsourced their own taste

zh-tw.content:
配眼鏡的時候，店員調出舊資料問：「鏡框跟上次一樣就好嗎？」
我說：「不一樣。」
「那你想要什麼樣的？」
我卡住了。
這副是他挑的，他說圓的看起來比較溫柔。
我戴了四年，從來沒問過自己喜歡哪一種。
最後我挑了一副方的，我媽說很醜，我很喜歡。
看得清楚是重點，
但要用誰的眼光看，是我的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分手後第一次為自己做選擇卻突然空白的人。從一件不會後悔的小事開始練，鏡框、髮型、晚餐都可以。
variations: 「鏡框跟上次一樣嗎？」「不一樣。」「那要什麼樣的？」——我卡住了。
戴了四年他挑的鏡框，我從來沒問過自己喜歡哪一種。

en.content:
At the optician's, they pulled up my old file. "Same frames as last time?"
I said no.
"Okay — what are you looking for?"
I froze.
He picked these. He said round ones made me look softer.
Four years, and I never once asked myself what I liked.
I walked out with square frames. My mom says they're ugly. I love them.
Seeing clearly is the point.
Whose eyes you see through is up to me.
en.editorNote: For the first time you get to choose something for yourself and your mind goes blank. Start with something low-stakes — frames, a haircut, what's for dinner.
variations: "Same frames as last time?" "No." "What are you looking for?" I froze.
Four years in his frames, and I never asked myself what I liked.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; the three questions everyone asks a year out, answered without flinching

zh-tw.content:
分手滿一年，大家最常問我三個問題。
一、你們還有聯絡嗎？沒有。而且我不是在忍，是真的沒事要說。
二、你會後悔嗎？會。我後悔的是拖太久才走，不是走。
三、你還敢再愛嗎？敢。只是這次我會先確認，對方願不願意一起長大。
這三題我以前一題都答不出來，
現在答得比點餐還快。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合快被親友問到煩的人。把答案先寫好，下次被問就不用在餐桌上臨場崩潰。
variations: 還有聯絡嗎？沒有。後悔嗎？後悔太晚走。還敢愛嗎？敢。
以前一題都答不出來，現在答得比點餐還快。

en.content:
A year out, people ask me the same three questions.
One: do you two still talk? No. And I'm not white-knuckling it — there's genuinely nothing left to say.
Two: do you regret it? Yes. I regret how long I stayed, not that I left.
Three: would you do it again? Yes. I'd just check first whether the other person is willing to grow up alongside me.
A year ago I couldn't answer any of them.
Now I answer faster than I order coffee.
en.editorNote: For when friends and family won't stop asking. Write the answers down once, so the next dinner table doesn't catch you off guard.
variations: Still talk? No. Regret it? Only how long I stayed. Try again? Yes.
A year ago I couldn't answer. Now I answer faster than I order coffee.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; a co-op game save file stuck on a two-player puzzle until a single-player patch shipped

zh-tw.content:
我們一起玩的那款遊戲，存檔卡在第三章那個要兩個人一起拉的機關。
一個人拉不動，我就讓它擺在那，擺了快兩年。
上禮拜開機，跳出更新公告：新增單人模式，系統會派一隻 NPC 幫你。
我笑了很久，然後把那關過了。
NPC 當然沒有他有默契，
但它至少不會玩到一半就登出。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被「這件事沒有他就做不了」卡住的人。過關的方法通常不只一種，只是你還在等原本那個人上線。
variations: 卡了快兩年的雙人關卡，更新後我一個人過了。
NPC 沒有他有默契，但它不會玩到一半登出。

en.content:
That co-op game we played together — my save is stuck on the chapter three puzzle, the one where two people pull at once.
One person can't move it. So I left it sitting there for almost two years.
Last week I booted it up and got a patch note: single-player mode added, an NPC now handles the second lever.
I laughed for a while. Then I cleared it.
The NPC doesn't read me the way he did.
But it never logs off halfway through.
en.editorNote: For anything you've filed under "can't do this without him." There's usually another way through — you're just still waiting for the original player to come online.
variations: Stuck on a two-player puzzle for two years. Patch dropped. Cleared it alone.
The NPC has worse chemistry, but it never logs off halfway through.

items.sourceNote: Original composition; being sick alone reveals how memory over-weights one kind gesture against several absences

zh-tw.content:
上禮拜重感冒，燒到只能躺著。
自己叫車去診所，自己領藥，自己煮了一鍋很難吃的粥。
躺著的時候我一直想到他那次幫我買粥，
想著想著才算清楚——
那是三年裡的一次。
剩下那幾次我發燒，他說他在忙。
記憶很偏心，它只留最好的那一格給你反覆播。
我不是一個人生不了病，
我只是被一碗粥騙了很久。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合還在用「可是他也對我很好過」說服自己的人。把那件好事放回時間軸上數一遍，你會知道那是常態還是例外。
variations: 他幫我買過一次粥，那是三年裡的一次。
記憶很偏心，它只留最好的那一格給你反覆播。

en.content:
Bad flu last week. Fever high enough that I couldn't get off the couch.
Got myself to the clinic, got my own prescription, made myself a genuinely terrible pot of congee.
Lying there, I kept thinking about the time he brought me soup.
And then I actually did the math.
That was once. In three years.
Every other time I got sick, he was busy.
Memory is biased. It saves the best frame and plays it on loop.
It's not that I can't be sick alone.
It's that one bowl of soup fooled me for a very long time.
en.editorNote: For anyone still arguing "but he was good to me sometimes." Put that good moment back on the timeline and count. You'll see whether it was the rule or the exception.
variations: He brought me soup once. Once, in three years.
Memory saves the best frame and plays it on loop.
